Can I have a fulfilled heart if there is a vision, a hope, and or a dream in my life that lies barren and unrealized? Must I go through life carrying a cross of pain and loneliness while God answers the prayers of my friends and gives them the desires of their hearts? Is something wrong with me? Is my faith too weak? Have I not prayed enough, surrendered enough, been obedient enough? What is life all about? Why don’t I have peace and joy? Does God have a plan and a purpose for me?

“Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore” (Psalms 16:11).

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper” (Psalms 1:3).

God has a path provided for each of us that will lead to a fulfilled heart. In God’s presence, there is fullness of joy! God’s desire is that your heart would be like a riverside tree, filled with life, health, strength, and fruit. He desires that you experience grace, joy, and peace, in your everyday life. God wants to fill your heart with his desires and purposes. He longs for you to seek after his will and plan. If you walk on his pathway, you will be filled with blessing and grace. This does not mean that every desire that you may have comes to pass (I don’t think that will ever happen for anyone in this life) but rather that your heart is full of the blessings of God. Your heart does not need to feel like a desert, the Water of Life can fill it.

“But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Where does Fulfillment Begin?

Fulfillment starts in your relationship with God. Does He feel cold and distant to you, or do you find joy and peace in praying and walking with him? Do you know that your sins are forgiven and that you are accepted as His child? Do you obey God with a willing heart or are there areas in your life where you resist his will as revealed in the Bible? Walking in the love and grace of God is the most important thing you can do in life. This is the first step on the pathway to a fulfilled heart.

If you are struggling in your relationship with God and are not sure of his love, forgiveness, and acceptance, here are some directions from the Bible for you.

“But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) 7 Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) 8 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; 9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. 10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10:6-10).

You should never think that Christ is in some unapproachable place, and unavailable to you. Christ is made known to you by the Bible, his Holy Spirit, and by his creation. Unbelief, sin, disobedience, and unforgiveness to others can keep you from experiencing his love and grace. Opening your heart to Him by faith, believing in your heart, and confessing with your mouth the Lord Jesus, will restore your relationship with God. He will wash away your sin and receive you as his child. Christ came to this earth to reconcile us to God. He paid the price of our sin and guilt. We can receive his gift of salvation through faith and repentance. Faith is simply hearing the Word of God and receiving it into our hearts.

As we receive the Word of God into our hearts, it enables us to be obedient to his will. We choose to believe all that God has spoken to us in the Bible. We let go of all our doubts and embrace His Word. Repentance is turning away from our own selfish will and our sinful ways and choosing to obey God and his Word. In 1 John 1:9 God has said that if we confess our sins, He will forgive us. Do you truly believe this? Is it hard for you to accept that he will forgive you? It is impossible for God to lie, therefore his Word and promises can always be trusted.

Practical ways to walk with God

“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit” (Romans 8:1).

There are spiritual prerequisites needed to walk with God. If we don’t have a right heart, these practical things won’t actually help us walk with God. It will only be an empty activity with no real meaning and little benefit.

With our hearts full of faith and love we need to believe everything in the Bible. We need to believe all its history, everything it says about the man, Jesus, all the prophecies, and all the direction God gives us in the Word.

We also need a surrendered heart and choose to follow and obey God in everything. There is no area in which we choose to neglect or disobey. We need to have confessed our sins and be born again by the Spirit of God.

Pray. For yourself, God’s kingdom, your family, the church, neighbors, widows and widowers, orphans, missionaries, governments, and the sick. Pray for people who have lost loved ones, hungry people, people in prison, and people who need salvation. Pray for God to send workers into the vineyard.

Study the Word. Memorize it and read it to others. Discuss it.

Sing praises to God! God has been so merciful to you. Rejoice in your salvation!

“And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people” (Romans 15:9).

Contentment

Another big step in the pathway to a fulfilled heart is contentment. You can never be fulfilled if you aren’t content in knowing that you are in the will of God.

“Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. 6 So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me” (Hebrews 13:5).

What is covetousness? My definition of covetousness is having a strong desire for something that is outside of God’s will for me right now. Normally, covetousness will drive you to violate scripture and God’s will, to try to obtain the thing you have a desire for. For instance, if you are covetous of money, you will tend to do unethical things or neglect to follow the direction in the Bible in your pursuit of money. You may cheat, steal, scam, overcharge, or become a workaholic and neglect God, family, church, or the needy.

God has given us desires, and it is a good thing to pursue them if our heart is surrendered, seeking God’s will and pursuing it according to the direction given in the Bible. Seek to move forward, but never force your own will. Be open to the people that God has put in your life for direction.

You may be at the age when your friends are getting married. You also desire to get married, but all the doors slam shut in your face. It seems like God reveals his will to others but not you. Know that an unanswered prayer is an answer for you right here, right now.

God reveals his will to you day by day and moment by moment. Married people don’t know the long-term will of God for their lives any more than unmarried people. The reality is that my family could be taken away from me in an instant. No one is promised anything earthly for tomorrow. God promises us spiritual blessings but not physical or earthly ones.

Be careful with your expectations. You can create many hardships for yourself if you are very strong in your expectations. As an example, Matthew 20 has the story of the householder who promised his workers a penny for a day’s work. Later in the day, he hired other workers. In the evening, he was paying his workers, starting with the ones hired last, and gave them each a penny. Because of his generosity, the first workers expected more than he had promised them. Since they expected him to give them more than a penny, they murmured against him. Never have strong expectations for things that God hasn’t promised in the Bible, even if you feel like God has revealed it to you by his Spirit. It is far better to have a humble, open heart to God, family, and the brotherhood.

Fellowship

Fellowship with God’s people is another important step in the pathway to fulfillment. Don’t isolate yourself, but rather make yourself a part of God’s people.

“Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. 42 And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers” (Acts 2:41).

It can be easy to fall into the trap of feeling like you are different from everyone else and don’t fit in. Remember that everyone is unique, and together we make up the body of Christ. You are an important member and have gifts and abilities that are needed in your local fellowship. Spend time with people and find ways to be a blessing and help others.

Identity

Embrace your identity. You may wonder, who am I? Where do I fit in? This can be especially difficult if you have a strong desire to be married but are not. You might see others as becoming something that you desire to be but are not.

You might wonder, what is wrong with me that I am not married? This is wrong thinking. The reality is that there are many married people who are in a worse place than you. Be open when those around you have thoughts about changes you can and should make in your life, but don’t condemn yourself as not good enough and that others do not accept you. Ephesians chapter 1 says that you are chosen by God to be washed of your sins through the blood of Jesus and to be adopted as His child. You are accepted by God, and you are to be “to the praise of his glory!”

Purpose

The last step I am writing about is about purpose. What is one thing that you really enjoy doing that is a blessing to the church or Kingdom? God has a purpose for you to fulfill. You are a part of His kingdom that you can put time and energy into. God has called each one of us to be a servant, to follow in the footsteps of our Lord Jesus. It can be as simple as giving a glass of cold water in the name of Jesus. No task is too small or mundane to be a part of His kingdom. Be available. Have the heart of a servant. When you see a need, offer a helping hand or a listening ear.

God het ’n pad voorsien vir elk van ons wat na ’n vervulde hart sal lei. In God se teenwoordigheid is daar volle vreugde! God se begeerte is dat jou hart soos ’n boom langs die rivier sal wees, gevul met lewe, gesondheid, krag en vrug. Hy verlang dat jy genade, vreugde en vrede in jou daaglikse lewe sal ervaar. Dit beteken nie dat elke begeerte wat jy mag hê tot vervulling kom nie (ek dink nie dit sal ooit vir iemand in hierdie lewe gebeur nie), maar eerder dat jou hart vol is van die seëninge van God. “But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Waar begin vervulling?

Vervulling begin in jou verhouding met God. Voel Hy koud en ver van jou af, of vind jy vreugde en vrede in gebed en in die wandel met Hom? Weet jy dat jou sondes vergewe is en dat jy as Sy kind aanvaar word? Gehoorsaam jy God met ’n gewillige hart of is daar areas in jou lewe waar jy sy wil, soos dit in die Bybel geopenbaar word, weerstaan? Wandel in die liefde en genade van God is die belangrikste ding wat jy in die lewe kan doen. Dit is die eerste stap op die pad na ’n vervulde hart.

The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; 9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. 10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10:6-10).

Jy moet nooit dink dat Christus in ’n onbereikbare plek is en vir jou onbeskikbaar is nie. Christus word aan jou bekendgemaak deur die Bybel, Sy Heilige Gees en deur Sy skepping. Ongeloof, sonde, ongehoorsaamheid en onvergewensgesindheid teenoor ander kan jou verhinder om sy liefde en genade te ervaar. Om jou hart vir Hom te open deur geloof, in jou hart te glo en met jou mond die Here Jesus te bely, sal jou verhouding met God herstel. Hy sal jou sonde wegwas en jou as Sy kind ontvang. Christus het na hierdie aarde gekom om ons met God te versoen. Hy het die prys van ons sonde en skuld betaal. Ons kan Sy gawe van redding deur geloof en bekeering ontvang. Geloof is eenvoudig om die Woord van God te hoor en dit in ons harte te ontvang.

Soos ons die Woord van God in ons harte ontvang, stel dit ons in staat om gehoorsaam te wees aan Sy wil. Ons kies om alles te glo wat God in die Bybel aan ons gesproken het. Ons laat al ons twyfel los en omhels Sy Woord. Bekeer is om weg te draai van ons eie selfsugtige wil en ons sondige maniere en te kies om God en Sy Woord te gehoorsaam. In 1 Johannes 1:9 het God gesê dat as ons ons sondes bely, Hy ons sal vergewe. Glo jy dit regtig? Vind jy dit moeilik om te aanvaar dat Hy jou sal vergewe? Dit is onmoontlik vir God om te lieg, dus kan Sy Woord en beloftes altyd vertrou word.

Praktiese maniere om met God te wandel

“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit” (Romans 8:1).

Daar is geestelike vereistes nodig om met God te wandel. As ons nie ’n regte hart het nie, sal hierdie praktiese dinge ons nie werklik help om met God te wandel nie. Dit sal net ’n leë aktiwiteit wees sonder werklike betekenis en min voordeel.

Met ons harte vol geloof en liefde moet ons alles in die Bybel glo. Ons moet al sy geskiedenis glo, alles wat daar oor die Mens, Jesus, staan, al die profesieë en al die leiding wat God vir ons in die Woord gee.

Ons het ook ’n oorgee-hart nodig en moet kies om God in alles te volg en te gehoorsaam. Daar is geen area waarin ons kies om te verwaarloos of ongehoorsaam te wees nie. Ons moet ons sondes bely en wedergebore wees deur die Gees van God.

Bid. Vir jouself, God se koninkryk, jou familie, die kerk, bure, weduwees en weduine, wees, sendingwerkers, regerings en die siekes. Bid vir mense wat geliefdes verloor het, hongerige mense, mense in tronk, en mense wat redding nodig het. Bid dat God werkers in die wingerd sal stuur.

Bestudeer die Woord. Memoriseer dit en lees dit vir ander. Bespreek dit.

Sing lof aan God! God was so barmhartig teenoor jou. Wees bly oor jou redding!

“And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people” (Romans 15:9).

Inhoudsamesheid

’n Ander groot stap op die pad na ’n vervulde hart is innehoudsamesheid. Jy kan nooit vervul wees as jy nie inhoudsam is dat jy in God se wil is nie.

“Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. 6 So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me” (Hebrews 13:5).

Wat is hebsug? My definisie van hebsug is om ’n sterk begeerte te hê vir iets wat buite God se wil vir my op die oomblik is. Gewoonlik sal hebsug jou dryf om die skrif en God se wil te oortrê om te probeer om die ding te verkry waarvoor jy ’n begeerte het. Byvoorbeeld, as jy hebsugtig is oor geld, sal jy geneig wees om onetiese dinge te doen of versuim om die leiding in die Bybel te volg in jou strewe na geld. Jy mag bedrieg, steel, bedrog pleeg, oorlaai, of ’n werkverslaafde word en God, familie, kerk of die behoeftiges verwaarloos.

God het ons begeertes gegee, en dit is ’n goeie ding om hulle na te streef as ons hart oorgegee is, God se wil soek en dit volgens die leiding in die Bybel nastreef. Strewe daarna om vorentoe te beweeg, maar dwing nooit jou eie wil af nie. Wees oop vir die mense wat God in jou lewe geplaas het vir leiding.

Jy mag in ’n ouderdom wees waar jou vriende trou. Jy begeer ook om te trou, maar al die deure slaan in jou gesig toe. Dit lyk asof God sy wil aan ander openbaar, maar nie aan jou nie. Weet dat ’n onbeantwoorde gebed ’n antwoord vir jou reg hier en nou is.

God openbaar sy wil aan jou dag vir dag en oomblik vir oomblik. Getroude mense ken nie die langtermyn- wil van God vir hulle lewens meer as ongetroude mense nie. Die werklikheid is dat my familie in ’n oomblik van my weggeruk kon word. Niemand word iets aardse vir môre belowe nie. God belowe ons geestelike seëninge, maar nie fisiese of aardse nie.

Wees versigtig met jou verwagtinge. Jy kan baie moeilikheid vir jouself skep as jy baie sterk in jou verwagtinge is. As voorbeeld het Matteus 20 die verhaal van die huisheer wat sy arbeiders ’n pennie vir ’n dag se werk belowe het. Later daardie dag het hy ander werkers aangestel. In die aand het hy sy werkers betaal, beginnende met die laaste aangestelden, en het elkeen ’n pennie gegee. Vanweë sy vrygewigheid het die eerste werkers meer verwag as wat hy hulle belowe het. Omdat hulle verwag het dat hy hulle meer as ’n pennie sou gee, het hulle oor hom gemurmureer. Moet nooit sterk verwagtinge hê vir dinge wat God nie in die Bybel belowe het nie, selfs al voel jy asof God dit deur sy Gees aan jou geopenbaar het. Dit is baie beter om ’n nederige, oop hart teenoor God, familie en die broederskap te hê.

Gemeenskap

Gemeenskap met God se mense is nog ’n belangrike stap op die pad na vervulling. Isolateer jouself nie, maar maak jouself deel van God se mense.

“Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. 42 And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers” (Acts 2:41).

Dit kan maklik wees om in die strik te val om te voel dat jy anders is as almal en nie inpas nie. Onthou dat almal uniek is, en saam vorm ons die liggaam van Christus. Jy is ’n belangrike lid en het gawes en vermoëns wat in jou plaaslike gemeenskap nodig is. Spandeer tyd met mense en vind maniere om ’n seën te wees en ander te help.

Identiteit

Omhels jou identiteit. Jy mag wonder: wie is ek? Waar pas ek in? Dit kan veral moeilik wees as jy ’n sterk begeerte het om te trou maar nie is nie. Jy sien dalk ander word wat iets word wat jy begeer om te wees, maar nie is nie.

Jy mag wonder: wat is fout met my dat ek nie getroud is nie? Dit is verkeerde denke. Die werklikheid is dat daar baie getroude mense is wat in ’n slegter plek as jy is. Wees oop wanneer diegene rondom jou gedagtes het oor veranderinge wat jy kan en behoort te maak in jou lewe, maar veroordeel jouself nie as nie goed genoeg en dat ander jou nie aanvaar nie. Efesiërs hoofstuk 1 sê dat jy deur God gekies is om van jou sondes gewas te word deur die bloed van Jesus en om as Sy kind aangeneem te word. Jy word deur God aanvaar, en jy is om “tot die prysing van Sy heerlikheid!”

Doel

Die laaste stap waaroor ek skryf, handel oor doel. Wat is een ding wat jy regtig geniet om te doen wat ’n seën vir die kerk of die Koninkryk is? God het ’n doel vir jou om te vervul. Jy is deel van Sy koninkryk waaraan jy tyd en energie kan gee. God het elk van ons geroep om ’n dienaar te wees, om in die voetspore van ons Here Jesus te volg. Dit kan so eenvoudig wees soos om ’n glas koue water in die naam van Jesus te gee. Geen taak is te klein of alledaags om deel van Sy koninkryk te wees nie. Wees beskikbaar. Het die hart van ’n dienaar. Wanneer jy ’n behoefte sien, bied ’n helpende hand of ’n luisterende oor aan.

Prayer lays hold of God's plan and becomes the link between His will and its accomplishment on earth. Amazing things happen, and we are given the privilege of being the channels of the Holy Spirit's prayer.

—Elisabeth Elliot

In May 2001, God blessed our family with a baby girl. This baby created a lot of excitement as the news flew like wildfire. “Did you hear Ivans have a girl?” Her only sister was 14 years old, and the last five babies had been boys. Such a special baby deserved a special name. We named her Judith Irene after her grandmother and called her Judy for short.

The first 24 hours after birth, Judy grunted and squawked almost continuously. “She is disgruntled about being born,” I joked. After that first day she settled into a normal baby routine with no sign of anything unordinary.

One morning when Judy was about 18 months old, I was in the living room having my personal devotions. She was in the adjoining kitchen when we heard an odd noise—a rhythmical scratch-thunk. I looked quizzically at Ivan. “What is that noise?” With raised eyebrows, he shrugged his shoulders. When the sounds continued, I got curious enough to heft myself out of my rocking chair and trudge toward the source of the sounds. An uneasy suspicion reared its head in the back of my mind and grew with every step I took. When I entered the kitchen, Judy lay on the floor, jerking rhythmically. I had never seen anyone in a seizure before, but somehow, I just knew. She’s having a seizure!

“Shall we call 911?” Ivan headed toward the phone. I debated. Since Ivan was a firefighter, we had an emergency scanner in the house. After hearing countless calls over the years and knowing it could sometimes take the ambulance a while to respond, I wasn't at rest waiting at home while our daughter was seizing.

“Let’s take her in.” I wasn’t willing to sit there and wait until help arrived.

Judy was still jerking. Ivan scooped her off the floor and handed her to me so he could get his keys. Holding Judy close, I headed for the door. “Bring my shoes,” I called over my shoulder as I hurried stocking-footed down the porch steps and toward the pickup truck parked in the lower driveway. Ivan passed me up, opened the door for me, and ran around to the driver’s side. Coming down the short, steep hill, my feet slipped in the morning dew, and I landed halfway under the truck with one leg forward and the other one bent back under me. For an instant, I thought I had broken my leg, but after a stunned second or two, I got to my feet, gathered my precious burden, and struggled into the pickup. Judy was still jerking and, worse yet, was no longer breathing properly. Saliva pooled in the corners of her mouth, turning into foam. Oh my baby! What is wrong with her? Is she going to die?! It’s amazing how many thoughts can run through your mind in a situation like this. Why, oh why doesn’t Ivan drive faster? She’s not breathing! I glanced over at the speedometer. It was pointed hard right. Oh, he was driving fast. With my whole body and mind, I willed us to be at the hospital.

We had a straight drive to the hospital, and Ivan pulled right up to the emergency entrance. I jumped out of the truck with my baby, yelled over my shoulder to bring my shoes along in, and ran for the emergency door. A nurse was just coming around the corner and I all but threw my precious baby into her startled arms. “She’s having a seizure!” I squeaked out. The nurse took one look at Judy, turned, and rushed down the hall with me at her heels. By the time we got into a room, Judy had finally stopped seizing. As she lay on the stretcher, semi-comatose, she went into a second, milder seizure.

Once she came out of the second seizure and things calmed down, the doctor ordered some tests. After reviewing the test results, the doctor decided she had experienced a febrile seizure, one that results from body temperature moving up or down too rapidly. He said they were common in babies and young children and didn’t seem too concerned. My mothering instincts questioned his diagnosis, but I was no doctor so we went with what he said.

This was our introduction to the world of seizures. A few weeks later she had another seizure. And then another. Our parents encouraged us to get a second opinion. This second doctor decided that Judy should have an MRI, even though the first doctor still maintained that she was just having febrile seizures and wasn’t in any hurry to do the MRI. Several weeks passed until they worked her into the schedule. The day after the MRI, we got a call from the doctor’s office. An appointment with a neurosurgeon had been made for two days later. The situation had changed from “no hurry” to “you will be there, no questions asked”. The neurosurgeon said Judy had an AVM and tried to explain what that was, but most of the information soared right over my head. An appointment for an angiogram was scheduled, and explanations of procedures and requirements for us as her parents were added to my spinning brain. As I tried to digest all the information I was receiving in one phone call, I realized they were preparing for the possibility of surgery.

Our prayers were getting more earnest as we progressed through an EEG (brain scan looking for seizure activity) and more doctor visits. We desired healing for our baby so she could live a normal life. Our faith in God came into play as we tried to resign ourselves to His will. Friends, family, and acquaintances all joined us in prayer.

We owned a bulk food store, and many local non-Mennonite folks knew us. We had become good friends with some Christians from a local church. When they heard of the circumstances, they asked if they could have a prayer meeting to lay hands on Judy and pray for her healing. Although the church we attended did not generally do this, we appreciated their sincerity and faith in God, so we agreed to it.

The evening came when we gathered at their church with their pastor and some of the members who knew us. They took turns praying and claimed God’s healing for Judy because they “knew” it was His will to heal her. They specifically asked that the doctors wouldn’t find anything when they did the angiogram. Then they asked us to pray. Although not used to praying out loud, particularly in front of other people, we had confidence that God could heal our baby and wanted to do our part. We prayed for God’s will and voiced our acceptance of whatever He chose.

The next day, we made the hour-and-a-half drive to Madison Children’s Hospital for the angiogram. The purpose for this test was to identify what was causing her seizures and to find its exact location. After the test, we went home to await the results.

I didn’t want my lack of faith to block my daughter’s healing, and I knew God could heal her, but who was I to tell Him what to do? As I struggled through it, we waited for news from the doctor.

Two days later we got a phone call from the doctor’s office. The nurse on the line told us the angiogram hadn’t shown anything! It seemed to puzzle them. It wasn’t at all what they had expected, and they didn’t understand why they couldn’t find the problem. Praise God! We marveled at the miracle He had wrought.

When we took Judy to her next appointment with the neurosurgeon, I asked him what Judy’s problem was since the angiogram found nothing unusual. He said it appeared she had a small amount of bleeding on her brain, but not to worry about it. I thought that was one of the strangest statements I ever heard. I had always been under the impression that bleeding on the brain is very serious and not to be ignored. But I was pretty sure I knew what had happened and told the doctor about the prayers. His response was noncommittal, and I couldn’t tell what he really thought.

They scheduled Judy for a second doctor’s visit and MRI in six months, which I thought was a little strange, considering that they didn’t think there was anything wrong with her. I wasn’t planning to need that MRI or appointment since I believed God had healed her.

That summer, we weaned her off her seizure medications, and she appeared to be healthy. The six months were almost over, and we believed her problems were behind us.

Then, one week before the scheduled MRI, she had a seizure. What a shock! How could this be? Hadn’t God healed her?? What was happening? I felt betrayed. All I could ask was, “Why?” And now what were we going to do?

Such emotional turmoil and soul-searching! I felt let down and shaken in my faith. I had believed in God and that was finally where I ended up every time when I struggled. Solid as a rock under all the turmoil was the truth that God is, and His ways are far above my understanding. I found at the core of my belief in God a safe place where He knows and has my best interest in mind. And that plan might not include the things I want to happen in my limited earth-view.

What if His plan was higher? What if there was someone we would encounter through our medical journey who needed to see Christ in us? Were we willing to be His witness at the expense of our comfort and an easier life?

Our precious little girl ended up having brain surgery at only three and a half years old. Dealing with seizures, surgery, and countless tests over the years caused us no small amount of stress, but God had and still has a plan, and the “whys” we ask might not be revealed until we see Him face to face.

So, does God always answer prayer? I say yes, He does. Sometimes He says, “Yes,” and we get what we want; sometimes, His answer is“No,” and we do not get what we ask for. Sometimes, He whispers, “Wait”, and in His own time and way, He allows us our heart’s desire. Like a child who trusts his parents, I will leave the answers to my prayers in the hands of our almighty God and trust Him to know what is best for my life.

Doa menggenggam rencana Allah dan menjadi penghubung antara kehendak-Nya dan pelaksanaannya di bumi. Hal-hal mengejutkan terjadi, dan kita diberi hak istimewa menjadi saluran doa Roh Kudus.

—Elisabeth Elliot

Pada Mei 2001, Tuhan memberkati keluarga kami dengan seorang bayi perempuan. Bayi ini menimbulkan banyak kegembiraan saat kabar itu menyebar dengan cepat. “Apakah kalian dengar Ivans dapat anak perempuan?” Kakak perempuannya baru berusia 14 tahun, dan lima bayi sebelumnya semuanya laki-laki. Bayi yang istimewa seperti itu pantas mendapat nama istimewa. Kami menamainya Judith Irene menurut nama neneknya dan memanggilnya Judy untuk singkatnya.

24 jam pertama setelah kelahiran, Judy mendengus dan bersuara hampir terus-menerus. “Dia kesal karena dilahirkan,” saya bercanda. Setelah hari pertama itu dia berangsur-angsur masuk ke rutinitas bayi yang normal tanpa tanda-tanda sesuatu yang luar biasa.

Suatu pagi ketika Judy berumur sekitar 18 bulan, saya sedang di ruang tamu melakukan devosi pribadi. Dia berada di dapur yang bersebelahan saat kami mendengar suara aneh—suatu ketukan-garukan ritmis. Saya memandang Ivan dengan heran. “Suara apa itu?” Dengan alis terangkat, dia mengangkat bahu. Ketika suara itu terus terdengar, rasa ingin tahu membuat saya bangkit dari kursi goyang dan berjalan menuju asal suara itu. Kecurigaan yang tidak nyaman muncul di belakang pikiran saya dan tumbuh setiap langkah yang saya ambil. Ketika saya memasuki dapur, Judy terbaring di lantai, bergerak-kejang secara ritmis. Saya belum pernah melihat siapa pun mengalami kejang sebelumnya, tetapi entah bagaimana saya langsung tahu. Dia sedang kejang!

“Haruskah kita panggil 911?” Ivan bergerak menuju telepon. Saya ragu-ragu. Karena Ivan seorang pemadam kebakaran, kami memiliki pemindai keadaan darurat di rumah. Setelah mendengar banyak panggilan selama bertahun-tahun dan mengetahui bahwa kadang-kadang ambulans bisa terlambat, saya tidak tenang menunggu di rumah sementara putri kami sedang kejang.

“Ayo kita bawa dia.” Saya tidak sanggup duduk menunggu sampai bantuan datang.

Judy masih kejang. Ivan mengangkatnya dari lantai dan menyerahkannya kepada saya sehingga dia bisa mengambil kunci. Memeluk Judy erat, saya berjalan menuju pintu. “Bawa sepatuku,” teriak saya sambil tergesa-gesa menuruni anak tangga beranda tanpa memakai sepatu menuju truk pickup yang terparkir di jalan masuk bawah. Ivan mendahului saya, membuka pintu untuk saya, dan berlari mengitari ke sisi pengemudi. Saat turun bukit pendek dan curam, kaki saya tergelincir di embun pagi, dan saya jatuh setengah masuk di bawah truk dengan satu kaki ke depan dan yang lain tertekuk ke belakang di bawah saya. Sesaat saya berpikir saya mungkin patah kaki, tetapi setelah beberapa detik terpana, saya bangkit, mengumpulkan beban berharga saya, dan berjuang masuk ke dalam pickup. Judy masih kejang dan, lebih buruk lagi, tidak bernapas dengan baik. Air liur menggenang di sudut mulutnya, berubah menjadi busa. Ya ampun bayiku! Apa yang terjadi padanya? Apakah dia akan mati?! Luar biasa betapa banyak pikiran yang bisa melintas di benak dalam situasi seperti ini. Mengapa, oh mengapa Ivan tidak mengendarai lebih cepat? Dia tidak bernapas! Saya melirik ke speedometer. Jarumnya menukik ke kanan. Oh, ternyata dia sedang ngebut. Dengan segenap tubuh dan pikiran, saya memaksa agar kami segera sampai di rumah sakit.

Kami memiliki jalan langsung ke rumah sakit, dan Ivan berhenti tepat di depan pintu darurat. Saya meloncat keluar dari truk membawa bayi saya, berteriak agar dia membawa sepatuku masuk, dan berlari menuju pintu darurat. Seorang perawat baru saja membelok di sudut dan saya nyaris melemparkan bayi berharga saya ke pelukannya yang terkejut. “Dia sedang kejang!” saya terbatuk. Perawat itu menatap Judy sekali, lalu berbalik dan bergegas menyusuri lorong dengan saya mengikuti di belakang. Saat kami sampai di sebuah ruang, Judy akhirnya berhenti kejang. Saat dia terbaring di tandu, setengah koma, dia mengalami kejang kedua yang lebih ringan.

Setelah dia keluar dari kejang kedua dan keadaan tenang, dokter memerintahkan beberapa tes. Setelah meninjau hasil tes, dokter memutuskan bahwa dia mengalami kejang demam, yaitu yang disebabkan oleh suhu tubuh yang naik atau turun terlalu cepat. Dia mengatakan kejang semacam itu umum pada bayi dan anak kecil dan tampak tidak terlalu khawatir. Naluri keibuan saya mempertanyakan diagnosisnya, tetapi saya bukan seorang dokter sehingga kami menerima apa yang dia katakan.

Inilah pengenalan kami ke dunia kejang. Beberapa minggu kemudian dia mengalami kejang lagi. Lalu kejang lagi. Orang tua kami mendorong kami untuk mencari pendapat kedua. Dokter kedua ini memutuskan bahwa Judy harus menjalani MRI, meskipun dokter pertama tetap berpendapat bahwa itu hanya kejang demam dan tidak bergegas melakukan MRI. Beberapa minggu berlalu sampai mereka memasukkannya ke dalam jadwal. Sehari setelah MRI, kami mendapat telepon dari kantor dokter. Janji dengan seorang ahli bedah saraf dibuat dua hari kemudian. Situasinya berubah dari “tidak mendesak” menjadi “anda harus datang, tanpa pertanyaan”. Sang ahli bedah saraf mengatakan Judy memiliki AVM dan mencoba menjelaskan apa itu, tetapi sebagian besar informasi itu melayang di atas kepala saya. Janji untuk angiogram dijadwalkan, dan penjelasan mengenai prosedur dan persyaratan bagi kami sebagai orang tua ditambahkan ke otak saya yang berputar-putar. Saat saya mencoba mencerna semua informasi yang saya terima dalam satu panggilan telepon, saya menyadari mereka sedang bersiap untuk kemungkinan pembedahan.

Doa kami menjadi semakin sungguh-sungguh saat kami menjalani EEG (pemeriksaan otak untuk mencari aktivitas kejang) dan kunjungan dokter yang lebih banyak. Kami mendambakan penyembuhan bagi bayi kami sehingga dia bisa hidup normal. Iman kami kepada Allah berperan saat kami mencoba menyerahkan diri pada kehendak-Nya. Teman, keluarga, dan kenalan semuanya bergabung mendoakan kami.

Kami memiliki sebuah toko bahan makanan grosir, dan banyak orang non-Mennonit setempat mengenal kami. Kami menjadi teman baik dengan beberapa orang Kristen dari sebuah gereja lokal. Ketika mereka mendengar keadaan kami, mereka menanyakan apakah mereka bisa mengadakan pertemuan doa untuk meletakkan tangan atas Judy dan mendoakan penyembuhan baginya. Meskipun gereja yang kami hadiri umumnya tidak melakukan hal semacam ini, kami menghargai ketulusan dan iman mereka kepada Allah, jadi kami setuju.

Malam itu kami berkumpul di gereja mereka bersama gembala dan beberapa anggota yang mengenal kami. Mereka bergiliran berdoa dan menyatakan penyembuhan Tuhan bagi Judy karena mereka “tahu” itu kehendak-Nya untuk menyembuhkannya. Mereka secara khusus memohon agar para dokter tidak menemukan apa-apa saat melakukan angiogram. Lalu mereka meminta kami untuk berdoa. Meskipun tidak terbiasa berdoa dengan keras, terutama di hadapan orang lain, kami percaya bahwa Allah sanggup menyembuhkan bayi kami dan ingin melakukan bagian kami. Kami berdoa untuk kehendak Allah dan menyatakan penerimaan kami terhadap apa pun yang Dia pilih.

Keesokan harinya, kami melakukan perjalanan satu setengah jam ke Madison Children’s Hospital untuk angiogram. Tujuan tes ini adalah untuk mengidentifikasi apa yang menyebabkan kejangnya dan menemukan lokasi pastinya. Setelah tes, kami pulang untuk menunggu hasil.

Saya tidak ingin kurangnya iman saya menghalangi penyembuhan putri saya, dan saya tahu Allah bisa menyembuhkannya, tetapi siapa saya untuk memberitahu Dia apa yang harus dilakukan? Saat saya bergulat dengan itu, kami menunggu kabar dari dokter.

Dua hari kemudian kami menerima telepon dari kantor dokter. Perawat di garis telepon mengatakan angiogram tidak menunjukkan apa pun! Itu tampak membingungkan bagi mereka. Itu sama sekali bukan apa yang mereka harapkan, dan mereka tidak mengerti mengapa mereka tidak bisa menemukan masalahnya. Puji Tuhan! Kami takjub atas mujizat yang telah Dia lakukan.

Ketika kami membawa Judy ke janji berikutnya dengan ahli bedah saraf, saya bertanya apa masalah Judy karena angiogram tidak menemukan apa-apa yang tidak biasa. Dia berkata tampaknya ada sejumlah kecil perdarahan di otaknya, tetapi tidak perlu dikhawatirkan. Saya pikir itu salah satu pernyataan paling aneh yang pernah saya dengar. Saya selalu beranggapan bahwa perdarahan di otak sangat serius dan tidak boleh diabaikan. Tetapi saya cukup yakin saya tahu apa yang telah terjadi dan menceritakan tentang doa-doa itu kepada dokter. Responsnya tidak menentu, dan saya tidak bisa memastikan apa yang sebenarnya dia pikirkan.

Mereka menjadwalkan kunjungan dokter dan MRI kedua dalam enam bulan, yang saya rasa agak aneh, mengingat mereka tidak berpikir ada yang salah dengan dia. Saya tidak berencana membutuhkan MRI atau janji itu karena saya percaya Allah telah menyembuhkannya.

Pada musim panas itu, kami menghentikan obat kejangnya, dan dia tampak sehat. Enam bulan hampir berakhir, dan kami percaya masalahnya sudah berlalu.

Lalu, satu minggu sebelum MRI yang dijadwalkan, dia mengalami kejang. Betapa terkejutnya kami! Bagaimana bisa ini terjadi? Bukankah Allah telah menyembuhkannya?? Apa yang sedang terjadi? Saya merasa dikhianati. Yang bisa saya tanyakan hanyalah, “Mengapa?” Dan sekarang apa yang akan kami lakukan?

Begitu banyak pergolakan emosi dan pencarian jiwa! Saya merasa kecewa dan terguncang dalam iman saya. Saya telah percaya kepada Allah dan itu selalu menjadi tempat akhir saya setiap kali saya bergumul. Kokoh bak batu di tengah semua kegelisahan itu adalah kebenaran bahwa Allah ada, dan jalan-Nya jauh melampaui pengertian saya. Saya menemukan di inti kepercayaan saya pada Allah suatu tempat yang aman di mana Dia mengetahui dan menginginkan yang terbaik bagi saya. Dan rancangan itu mungkin tidak termasuk hal-hal yang saya inginkan terjadi dalam pandangan duniawi saya yang terbatas.

Bagaimana jika rencana-Nya lebih tinggi? Bagaimana jika ada seseorang yang akan kami temui melalui perjalanan medis kami yang perlu melihat Kristus dalam diri kami? Apakah kami bersedia menjadi saksi-Nya dengan mengorbankan kenyamanan dan kehidupan yang lebih mudah?

Putri kecil kami yang berharga akhirnya menjalani operasi otak pada usia tiga setengah tahun. Menghadapi kejang, operasi, dan tak terhitung tes selama bertahun-tahun menyebabkan kami tidak sedikit stres, tetapi Allah mempunyai dan masih mempunyai rencana, dan “mengapa” yang kami tanyakan mungkin tidak akan diungkapkan sampai kami melihat Dia muka dengan muka.

Jadi, apakah Allah selalu menjawab doa? Saya katakan ya, Dia memang menjawab. Kadang-kadang Dia berkata, “Ya,” dan kita mendapat apa yang kita inginkan; kadang-kadang jawaban-Nya adalah “Tidak,” dan kita tidak mendapat apa yang kita minta. Kadang-kadang Dia berbisik, “Tunggu”, dan pada waktu serta cara-Nya sendiri, Dia mengizinkan kita menerima keinginan hati kita. Seperti seorang anak yang percaya kepada orang tuanya, saya akan menyerahkan jawaban atas doa-doa saya ke tangan Allah yang mahakuasa dan mempercayai-Nya untuk mengetahui apa yang terbaik bagi hidup saya.

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

Saat saya bertobat, saya belum pernah mendengar istilah Anabaptis. Saya juga jarang mendengar tentang memberi kesaksian kepada orang lain. Saya ingat memikirkan semua teman saya yang tidak tahu apa-apa tentang apa yang baru saja terjadi pada saya. Pacar saya selama tujuh tahun tidak mengerti. Satu hal terus terlintas di benak saya: “Saya perlu memberitahu mereka!” Sesuatu yang baik telah terjadi pada saya, dan semua orang perlu tahu bahwa hal yang sama bisa terjadi pada mereka! Saya ingat suatu ketika saudara saya dan saya memikirkan tempat di mana kami bisa memberitahukan banyak orang tentang Yesus. Kami memutuskan pergi ke pertandingan bisbol liga utama. Saya gugup, saya takut, dan saya tidak akan pernah lupa apa yang terjadi. Saya belum pernah berbicara di depan kerumunan besar sebelumnya, tetapi ketika saya membuka mulut, Tuhan mengisinya.

Saya tidak hanya pergi dan berbicara kepada orang yang tidak saya kenal. Ketika saya bertemu teman lama, saya akan menceritakan apa yang terjadi pada saya. Mereka biasanya mengatakan bahwa mereka sudah pernah mendengarnya dan mencoba meyakinkan saya untuk tenang dan santai. Saya akan menjadi yang pertama mengakui bahwa saya membuat beberapa kesalahan di tahun-tahun pertama itu. Saya tercengang menyadari bahwa sementara banyak orang tidak menyukai saya, justru orang-orang yang mengatakan bahwa mereka orang Kristen tampak paling tidak menyukai saya. Suatu hari saya sedang berbincang dengan seorang pria tua yang mengatakan bahwa dia telah menjadi Kristen sepanjang hidupnya. Dalam pembicaraan itu, dia menunjuk ke sebuah bohlam lampu dan berkata, "Lihat bohlam itu? Ia tidak berbicara." Saya terkejut. Dia memberi tahu saya bahwa, ya, meskipun Yesus mengatakan kita adalah terang dunia, lampu seharusnya bersinar dengan tenang. Mereka tidak berbicara.

Saya tercengang. Apakah ini benar? Saya pulang untuk melakukan studi Alkitab. Tak lama kemudian saya menemukan ayat-ayat seperti Matius 4:23, "Dan Yesus berkeliling ke seluruh Galilea, mengajar dalam rumah-rumah ibadat mereka, dan memberitakan Injil tentang Kerajaan itu, serta menyembuhkan segala penyakit dan kelemahan di antara rakyat." Lalu di Matius 9, ketika Yesus "melihat orang banyak itu, tergeraklah hati-Nya oleh belas kasihan kepada mereka, karena mereka lelah dan tertinggal seperti domba-domba yang tidak bergembala. Lalu Ia berkata kepada murid-murid-Nya: Sangat banyak tuaiannya, tetapi sedikitkan pekerja; berdoalah karena itu kepada Tuhan yang empunya tuaian, supaya Ia mengutus pekerja-pekerja tuaian itu" (Matius 9:36-38).

Sepertinya ke mana pun Yesus pergi, Dia berbicara kepada orang-orang tentang kerajaan itu. Saya telah melihat orang-orang bersaksi tentang Allah, tetapi terkadang dengan cara yang menyinggung. Namun apakah itu berarti kita tidak boleh memberi kesaksian? Jika Anda membaca kitab Kisah Para Rasul, hampir semua yang Anda lihat adalah—Injil yang keluar! Dalam satu peristiwa, para otoritas menangkap murid-murid dan berkata mereka boleh bebas jika mereka hanya mau diam. Namun, murid-murid berkata mereka tidak bisa. "Sebab tidak mungkin kami tidak berbicara tentang apa yang telah kami lihat dan dengar" (Kisah Para Rasul 4:20). Kelak mereka dibungkam—oleh kematian.

Beberapa waktu kemudian saya mendengar tentang orang-orang yang disebut Anabaptis ini. Saat saya mempelajari mereka, saya mulai melihat bagaimana mereka juga tidak mau diam. Saya memesan sebuah salinan The Martyr’s Mirror dan tercengang ketika membaca tentang orang-orang ini yang hidup seperti para murid. Mereka memenuhi apa yang dikatakan Yesus, "Dan kamu akan dibenci oleh semua orang karena nama-Ku: tetapi siapa yang bertahan sampai pada akhirnya, ia akan diselamatkan" (Mat. 10:22). Dan dalam Roma 8:36, "Seperti ada tertulis: Untuk Engkau kami dibunuh setiap hari; kami dianggap seperti domba yang disembelih."

Saudara-saudari terkasih, saya percaya apinya mulai padam. Saya mendengar banyak dari kaum Anabaptis kita berbicara tentang hidup tenang dan damai. Yesus memberitahu kita dalam perumpamaan penabur, "Adapun yang menerima benih itu di antara duri-duri ialah orang yang mendengar firman itu; tetapi kekawatiran dunia ini dan tipu daya kekayaan mencekik firman itu, sehingga ia tidak berbuah" (Mat. 13:22). Mungkinkah itu tempat banyak dari kita berada? Kita hidup di tanah merdeka Amerika di mana uang tampaknya mudah diperoleh. Adakah kemungkinan kita telah ditipu oleh kekayaan kita sendiri dan kepedulian dunia ini? Apakah kita menjadi seperti dunia untuk menghindari dianiaya olehnya?

Bertahun-tahun yang lalu, sekelompok Anabaptis melarikan diri dari penganiayaan dan pindah ke negara di mana ada lebih sedikit penindasan. Mereka membuka toko furnitur untuk menopang diri, tetapi mereka tidak bisa menjual furnitur karena mereka adalah Anabaptis yang ditakuti. Segera, situasi menjadi putus asa karena mereka tidak memiliki uang untuk membeli makanan. Suatu hari seorang lelaki kaya masuk ke toko. Semua pekerja menghentikan apa yang mereka lakukan. Mereka berpikir, "Barangkali orang ini akan membeli sesuatu, dan kita bisa makan!" Seorang saudara tua mendekati calon pembeli itu dan bertanya apakah ia mengenal Yesus. Setelah obrolan singkat, pria itu keluar dari toko dalam amarah. Para pekerja yang kelaparan bertanya mengapa sang tua menakut-nakuti satu-satunya kesempatan mereka untuk mendapatkan penjualan. Ia menjelaskan bahwa bagi pria itu mengenal Yesus jauh lebih penting daripada bagi mereka untuk memperoleh sedikit uang.

Dalam pola pikir Anabaptis awal, Injil Yesus adalah nomor satu. Seperti dalam Kisah Para Rasul, mereka tidak bisa tidak berbicara tentang hal-hal yang telah mereka lihat dan dengar. Dan mereka pun, juga, "dibunuh setiap hari."

Jadi, apa yang kita lakukan dengan ayat tentang hidup tenang dan damai? Ayat itu terdapat dalam 1 Timotius 2:1-2: "Segala permohonan, doa, permintaan, dan syukur haruslah dilakukan untuk semua orang—untuk raja-raja dan semua orang yang memegang otoritas—supaya kita dapat hidup tenang dan damai dalam segala kesalehan dan kehormatan." Apa yang dimaksud rasul Paulus ketika menulis itu? Apakah ia bermaksud bahwa kita harus diam tentang Injil dan tidak pernah menantang orang berdosa? Sulit untuk percaya bahwa Paulus menyuruh kita melakukan sesuatu yang tidak pernah dilakukannya, sesuatu yang Kristus sendiri tidak pernah lakukan. Faktanya, tidak seorang pun dalam tulisan suci yang mengikuti Allah yang diam mengenai iman mereka. Dalam banyak catatan tentang orang-orang Kristen awal yang ditangkap karena iman mereka, para otoritas akan memohon kepada mereka untuk berdiam saja! Tetapi mereka menolak, sama seperti para murid. Mereka juga memilih mati, daripada hidup tenang dan damai.

Seorang Anabaptis muda yang ditangkap meninggalkan istri tercintanya yang sedang menantikan anak pertama mereka. Para otoritas menunggu sampai anak itu lahir lalu membawa bayi itu kepada ayah baru itu di penjara. Mereka memberitahunya bahwa dia sekarang menjadi ayah dan bisa pulang untuk bersama istri dan anak laki-lakinya. Dia bahkan bisa terus percaya dengan cara yang sama, tetapi dia harus diam dan tidak bersuara menentang dosa di gereja negara. Sang ayah muda menolak. Bagi dia, diam bukanlah pilihan. Mereka membakar dia di tiang pancang.

Jadi, apa arti 1 Timotius 2:1-2? Tampaknya orang-orang Kristen dalam Alkitab dan gereja awal semuanya berpusat pada menyebarkan Injil, semua tentang gereja Kristus. Mereka berkeliling memberitakan Injil, mengadakan pertemuan di bukit-bukit, hutan, atau di mana pun orang mau datang. Itulah hidup mereka. Dalam ayat di 1 Timotius 2, Paulus mengatakan kita harus berdoa agar para penguasa membiarkan kita hidup dalam damai sehingga kita dapat memberitakan Injil. Orang Kristen seharusnya keluar menyebarkan firman dan menekan masuk ke dalam kerajaan. Doa kita ialah agar para penguasa membiarkan kita hidup dalam damai, sementara kita melayani Pangeran damai sejahtera.

Hari ini mudah menjadi orang Kristen ketika Anda menetap dan menjalani hidup tenang dan damai, tanpa pernah menantang orang berdosa atau menegur seorang saudara. Tapi siapa yang bilang itu akan mudah?

Ketika kami tinggal di Haiti, kami mengajar jemaat kami tentang biaya mengikuti Yesus. Luar biasa mendengar kesaksian orang-orang Haiti tentang menerapkan ajaran Yesus dalam hidup mereka. Suatu kali, dua anggota memberitahu kami bahwa mereka hampir kehilangan pekerjaan karena mengikuti Injil. Mendengar mereka berdiri untuk mengikuti kebenaran membuat saya senang. Seorang saudari lain di gereja memberitahu saya bahwa sekolah tempat anak-anaknya bersekolah memakai seragam dan para gadis diwajibkan memakai celana. Ketika ia mengirim putrinya ke sekolah dengan memakai gaun yang sopan, putrinya pulang membawa catatan dari kepala sekolah yang mengatakan dia tidak boleh kembali ke sekolah dengan mengenakan benda itu.

1 Petrus 4:14 mengatakan, "Jika kamu dicela karena nama Kristus, maka kamu berbahagia, karena roh kemuliaan dan roh Allah ada pada kamu. Bagi mereka ia dicela, tetapi bagi kamu ia dimuliakan."

Kegembiraan sejati datang dari penderitaan. Penderitaan datang dari menaati Yesus. Apakah kita terlalu sibuk dengan hal-hal remeh sementara dunia menuju neraka? Mari kita mengikuti Yesus seperti orang-orang Kristen awal, di mana orang tidak dapat menyangkal bahwa kuasa Allah bekerja dalam diri mereka. Kita memiliki sesuatu yang dibutuhkan semua orang. Apa yang kita tunggu? Mari bersatu kembali, berkumpul kembali, menyangkal diri, memikul salib, dan mengikuti Dia!

It was one of those Sunday afternoons in late spring when the sun was finally shining warmly. It was the time of year when little boys seem to have plenty of extra energy. Little Davy was sitting on the road bank with some neighborhood boys who had stopped by. He felt like jumping up and down in anticipation of the upcoming race.

Two older boys, Big David and Paul, showed up with brand-new bicycles. These were not the ordinary bicycles the other boys had. They were beautiful Vista bicycles with gleaming new paint, shiny chrome fenders, and three speeds. These bicycles glided smoothly on the chip-and seal road without a rattle. With new ball bearings, they whizzed along with hardly any effort being applied to the pedals. Even though there did not seem to be much difference between the bicycles, Big David’s was a gleaming chestnut brown, and Paul’s a sparkling metal flake blue.

“Well,” Big David began to brag, “With my longer legs, and freshly sprayed WD40, my bike is sure to be the fastest.”

“No,” challenged Paul, “my shorter legs can pump faster, and Schwinn’s high-test bicycle oil by far outperforms WD40, which really is only for squeaks.”

“A race! A race!” the other boys said, “Why not settle it with a race?”

“Okay,” Big David said, “We’ll have a race and see whose bike is really the fastest.”

“You bet!” Paul agreed. “We’ll start at the top of Billy’s hill and race all the way down to the bottom,” he said, pointing to the road bank where the other boys were sitting.

One, two, three, GO and they were off! Down the hill they came, pedaling for all they were worth.

“Go Paul!” and “Go Big David!” shouted the boys at the bottom of the hill. All the commotion woke up Little Davy’s rat terrier dog, Nellie. Yapping loudly, Nellie zoomed around the silo as fast as her four little legs could carry her. She headed straight for Big David’s bicycle in the front, barking loudly to try to make it stop. Poor Nellie did not realize another bicycle was trying to pass up the first one.

Thump, the passing bicycle hit the dog! Crash, bang, the two bicycles ran into each other!

“Hey – aye!” Oooff! Two boys flew over the handlebars and landed hard on the road. Those shining bicycles were no longer gleaming. They were lying on a heap, scratched and streaked with tar. Nellie limped back beside the silo and stayed lying there for several hours.

The other boys stood on the bank with their mouths open. Quickly, they ran to the two big boys lying by their new bicycles. “Are you okay?” they asked.

“I’ll be okay,” Paul said slowly, “but no more races. Who even cares whose bike is the fastest.”

Even though Little Davy is now a grandpa, he has not forgotten the bicycle race on that long ago Sunday afternoon, when Big David and Paul learned that bragging and showing off usually comes to a crashing end.

Det var en av de där söndagseftermiddagarna i sen vår när solen äntligen sken varmt. Det var den årstiden då små pojkar tycks ha massor av extra energi. Lilla Davy satt på vägkanten med några grannpojkar som hade svängt förbi. Han kände hur han ville hoppa upp och ner i väntan på det kommande loppet.

Två äldre pojkar, Stora David och Paul, dök upp med sprillans nya cyklar. Det var inte de vanliga cyklarna som de andra pojkarna hade. Det var vackra Vista-cyklar med glänsande ny lack, skinande kromskärmar och tre växlar. Dessa cyklar gled lätt på den grus- och förseglade vägen utan ett skallrande ljud. Med nya kullager susade de fram med knappt något tryck på pedalerna. Fastän det inte verkade vara så stor skillnad mellan cyklarna, var Stora Davids skinande kastanjebruna och Pauls en gnistrande metallflingeblå.

”Tja,” började Stora David och skryta, ”med mina längre ben och nysprayad WD40 kommer min cykel garanterat vara snabbast.”

”Nej,” invände Paul, ”mina kortare ben kan trampa snabbare, och Schwinns högpresterande cykelolja överträffar WD40 med råge, det är ju egentligen bara för gnissel.”

”Ett lopp! Ett lopp!” sa de andra pojkarna, ”Varför avgör vi det inte med ett lopp?”

”Okej,” sa Stora David, ”Vi kör ett lopp och ser vems cykel som verkligen är snabbast.”

”Självklart!” höll Paul med. ”Vi startar uppe vid Billys backe och tävlar hela vägen ner till botten,” sa han och pekade mot vägkanten där de andra pojkarna satt.

En, två, tre, START och iväg bar det! Ner för backen kom de, trampande så gott de kunde.

”Heja Paul!” och ”Heja Stora David!” ropade pojkarna vid backens fot. All uppståndelse väckte Lilla Davys råttterrier Nellie. Skällande högt svirade Nellie runt silon så snabbt hennes fyra små ben kunde bära henne. Hon styrde rakt mot Stora Davids cykel längst fram och skällde högljutt för att försöka få den att stanna. Stackars Nellie insåg inte att en annan cykel försökte köra om den första.

Thump, den omkörande cykeln träffade hunden! Krasch, pang, de två cyklarna krockade med varandra!

”Hej – aj!” Oooff! Två pojkar flög över styrena och landade hårt på vägen. De blänkande cyklarna var inte längre skinande. De låg i en hög, repiga och strimmiga av tjära. Nellie haltade tillbaka bredvid silon och låg där i flera timmar.

De andra pojkarna stod på banken med gapande munnar. Snabbt sprang de fram till de två stora pojkarna som låg vid sina nya cyklar. ”Är ni okej?” frågade de.

”Jag klarar mig,” sade Paul långsamt, ”men inga fler lopp. Vem bryr sig ens om vems cykel är snabbast.”

Fastän Lilla Davy nu är morfar, har han inte glömt cykelloppet den där för länge sedan söndagseftermiddagen, när Stora David och Paul lärde sig att skryt och visa upp-sig vanligtvis slutar i en krasch.

Greetings in the worthy name of the Lord Jesus Christ. As I gaze out across the barren January landscape, I can’t help but wonder what this new year will bring. Undoubtedly, it will bring a mixture of joy and sorrow, excitement and drear, laughter and tears, and everything else in between, which only an Almighty Creator God can arrange in such a way that will magnify His worthy power and excellence. Yet our finite, negative minds tend to anticipate all the bad things that could happen. Will inflation drive food prices even higher? Will widespread fighting erupt across the Middle East? What will happen in the elections? Will the losing party resort to protests and rioting?

I suppose, since the fall of man, these fear-driven thoughts have roamed through the minds of humanity at the beginning of each year. Yet, as it is so aptly pointed out by the writer of the article, “God’s Faithfulness Manifest Even in the Curse”, God has kindly provided for humanity since the beginning of time. Looking back at God’s faithfulness to man over the centuries, we have no reason to doubt God will do the same for us in 2024.

Despite God’s faithfulness to us, the effects of the fall of man are still evident. Family members get sick, church and relationship struggles rob us of sleep, the checkbook runs dry, the children squabble and cry, and the demands of our schedules have us hopping from one event to the next. And sometimes, it seems that all these calamities hit us at the same time. Our bodies and minds are not created to handle this. We become weary. Bone tired. Exhausted to the point when even thinking hurts. We face burnout. In this issue, “A Word From the Doctor” guides us as we face the maze of life, giving us practical and Biblical solutions to avoid or recover from burnout. He writes, “Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.”

Perhaps one good remedy to reduce the stress of life would be to go for a bike ride. But we need to be careful and avoid getting into a bike race like the two lads did in this issue’s children’s story. We may end up with more stress than we bargained for.

Despite our best efforts to live stress-free lives, we still meet with the unexpected. Last week I was cleaning out our broiler houses in preparation for a new flock. I leaned across the tractor fender to push a partly opened door out of the way. As I stood up, my foot accidentally hit the hydrostatic pedal, lurching the tractor forward and throwing me off-balance. My foot somehow got caught under the pedal, and for a split second, I feared I would fall right in front of the rear wheel. In a last-ditch effort, I threw myself away from the tractor. My foot slipped out of my shoe, and I landed unharmed on the ground. The tractor slowly headed off with my shoe still wedged under the pedal. All ended well, and a few lessons were learned. It was nothing other than the providence of God that prevented a freak incident from becoming a bad accident. Truly I agree with Solomon, “For the LORD shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken” (Proverbs 3:26).

As we navigate through this year, let’s join the hymnwriter in worship, where he writes:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view, I’m lost
In wonder, love and praise.

It is only by the mercies of an all-loving God that we have life and breath. May we give our all to Him and to the work of His kingdom in heartfelt thanksgiving for His unspeakable gift.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Salam dalam nama yang layak, Tuhan Yesus Kristus. Saat aku menatap lanskap Januari yang tandus, aku tak bisa menahan diri untuk bertanya-tanya apa yang akan dibawa tahun baru ini. Tidak diragukan lagi, ia akan membawa campuran sukacita dan dukacita, kegembiraan dan kelesuan, tawa dan air mata, serta segala sesuatu di antaranya, yang hanya dapat diatur sedemikian rupa oleh Allah Pencipta yang Mahakuasa sehingga memuliakan kekuatan dan keagungan-Nya yang layak. Namun pikiran kita yang fana dan cenderung negatif seringkali mengantisipasi semua hal buruk yang mungkin terjadi. Akankah inflasi mendorong harga makanan semakin tinggi? Akankah terjadi pertempuran meluas di Timur Tengah? Apa yang akan terjadi dalam pemilihan? Akankah pihak yang kalah mengambil jalan protes dan kerusuhan?

Kurasa, sejak kejatuhan manusia, pikiran-pikiran yang didorong ketakutan ini telah berkeliaran dalam benak umat manusia pada awal setiap tahun. Namun, seperti yang begitu tepat ditunjukkan oleh penulis artikel, “Kesetiaan Allah Terlihat Bahkan dalam Kutukan”, Allah telah baik hati menyediakan bagi umat manusia sejak awal waktu. Melihat kembali kesetiaan Allah kepada manusia selama berabad-abad, kita tidak punya alasan meragukan bahwa Allah akan melakukan hal yang sama bagi kita pada 2024.

Meski Allah setia kepada kita, akibat kejatuhan manusia masih nyata. Anggota keluarga sakit, pergumulan dalam jemaat dan hubungan merampas tidur kita, rekening menjadi kosong, anak-anak bertengkar dan menangis, dan tuntutan jadwal membuat kita melompat dari satu acara ke acara berikutnya. Dan kadang-kadang, tampaknya semua bencana ini menimpa kita pada waktu yang sama. Tubuh dan pikiran kita tidak diciptakan untuk menghadapi ini. Kita menjadi lelah. Lemas sampai ke tulang. Lelah sampai berpikir pun terasa menyakitkan. Kita menghadapi kelelahan total. Dalam edisi ini, “Sepatah Kata dari Dokter” membimbing kita saat menghadapi labirin kehidupan, memberi solusi praktis dan Alkitabiah untuk menghindari atau pulih dari kelelahan total. Ia menulis, “Yesus mengetahui keterbatasan kita. Ia menghendaki kita memiliki keseimbangan, hidup sedemikian rupa sehingga kita tidak hanya memiliki kekuatan untuk hari ini tetapi juga untuk besok, minggu depan, dan tahun depan – sampai Ia datang kembali.”

Mungkin salah satu obat yang baik untuk mengurangi stres hidup adalah pergi bersepeda. Tetapi kita perlu berhati-hati dan menghindari masuk ke dalam perlombaan sepeda seperti yang dilakukan dua pemuda dalam cerita anak-anak edisi ini. Kita mungkin berakhir dengan lebih banyak stres daripada yang kita perkirakan.

Meski kita berupaya hidup tanpa stres, kita tetap bertemu dengan hal-hal tak terduga. Minggu lalu aku sedang membersihkan kandang pemanas ayam sebagai persiapan untuk kawanan baru. Aku membungkuk melewati fender traktor untuk mendorong pintu yang sebagian terbuka agar tidak menghalangi. Saat aku berdiri, kakiku secara tidak sengaja mengenai pedal hidrostatik, membuat traktor maju mendadak dan melemparkanku kehilangan keseimbangan. Entah bagaimana kakiku tersangkut di bawah pedal, dan sekejap aku takut akan jatuh tepat di depan roda belakang. Dalam usaha terakhir, aku melemparkan tubuh menjauh dari traktor. Kakiku terlepas dari sepatuku, dan aku mendarat tanpa cedera di tanah. Traktor perlahan melaju pergi dengan sepatuku masih terselip di bawah pedal. Semua berakhir baik, dan beberapa pelajaran dipetik. Tidak ada yang lain selain pemeliharaan Allah yang mencegah insiden aneh itu menjadi kecelakaan buruk. Sungguh aku setuju dengan Salomo, “Sebab TUHAN akan menjadi pengharapanmu, dan Ia akan menjaga kakimu supaya jangan tertangkap” (Amsal 3:26).

Saat kita menavigasi tahun ini, marilah kita bergabung dengan penulis himne dalam ibadah, yang menulis:

Bilamana segala rahmat-Mu, ya Allahku,
Jiwaku yang bangkit memandang,
Terpana oleh pemandangan, aku hilang
Dalam kekaguman, kasih dan pujian.

Hanya oleh rahmat Allah yang penuh kasih kita diberi hidup dan nafas. Kiranya kita menyerahkan segala-galanya kepada-Nya dan kepada pekerjaan kerajaan-Nya dalam ucapan syukur yang tulus untuk karunia-Nya yang tak terkatakan.

Berkat bagi semua,

Edward Martin
