الصلاة تمسك بخطة الله وتصبح الحلقة الواصلة بين إرادته وتحقيقها على الأرض. تحدث أمور مدهشة، ويُمنح لنا امتياز أن نكون قنوات صلاة الروح القدس.

—إليزابيث إليوت

في مايو 2001، بارك الله عائلتنا بفتاة صغيرة. أثارت ولادتها حماسة كبيرة وانتشر الخبر كالنار في الهشيم. "هل سمعتوا أن عائلة إيفانز أنجبت فتاة؟" كانت أختها الوحيدة بعمر 14 عامًا، وكانت آخر خمس مواليد صبية. كانت هذه الطفلة الخاصة تستحق اسمًا خاصًا. سمّيناها جوديث إيرين على اسم جدتها ودعوناها جودي اختصارًا.

في الأربع والعشرين ساعة الأولى بعد الولادة، كانت جودي تتأوه وتصرخ تقريبًا بلا انقطاع. "إنها مستاءة من ولادتها" مازحتُ. بعد ذلك اليوم الأول استقرت ضمن روتين طبيعي للرضع دون علامة على أي شيء غير عادي.

في صباحٍ عندما كان عمر جودي حوالي 18 شهرًا، كنت في غرفة المعيشة أمارس عبادتي الشخصية. كانت في المطبخ المجاور عندما سمعنا صوتًا غريبًا—خدش-طرطقة إيقاعية. نظرت باستغراب إلى إيفان. "ما هذا الصوت؟" رفع حاجبيه وهز كتفيه. عندما استمرّت الأصوات، شعرت بالفضول فنهضت من كرسي الهزاز متجهة نحو مصدر الصوت. تلدّح شعور قلق في مؤخرة ذهني وتزايد مع كل خطوة أخطوها. عندما دخلت المطبخ كانت جودي مستلقية على الأرض، ترتعش إيقاعياً. لم أرَ أحدًا في نوبة تشنج من قبل، لكن somehow، عرفته فورًا. إنها في نوبة تشنج!

"هل نتصل برقم الطوارئ؟" اتجه إيفان نحو الهاتف. ترددت. بما أن إيفان كان رجل إطفاء، كان لدينا جهاز استقبال للطوارئ في المنزل. بعد سماع نداءات لا حصر لها على مر السنين ومعرفة أنه أحيانًا قد يستغرق وصول الإسعاف بعض الوقت، لم أشعر بالراحة وأنا أنتظر بالمنزل بينما ابنتنا تتشنج.

"لنأخذها إلى المستشفى." لم أكن مستعدة للجلوس والانتظار حتى تصل المساعدة.

كانت جودي لا تزال ترتعش. حملها إيفان من على الأرض وسلمها لي حتى يحصل على مفاتيحه. محمولة بجودي عن قرب، توجهت نحو الباب. "أحضِر حذائي" ناديت خلفي بينما كنت أهرول حافية القدمين نحو شاحنة البيك آب المتوقفة في الممر السفلي. تخطاني إيفان وفَتَح الباب لي وركض حول جهة السائق. أثناء نزولي التل القصير والمنحدر انزلقت قدماي في ندى الصباح، وسقطت تحت الشاحنة بشكل جزئي مع ساق أمامية وساق أخرى مثنية إلى الخلف تحتيّ. لوهلة فكرت أنني كسرت ساقي، لكن بعد ثانية أو اثنتين من الدهشة نهضت، جمعت حملتي الثمينة، وكافحت لأصعد إلى الشاحنة. كانت جودي لا تزال ترتعش والأسوأ أنها لم تعد تتنفس بشكل صحيح. تراكمت اللعاب في زوايا فمها وتحول إلى رغوة. يا طفلي! ما الذي بها؟ هل ستموت؟! من المدهش كم من الأفكار يمكن أن تجري في ذهن الإنسان في مثل هذا الموقف. لماذا، آه لماذا لا يقود إيفان أسرع؟ إنها لا تتنفس! نظرت إلى عداد السرعة. كان مؤشره مشدودًا إلى اليمين. آه، كان يقود بسرعة. بكل جسدي وعقلي تمنَّيت أن نصل إلى المستشفى.

كان الطريق إلى المستشفى مباشرًا، وتوقّف إيفان عند مدخل الطوارئ مباشرة. قفزت من الشاحنة ومعي طفلتي، صرخت على عجل أن يحضر حذائي إلى الداخل، وركضت نحو باب الطوارئ. كانت ممرضة تخرج حول الزاوية فألقيت طفليتي الثمينة في ذراعيها المندهشة. "إنها تتشنج!" همست بصرخة. نظرت الممرضة إلى جودي ثم أدارت ظهرها وركضت في الممر وأنا ألاحقها. بحلول الوقت الذي دخلنا فيه الغرفة توقفت جودي أخيرًا عن التشنج. بينما كانت مستلقية على النقالة في نصف غيبوبة دخلت نوبة تشنج ثانية أخفّ.

بعد أن خرجت من النوبة الثانية واطمأنت الأمور، طلب الطبيب بعض الفحوصات. بعد مراجعة نتائج الفحوصات قرر الطبيب أنها تعرضت لتشنج حراري ناتج عن ارتفاع أو هبوط مفاجئ في درجة حرارة الجسم. قال إن هذه التشنجات شائعة عند الرضع والأطفال الصغار ولم يبدو عليه القلق كثيرًا. غرّبت غريزتي الأمومية تشخيصه، لكنني لم أكن طبيبة فوافقنا على ما قاله.

كانت هذه مقدمتنا لعالم التشنجات. بعد أسابيع قليلة حدث لها تشنج آخر. ثم حدث آخر. شجعنا والدانا على أخذ رأي ثانٍ. قرر الطبيب الثاني أن تجري جودي رنينًا مغناطيسيًا بالرغم من أن الطبيب الأول ما زال متمسكًا بأنها تعاني تشنجات حرارية ولم يكن مستعجلاً لإجراء الرنين. مرّت عدة أسابيع حتى أُدرجت في الجدول. في اليوم التالي للرنين اتصلوا بنا من عيادة الطبيب. تم تحديد موعد مع جراح أعصاب بعد يومين. تغير الموقف من "لا حاجة للعجلة" إلى "ستكونون هناك بلا نقاش". قال جراح الأعصاب إن لدى جودي تشابكا وعائياً شريانيًا وريديًا (AVM) وحاول أن يشرح ما هو ذلك، لكن معظم المعلومات طارت فوق رأسي. تم تحديد موعد لعمل تصوير وعائي، وأضيفت إلى عقلي الدوار شروحات عن الإجراءات والمتطلبات منا كوالدين. بينما حاولت استيعاب كل هذه المعلومات التي تلقيتها في مكالمة هاتفية واحدة، أدركت أنهم كانوا يستعدون لإمكانية إجراء عملية جراحية.

ازداد إلحاح صلواتنا مع تقدمنا عبر تخطيط كهربية الدماغ (فحص للدماغ يبحث عن نشاط التشنج) وزيارات أطباء أكثر. كنَّا نتوق للشفاء لطفلتنا كي تعيش حياة طبيعية. دخل إيماننا بالله حيز التطبيق بينما كنا نحاول الخضوع لإرادته. انضم إلينا أصدقاء وعائلة ومعارف في الصلاة.

كنا نملك متجرًا للمواد الغذائية بالجملة، وكان كثير من غير المينونايت المحليين يعرفوننا. أصبحنا أصدقاء مقربين مع بعض المسيحيين من كنيسة محلية. عندما سمعوا بالظروف، طلبوا أن يعقدوا اجتماع صلاة ليضعوا أيديهم على جودي ويصلوا لشفائها. رغم أن الكنيسة التي نحضرها عادة لا تفعل هذا، فقد قدّرنا إخلاصهم وإيمانهم بالله، فوافقنا.

حلّ المساء واجتمعنا في كنيستهم مع قسّهم وبعض الأعضاء الذين يعرفوننا. تناوبوا في الصلاة وادعوا شفاء الله لجودي لأنهم "كانوا يعلمون" أن تلك إرادته أن يشفيها. طلبوا بشكل خاص ألا يجد الأطباء أي شيء عند إجراء التصوير الوعائي. ثم دعونا لنصلي أيضًا. مع أننا لسنا معتادين على الصلاة بصوت عالٍ خصوصًا أمام الآخرين، كان لدينا ثقة بأن الله قادر على شفاء طفلنا وأردنا أن نؤدي دورنا. صلينا لإرادة الله وأعلنّاً قبولنا لأي ما يختار.

في اليوم التالي قمنا بالقيادة لمدة ساعة ونصف إلى مستشفى الأطفال في ماديسون لإجراء التصوير الوعائي. الهدف من هذا الفحص كان تحديد سبب تشنجاتها ومعرفة موقعه الدقيق. بعد الفحص عدنا إلى البيت لانتظار النتائج.

لم أكن أريد أن يمنع قلة إيماني شفاء ابنتي، وكنت أعلم أن الله قادر على شفائها، لكن من أنا لأُملي عليه ما يفعل؟ بينما كنت أكافح مع هذا، انتظرنا أخبار الطبيب.

بعد يومين اتصلوا بنا من عيادة الطبيب. قالت الممرضة على الطرف إن التصوير الوعائي لم يُظهر شيئًا! بدا ذلك محيرًا لهم. لم يكن ما توقعوه على الإطلاق، ولم يفهموا لماذا لم يتمكنوا من العثور على المشكلة. الحمد لله! تعجبنا من المعجزة التي صنعها.

عندما أخذنا جودي لموعدها التالي مع جراح الأعصاب، سألته ما كان خطب جودي بما أن التصوير الوعائي لم يجد شيئًا غير عادي. قال إنه يبدو أن هناك كمية صغيرة من النزف في دماغها، لكن لا داعي للقلق. ظننت أن هذه إحدى أغرب العبارات التي سمعتها في حياتي. كنت أعتقد دومًا أن النزف في الدماغ أمر خطير جدًا ولا يجب تجاهله. لكنني كنت متأكدة إلى حد ما من أنني أعرف ما حدث وأخبرت الطبيب عن الصلوات. كان رده لامباليًا، ولم أستطع اكتشاف ما يفكر فيه حقًا.

حددوا موعدًا لزيارة طبية ثانية ورنين بعد ستة أشهر، وهو ما بدا لي غريبًا قليلًا نظرًا لعدم اعتقادهم بوجود شيء خاطئ معها. لم أكن أنوي أن أحتاج ذلك الرنين أو الموعد لأنني كنت أؤمن أن الله شفاها.

في ذلك الصيف أوقفنا دواءاتها المضادة للتشنج تدريجيًا، وبدا أنها بصحة جيدة. كانت الستة أشهر قاربت على الانقضاء، وكنا نعتقد أن مشكلاتها باتت وراءنا.

ثم، قبل أسبوع من موعد الرنين المحدد، حدث لها تشنج. يا له من صدمة! كيف يحدث هذا؟ ألم يشفها الله؟؟ ماذا يحدث؟ شعرت بالخيانة. كل ما استطعت أن أسأله كان: "لماذا؟" وماذا سنفعل الآن؟

يا لها من اضطرابات عاطفية وتدقيق ذاتي! شعرت بخيبة ورجَّت إيماني. كنت أؤمن بالله وكان هذا في النهاية المكان الذي أعود إليه كلما كافحت. ثابتا كالصخر تحت كل الاضطراب كانت الحقيقة أن الله موجود، وطرقه أعلى بكثير من فهمي. وجدت في صميم إيماني بالله مكانًا آمنًا حيث يعرف ويضع مصلحتي في قلبه. وقد لا تتضمن تلك الخطة الأشياء التي أريد أن تحدث في منظوري الأرضي المحدود.

ماذا لو كانت خطته أسمى؟ ماذا لو كان هناك من سنصادفهم خلال رحلتنا الطبية يحتاجون أن يروا المسيح فينا؟ هل كنا مستعدين أن نكون شاهدين له على حساب راحتنا وحياة أسهل؟

انتهى بها الأمر إلى دخولها عملية جراحية في الدماغ وهي في الثالثة ونصف من عمرها فقط. التعامل مع التشنجات والعملية والاختبارات التي لا تُحصى على مر السنين سبب لنا قدرًا لا يستهان به من التوتر، لكن كان لله خطة ولا تزال، وقد لا تُكشف لنا أسباب الـ"لماذا" حتى نراه وجهًا لوجه.

إذن، هل يجيب الله الصلاة دائمًا؟ أقول نعم، يجيب. أحيانًا يقول "نعم" فنحصل على ما نريد؛ أحيانًا تكون إجابته "لا" فلا ينال ما طلبناه؛ وأحيانًا يهمس "انتظر"، وفي وقته وبحسب طريقته يسمح لنا بتحقيق ما في قلوبنا. كطفل يثق بوالديه، سأترك إجابات صلواتي في يد إلهي القدير والثقة بأنه أدرى بما هو خير لحياتي.

"O give thanks unto the God of heaven: for His mercy endureth for ever"
—Psalm 136:26

In your journey of life, from infancy to where you are today, have you ever taken a few minutes to meditate on the mercy God has shown you? Infancy to childhood, childhood to youth, youth to adulthood, and beyond, God's everlasting mercy is upon them that fear Him! The scripture says in Deuteronomy 7:9 that the mercy of God extends way past our short lives here on earth, even to a thousand generations. Take a moment and wonder in the glory and beauty of this unchanging, eternal attribute of God!

As we take a look at the history behind this hymn, let us endeavor to see the hand of God at work in the life of the hymn writer. The hymn, "When All Thy Mercies O My God," written in 1712, has been published in 994 hymnals and is to this day in the list of the best 100 hymns ever written. As the writer nears the end of his time on earth, he reflects in this hymn his awe at the mercies of God toward him throughout his life.

Joseph Addison, born May 1, 1672, was an English essayist, poet, and man of letters. Concerning his birth, we find that he “appeared weak and unlikely to live", Mr. Tyers says.* And that “he was laid out for dead as soon as he was born.” Without doubt, the providence of God preserved his young life and gave him nearly half a century to serve Him on the earth. He was the eldest son of Lancelot Addison, a well-learned man and minister in his church. His father, being a studious man himself, made sure his son Joseph had a good education. He commenced his studies in his hometown of Milston, in Wiltshire, England.

While in school around 1685, the 13-year-old hymn writer met and became best of friends with Richard Steele, the two of them being only a few months apart in age. They continued their friendship throughout the years, and 27 years later from 1711 to 1712, they cofounded The Spectator magazine, in which this hymn was first published.

After passing through several schools, Addison went to Oxford when he was about 15 years old. While he was there, he continued to gain in learning and skill, especially in the areas of writing Latin poems and essays. By the time he was 22, in 1694, he also began to show his skill at writing English poetry.

One of the most notable details of his life that conveyed to him the mercy of God is how he managed to narrowly escape an awful shipwreck. It was this tragedy and his frightening tale of survival that would go on to inspire the writing of this uplifting hymn.

Here is the hymn with the original 13 verses:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view,
I’m lost In wonder, love and praise.

Thy Providence my life sustained,
And all my wants redressed,
While in the silent womb I lay,
And hung upon the breast.

To all my weak complaints and cries
Thy mercy lent an ear,
Ere yet my feeble thoughts had learned,
To form themselves in prayer.

Unnumbered comforts to my soul
Thy tender care bestowed,
Before my infant heart conceived
From Whom those comforts flowed.

When in the slippery paths of youth
With heedless steps I ran,
Thine arm unseen conveyed me safe,
And led me up to man.

Through hidden dangers, toils, and deaths,
It gently cleared my way;
And through the pleasing snares of vice,
More to be feared than they.

O how shall words with equal warmth
The gratitude declare,
That glows within my ravished heart?
But thou canst read it there.

Thy bounteous hand with worldly bliss
Hath made my cup run o’er;
And, in a kind and faithful Friend,
Hath doubled all my store.

Ten thousand thousand precious gifts
My daily thanks employ;
Nor is the last a cheerful heart
That tastes those gifts with joy.

When worn with sickness, oft hast Thou
With health renewed my face;
And, when in sins and sorrows sunk,
Revived my soul with grace.

Through every period of my life
Thy goodness I’ll pursue
And after death, in distant worlds,
The glorious theme renew.

When nature fails, and day and night
Divide Thy works no more,
My ever grateful heart,
O Lord,Thy mercy shall adore.

Through all eternity to Thee
A joyful song I’ll raise;
For, oh, eternity’s too short
To utter all Thy praise!

As we endeavor to understand the life and story of the hymnologist, let's take a short look at some disappointments he faced. Being single into his 40s, he had hopes of someday having a happy marriage. His marriage to Charlotte, a widow of 15 years, didn’t turn out as he had anticipated. It is said that their courtship was long and anxious. They were married in August 1716 in his 44th year. A quote states that “He is said to have first known her by becoming tutor to her son. The marriage, if uncontradicted report can be credited, made no addition to his happiness; it neither found them nor made them equal."* In addition to his less-than-ideal marriage, the loss of his good friend Richard Steele sometime after that took a toll on him.

By the year 1717, his health began to decline rapidly, and by March 1718, he had to resign some of his work positions, having a great need for rest and quietness. "The disease under which Addison laboured appears to have been asthma. It became more violent after his retirement from office and was now accompanied by dropsy. His deathbed was placid and resigned, and comforted by those religious hopes which he had so often suggested to others..." *

One last note I will include here on the life of the hymn writer is the account of his passing. There was a young man by the name of Lord Warwick, rough and loose in character, who Addison had often tried to win to the faith, all to no avail. Nearing the end of his life, he endeavored one last attempt to impress this young man with the importance of Christianity. He sent for him to come and be present as he passed away, saying, "I have sent for you that you may see how a Christian can die." We have no record of how this experience affected Warwick’s behavior, but we can assume that it most likely did. Joseph Addison died at Holland House on the 17th of June, 1719, six weeks after his 47th birthday. He is buried in the Poet's Corner of Westminster Abbey.

This hymn has several tunes: “St Peter,” composed by Alexander Robert Reinagle in 1836, is used in the Church Hymnal and Christian Hymnary. The tune "Geneva" was composed by John Cole in 1805. He was born in Tewksbury, England, and came to the United States in his boyhood. Baltimore, Maryland became his American home, and he was educated there. Early in life, he became a musician and music publisher. He continued to compose music until his death. This tune is found in the Zion's Praises, Hymns of the Church, and Harmonia Sacra. The tune "Contemplation", composed by F.A.Gore Ouseley, is more widely used by evangelical and other church groups. Other hymns by Joseph Addison include "The Lord my Pasture Shall Prepare" and "The Spacious Firmament." Here is one final quote to help us understand who Joseph Addison was and what he believed. "His religion has nothing in it enthusiastic or superstitious; he appears neither weakly credulous nor wantonly skeptical; his morality is neither dangerously lax nor impracticably rigid. All the enchantment of fancy and all the cogency of argument are employed to recommend to the reader his real interest, the care of pleasing the Author of his being."

*sourced from Wikipedia and hymnary.org

"O geef dank aan de God des hemels: want Zijn goedertierenheid is in eeuwigheid"
—Psalm 136:26

In je levensreis, van zuigeling tot waar je nu bent, heb je ooit een paar minuten genomen om na te denken over de barmhartigheid die God jou heeft getoond? Van zuigeling naar kindertijd, van kindertijd naar jeugd, van jeugd naar volwassenheid en verder — Gods eeuwige barmhartigheid is over degenen die Hem vrezen! De Schrift zegt in Deuteronomium 7:9 dat de barmhartigheden van God veel verder reiken dan ons korte leven hier op aarde, zelfs tot duizend geslachten. Neem een ogenblik en verwonder je over de heerlijkheid en schoonheid van deze onveranderlijke, eeuwige eigenschap van God!

Als we naar de geschiedenis achter dit lied kijken, laten we dan proberen de hand van God te zien in het leven van de tekstschrijver. Het hymnegedicht „When All Thy Mercies O My God,” geschreven in 1712, is in 994 liedbundels gepubliceerd en staat tot op de dag van vandaag in de lijst van de beste 100 gezangen ooit geschreven. Terwijl de schrijver het einde van zijn aardse levenspad nadert, weerspiegelt hij in dit lied zijn ontzag over Gods barmhartigheden jegens hem gedurende zijn hele leven.

Joseph Addison, geboren 1 mei 1672, was een Engels essayist, dichter en man van letters. Over zijn geboorte vinden we dat hij “zwak verscheen en onwaarschijnlijk te zullen leven", zegt de heer Tyers.* En dat “hij bij de geboorte al voor dood werd neergelegd.” Zonder twijfel heeft Gods voorzienigheid zijn jonge leven bewaard en hem bijna een halve eeuw gegeven om Hem op aarde te dienen. Hij was de oudste zoon van Lancelot Addison, een geleerd man en predikant in zijn kerk. Zijn vader, zelf een ijverige geleerde, zorgde ervoor dat Joseph een goede opleiding kreeg. Hij begon zijn studie in zijn geboortedorp Milston, in Wiltshire, Engeland.

Toen hij op school was rond 1685, ontmoette de 13-jarige liedschrijver Richard Steele en werden ze de beste vrienden; ze waren maar enkele maanden van elkaar verwijderd in leeftijd. Ze hielden hun vriendschap door de jaren heen in stand, en 27 jaar later, van 1711 tot 1712, waren zij medeoprichters van het tijdschrift The Spectator, waarin dit lied voor het eerst werd gepubliceerd.

Na verschillende scholen te hebben doorlopen, ging Addison op ongeveer 15‑jarige leeftijd naar Oxford. Terwijl hij daar was, bleef hij in kennis en vaardigheid groeien, vooral op het gebied van het schrijven van Latijnse gedichten en essays. Tegen de tijd dat hij 22 was, in 1694, begon hij ook zijn talent in het schrijven van Engelse poëzie te tonen.

Een van de meest opmerkelijke gebeurtenissen in zijn leven die hem Gods barmhartigheid duidelijk maakte, is hoe hij ternauwernood aan een afschuwelijke schipbreuk ontsnapte. Het was deze ramp en zijn angstaanjagende verhaal van overleving die de inspiratie zouden vormen voor het schrijven van dit opbeurende lied.

Hier is het lied met de oorspronkelijke 13 coupletten:

Wanneer al Uw barmhartigheden, o mijn God,
Mijn opkomende ziel beziet,
Verheugd door dat gezicht,
Ben ik verloren in verwondering, liefde en lof.

Uw Voorzienigheid heeft mijn leven gedragen,
En al mijn noden verholpen,
Terwijl ik in de stille moederwijd lag,
En hing aan de borst.

Op al mijn zwakke klachten en kreten
Heeft Uw barmhartigheid een oor geleend,
Nog eer mijn zwakke gedachten geleerd hadden,
Zichzelf in gebed te vormen.

Ontelbare vertroostingen aan mijn ziel
Heeft Uw tedere zorg geschonken,
Voordat mijn kinderhart begreep
Van wie die vertroostingen vloeiden.

Toen ik op de glibberige paden der jeugd
Met onbezonnen stappen liep,
Heeft Uw onzichtbare arm mij veilig gedragen,
En geleid naar volwassenheid.

Door verborgen gevaren, zwoegen en doden,
Schoonde Hij zacht mijn pad;
En door de aangename strikken van zonde,
Meer te vrezen dan zij.

O hoe zullen woorden met gelijke warmte
De dankbaarheid verklaren,
Die binnenin mijn verrukte hart gloeien?
Maar U kunt het daar lezen.

Uw gulle hand heeft met wereldse zegen
Mijn beker doen overlopen;
En in een vriendelijke en trouwe Vriend,
Heeft Hij al mijn bezit verdubbeld.

Tien duizend duizend kostbare gaven
Vullen mijn dagelijkse dank;
En niet het minste is een blij hart
Dat die gaven met vreugde proeft.

Wanneer verzwakt door ziekte hebt U dikwijls
Met gezondheid mijn gelaat vernieuwd;
En, wanneer zondig en in droefheid gezonken,
Hebt U mijn ziel met genade herleefd.

Door elke periode van mijn leven
Zal ik Uw goedheid achtervolgen
En na de dood, in verre werelden,
Het heerlijke onderwerp vernieuwen.

Wanneer de natuur faalt, en dag en nacht
Uw werken niet meer scheiden,
Zal mijn altijd dankbaar hart,
O Heere, Uw barmhartigheid aanbidden.

Door alle eeuwigheid zal ik U
Een vreugdevol lied opheffen;
Want, o, de eeuwigheid is te kort
Om al Uw lof te uiten!

Terwijl we proberen het leven en verhaal van de hymnost te begrijpen, bekijken we kort enkele teleurstellingen waarmee hij geconfronteerd werd. Als vrijgezel tot in de veertig had hij hoop op een gelukkige huwelijksband. Zijn huwelijk met Charlotte, een weduwe van 15 jaar, liep niet zoals hij had verwacht. Er wordt gezegd dat hun hofmakerij lang en angstig was. Zij trouwden in augustus 1716, in zijn 44e jaar. Een citaat stelt dat “men zegt dat hij haar eerst leerde kennen door tutor te worden van haar zoon. Het huwelijk, als ongecontradigeerd gerucht geloofd kan worden, bracht geen toename van zijn geluk; het vond hen noch maakte hen gelijk."* Naast zijn minder‑dan‑ideale huwelijk, bracht ook het verlies van zijn goede vriend Richard Steele enige tijd daarna veel verdriet voor hem.

Tegen het jaar 1717 begon zijn gezondheid snel te verslechteren, en in maart 1718 moest hij sommige van zijn functies neerleggen, met een grote behoefte aan rust en stilte. "De ziekte waaronder Addison leed, lijkt astma te zijn geweest. Het werd heviger na zijn terugtreden uit ambt en ging nu gepaard met vochtopeenhoping. Zijn sterfbed was rustig en berustend, en getroost door die godsdienstige hoop die hij zo vaak aan anderen had gesuggereerd..." *

Een laatste noot die ik hier zal opnemen over het leven van de liedschrijver is het verslag van zijn sterven. Er was een jonge man genaamd Lord Warwick, ruw en los in karakter, die Addison vaak had proberen te winnen voor het geloof, maar zonder succes. Toen het einde van zijn leven naderde, deed hij nog één poging om deze jongeman te overtuigen van het belang van het christendom. Hij liet hem komen om aanwezig te zijn bij zijn overlijden, zeggende: "Ik heb u laten komen zodat u kunt zien hoe een christen kan sterven." We hebben geen verslag van hoe deze ervaring Warwicks gedrag beinvloedde, maar we mogen aannemen dat het waarschijnlijk effect had. Joseph Addison stierf in Holland House op 17 juni 1719, zes weken na zijn 47ste verjaardag. Hij is begraven in de Poets' Corner van Westminster Abbey.

Dit lied heeft verschillende melodieën: “St Peter,” gecomponeerd door Alexander Robert Reinagle in 1836, wordt gebruikt in de Church Hymnal en Christian Hymnary. De melodie "Geneva" werd gecomponeerd door John Cole in 1805. Hij werd geboren in Tewksbury, Engeland, en kwam in zijn jeugd naar de Verenigde Staten. Baltimore, Maryland werd zijn Amerikaanse thuis, en hij kreeg daar zijn opleiding. Vroeg in zijn leven werd hij muzikant en uitgever van muziek. Hij bleef muziek componeren tot zijn dood. Deze melodie is te vinden in Zion's Praises, Hymns of the Church, en Harmonia Sacra. De melodie "Contemplation", gecomponeerd door F.A. Gore Ouseley, wordt vaker gebruikt door evangelische en andere kerkelijke groepen. Andere gezangen van Joseph Addison zijn onder meer "The Lord my Pasture Shall Prepare" en "The Spacious Firmament." Hier is nog een citaat om ons te helpen begrijpen wie Joseph Addison was en wat hij geloofde. "Zijn religie heeft niets enthousiasts of bijgelovigs; hij lijkt noch zwak gelovig noch opzettelijk sceptisch; zijn moraliteit is noch gevaarlijk los noch onpraktisch streng. Al de betovering van verbeelding en al de overtuigingskracht van argument worden aangewend om de lezer zijn werkelijk belang aan te bevelen, de zorg om de Schepper van zijn bestaan te beha gen."

*gebaseerd op bronnen van Wikipedia en hymnary.org

Greetings in the worthy name of the Lord Jesus Christ. As I gaze out across the barren January landscape, I can’t help but wonder what this new year will bring. Undoubtedly, it will bring a mixture of joy and sorrow, excitement and drear, laughter and tears, and everything else in between, which only an Almighty Creator God can arrange in such a way that will magnify His worthy power and excellence. Yet our finite, negative minds tend to anticipate all the bad things that could happen. Will inflation drive food prices even higher? Will widespread fighting erupt across the Middle East? What will happen in the elections? Will the losing party resort to protests and rioting?

I suppose, since the fall of man, these fear-driven thoughts have roamed through the minds of humanity at the beginning of each year. Yet, as it is so aptly pointed out by the writer of the article, “God’s Faithfulness Manifest Even in the Curse”, God has kindly provided for humanity since the beginning of time. Looking back at God’s faithfulness to man over the centuries, we have no reason to doubt God will do the same for us in 2024.

Despite God’s faithfulness to us, the effects of the fall of man are still evident. Family members get sick, church and relationship struggles rob us of sleep, the checkbook runs dry, the children squabble and cry, and the demands of our schedules have us hopping from one event to the next. And sometimes, it seems that all these calamities hit us at the same time. Our bodies and minds are not created to handle this. We become weary. Bone tired. Exhausted to the point when even thinking hurts. We face burnout. In this issue, “A Word From the Doctor” guides us as we face the maze of life, giving us practical and Biblical solutions to avoid or recover from burnout. He writes, “Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.”

Perhaps one good remedy to reduce the stress of life would be to go for a bike ride. But we need to be careful and avoid getting into a bike race like the two lads did in this issue’s children’s story. We may end up with more stress than we bargained for.

Despite our best efforts to live stress-free lives, we still meet with the unexpected. Last week I was cleaning out our broiler houses in preparation for a new flock. I leaned across the tractor fender to push a partly opened door out of the way. As I stood up, my foot accidentally hit the hydrostatic pedal, lurching the tractor forward and throwing me off-balance. My foot somehow got caught under the pedal, and for a split second, I feared I would fall right in front of the rear wheel. In a last-ditch effort, I threw myself away from the tractor. My foot slipped out of my shoe, and I landed unharmed on the ground. The tractor slowly headed off with my shoe still wedged under the pedal. All ended well, and a few lessons were learned. It was nothing other than the providence of God that prevented a freak incident from becoming a bad accident. Truly I agree with Solomon, “For the LORD shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken” (Proverbs 3:26).

As we navigate through this year, let’s join the hymnwriter in worship, where he writes:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view, I’m lost
In wonder, love and praise.

It is only by the mercies of an all-loving God that we have life and breath. May we give our all to Him and to the work of His kingdom in heartfelt thanksgiving for His unspeakable gift.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Saluti nel degno nome del Signore Gesù Cristo. Mentre guardo il paesaggio spoglio di gennaio, non posso fare a meno di chiedermi cosa porterà questo nuovo anno. Indubbiamente porterà un miscuglio di gioia e dolore, eccitazione e mestizia, risate e lacrime, e tutto il resto nel mezzo, che solo un Dio Creatore Onnipotente può disporre in modo da magnificarne la degna potenza e eccellenza. Eppure le nostre menti finite e negative tendono ad anticipare tutte le cose brutte che potrebbero accadere. L’inflazione farà salire ancora di più i prezzi dei generi alimentari? Scoppieranno ampi conflitti in Medio Oriente? Cosa succederà nelle elezioni? Il partito sconfitto ricorrerà a proteste e saccheggi?

Suppongo che, dalla caduta dell’uomo, questi pensieri guidati dalla paura abbiano vagato per le menti dell’umanità all’inizio di ogni anno. Eppure, come viene così appropriatamente sottolineato dallo scrittore dell’articolo, “God’s Faithfulness Manifest Even in the Curse”, Dio ha provveduto bene all’umanità fin dall’inizio dei tempi. Guardando alla fedeltà di Dio verso l’uomo nei secoli, non abbiamo motivo di dubitare che farà lo stesso per noi nel 2024.

Nonostante la fedeltà di Dio verso di noi, gli effetti della caduta dell’uomo sono ancora evidenti. I membri della famiglia si ammalano, lotte in chiesa e nelle relazioni ci rubano il sonno, il conto è vuoto, i bambini litigano e piangono, e le esigenze dei nostri impegni ci fanno correre da un evento all’altro. E a volte sembra che tutte queste calamità ci colpiscano contemporaneamente. I nostri corpi e le nostre menti non sono creati per sopportare tutto ciò. Diventiamo stanchi. Stanchi fino alle ossa. Esausti al punto che persino pensare fa male. Affrontiamo il burnout. In questo numero, “A Word From the Doctor” ci guida mentre affrontiamo il labirinto della vita, offrendoci soluzioni pratiche e bibliche per evitare o riprendersi dal burnout. Egli scrive: “Gesù conosce i nostri limiti. Vuole che abbiamo equilibrio, vivendo in modo da avere non solo forza per oggi ma anche per domani, la settimana prossima e l’anno prossimo – fino a che Egli venga di nuovo.”

Forse un buon rimedio per ridurre lo stress della vita sarebbe fare un giro in bicicletta. Ma dobbiamo stare attenti ed evitare di finire in una gara di bici come hanno fatto i due ragazzi nella storia per bambini di questo numero. Potremmo ritrovarci con più stress di quanto avessimo previsto.

Nonostante i nostri migliori sforzi per vivere senza stress, ci imbattiamo comunque nell’inaspettato. La settimana scorsa stavo pulendo le nostre stalle per i polli in preparazione per un nuovo gregge. Mi sono chinato oltre il parafango del trattore per spostare di lato una porta parzialmente aperta. Mentre mi alzavo, il mio piede ha colpito accidentalmente il pedale idrostatico, facendo sobbalzare il trattore in avanti e sbilanciandomi. In qualche modo il mio piede si è incastrato sotto il pedale e per un istante ho temuto di cadere proprio davanti alla ruota posteriore. In un ultimo disperato tentativo mi sono lanciato lontano dal trattore. Il mio piede è scivolato fuori dalla scarpa e sono atterrato illeso a terra. Il trattore è lentamente ripartito con la mia scarpa ancora incuneata sotto il pedale. Tutto è finito bene e sono state apprese alcune lezioni. Non è stato nient’altro che la provvidenza di Dio a impedire che un episodio bizzarro si trasformasse in un grave incidente. Concordo pienamente con Salomone: “Poiché il SIGNORE sarà la tua fiducia e terrà il tuo piede dal venire preso” (Proverbi 3:26).

Mentre navighiamo in questo anno, uniamoci al cantore di inni nel culto, dove egli scrive:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view, I’m lost
In wonder, love and praise.

È solo per le misericordie di un Dio che ama che abbiamo vita e respiro. Possiamo offrire tutto a Lui e all’opera del Suo regno in ringraziamento sincero per il Suo dono inesprimibile.

Benedizioni a tutti,

Edward Martin

Just reading the title probably brings negative thoughts to your mind. We as humans don’t typically like to be told “no” because it goes against our nature. Sometimes we bring the “no” upon ourselves because of disobedience, such as when God said “no” to Moses. “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land . . . But the Lord . . . would not hear me: and the Lord said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter” (Deuteronomy 3:25,26).

In Deuteronomy 1:42, God said “no” to Israel. “And the Lord said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies”, but they rebelled at His “no.” “And ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you” (Deuteronomy 1:45).

God said “no” to Paul. “And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me” (2 Corinthians 12:7-9).

Let us focus our attention upon prayerful Paul’s acceptance of God’s “no.”

First, acceptance does not mean that the problem does not exist. Paul accepted God’s “no”, but still had the infirmities.

Second, acceptance does not mean woeful resignation. Paul “besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.” We should be persistent, even when God’s answer is not forthcoming. (cf. Luke 18:1-8).

Third, God’s “no” may be necessary to avoid a greater evil or infirmity. Twice, Paul says the thorn in the flesh was given “lest I should be exalted above measure.” Unlike Paul, however, we may not know the purpose for God’s “no,” but we can be assured of His faithfulness and goodness. With Paul, we too may have to endure one thing, which means accepting God’s refusal in order to achieve a higher purpose or benefit.

Fourth, Paul’s weakness, as a result of God’s “no,” made him strong. “Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10). The sorrow and suffering some endure has indeed made them strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.

Fifth, Paul’s infirmity allowed the power of Christ to rest upon him. God’s strength was complete, sufficient, and made perfect in weakness. Paul’s strength was seen to be of God. Therefore, Christ, not Paul, was glorified. The infirmities that Paul endured revealed the power not of himself but of God.

Sixth, God explained his answer of “no” by saying, “My grace is sufficient for thee.” God’s love and acceptance of us, His strength and power to assist us in our infirmities and with our weaknesses, is sufficient and complete.

Seventh, Paul gloried in his infirmities, but only after he accepted God’s “no.” Paul ultimately saw that this allowed God’s power to rest upon him. Paul’s weakness displayed and magnified divine power in a manner that human adequacy and personal sufficiency could never accomplish.

Eighth, unfortunately for him, Paul was the vessel, the sufferer, who had to endure afflictions that God’s grace, power, and glory might be truly reflected, but he was glad to bear it for those purposes (cf. 2 Co 4:7-11; Gal 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Until we are ready to do the same, we cannot accept or understand God’s “no.”

A “no” may come into our life for many various reasons.

When God says, “No,” the Christian must remember:

That God will do right. “He is … a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he” (Deuteronomy 32:4). One may not see; he may not, as Job did not, understand, but God will do right. “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” (Genesis 18:25).

That God’s ways are not ours. “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts” (Isaiah 55:8,9). God sees the end from the beginning. Nothing is hidden from him. “Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it” (Psalms 139:6). as a little child cries in protest when his mother pulls him from the road (It is such a great place to ride a tricycle!), so we may cry when God says, “No,” but He, like the child’s parent, knows danger the child may not be able to comprehend or appreciate fully.

That prayer has a chief purpose. Prayer should not be an attempt to manipulate the will of God. “Not my will, but thine, be done,” the suffering Savior cried, but when God says, “No,” we often forget that fact and complain in effect, “Not Thy will but mine be done.” Perhaps the supreme purpose of prayer is to seek God’s will for our lives, our wants, our needs, and our desires. It will help to remember that when God says “no.”

That a present “no” may be a “yes” in development. Paul was told that he was going to Rome (Acts 19:21; 23:11). But the bars of incarceration, the shackles of servitude, and the jaws of death seemed to say otherwise. Two years of confinement were not convincing evidence of a trip to Rome, nor was a hopeless sea voyage (Acts 24:27; 27:20). However, as we all know, Paul went to Rome (Acts 28:16)!

That God’s laws prevail. The laws of nature are laws of God. God does not will that one to fall off a cliff, but if certain physical laws are broken, he will. God has biological laws. Disease may be contracted, and suffering and death may follow. One may pray, “Give us this day our daily bread,” but if he does not use God’s laws to procure it, or if he contradicts God’s means of acquiring it, he will not receive it. As painful as it is to accept, we frequently are victims of earthly laws in the various and diverse orders of physical life. Of course, the reverse is also true. We often are blessed by the material laws of God (Matthew 5:45; Acts 14:17; 1 Timothy 5:23).

In conclusion, Job of old bore the lashes of unparalleled human calamity and agony and torture of mind, body, and soul. His faithfulness and steadfast endurance have blessed thirty centuries of sorrowing humanity. Stephen and James met untimely, violent deaths (Acts 7; 12). They died when we would have had them to live. By their suffering and death, the early disciples were shown the power of the new faith, that men could die and yet live in victory. Hence, multiplied millions have been emboldened and have accepted torture and death rather than denounce their faith and hope of eternal life.

Deliverance came. No, not to Stephen and James, nor to suffering servants such as Job, of like precious faith, but it came in unquenchable hope, in the hope that maketh not ashamed. It came through Him that is able to deliver us who, through fear of death, were subject to bondage. “Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.”

Bastano il titolo a far sorgere probabilmente pensieri negativi nella tua mente. Noi esseri umani di solito non amiamo sentirci dire “no” perché va contro la nostra natura. Talvolta ci procuriamo il “no” da soli a causa della disobbedienza, come quando Dio disse “no” a Mosè. “Ti scongiuro: fammi passare e veda il paese buono . . . Ma il Signore . . . non volle ascoltarmi; e il Signore mi disse: Ti basta; non mi parlare più di questa cosa” (Deuteronomio 3:25,26).

In Deuteronomio 1:42 Dio disse “no” a Israele. “E il Signore mi disse: Di’ loro: Non salite, e non combattete; perché io non sono tra voi, e non siate colpiti davanti ai vostri nemici”, ma essi si ribellarono al Suo “no”. “E voi tornaste e piangete davanti al Signore; ma il Signore non volle dar ascolto alla vostra voce, né porre mente a voi” (Deuteronomio 1:45).

Dio disse “no” a Paolo. “E perché non fossi sopra misura esaltato per le rivelazioni, fu data a me una spina nella carne, un messaggero di Satana per percotermi, perché non fossi esaltato oltre misura. Per questa cosa tre volte ho pregato il Signore che si allontanasse da me. Ed egli mi ha detto: Ti basta la mia grazia; perché la mia forza si dimostra perfetta nella debolezza. Molto volentieri dunque mi vanterò delle mie infermità, affinché la potenza di Cristo dimori su di me” (2 Corinzi 12:7-9).

Rivolgiamo la nostra attenzione all’accettazione del “no” da parte del preghierevole Paolo.

Primo, accettare non significa che il problema non esista. Paolo accettò il “no” di Dio, ma conservò tuttavia le infermità.

Secondo, accettare non significa rassegnazione desolata. Paolo “pregò il Signore per tre volte che si allontanasse da me.” Dobbiamo essere perseveranti, anche quando la risposta di Dio non arriva. (cfr. Luca 18:1-8).

Terzo, il “no” di Dio può essere necessario per evitare un male o un’infermità maggiore. Due volte Paolo dice che la spina nella carne gli fu data “affinché non fossi esaltato oltre misura.” Tuttavia, a differenza di Paolo, noi potremmo non conoscere lo scopo del “no” di Dio, ma possiamo essere certi della Sua fedeltà e bontà. Come Paolo, anche noi potremmo dover sopportare una cosa, cioè accettare il rifiuto di Dio per conseguire uno scopo o un beneficio più elevato.

Quarto, la debolezza di Paolo, come conseguenza del “no” di Dio, lo rese forte. “Perciò mi compiaccio nelle infermità, nelle offese, nelle necessità, nelle persecuzioni, nelle angustie per amor di Cristo; perché quando sono debole, allora sono forte” (2 Corinzi 12:10). Il dolore e la sofferenza che alcuni sopportano li ha effettivamente resi forti nel Signore e nella potenza della Sua forza.

Quinto, l’infermità di Paolo permise alla potenza di Cristo di riposare su di lui. La forza di Dio era completa, sufficiente e resa perfetta nella debolezza. La forza di Paolo apparve essere di Dio. Perciò fu Cristo, non Paolo, a essere glorificato. Le infermità che Paolo sopportò rivelarono la potenza non di lui stesso ma di Dio.

Sesto, Dio spiegò la Sua risposta di “no” dicendo: “Ti basta la mia grazia.” L’amore e l’accettazione di Dio verso di noi, la Sua forza e il Suo potere per assisterci nelle nostre infermità e debolezze, sono sufficienti e completi.

Settimo, Paolo si glorificò nelle sue infermità, ma solo dopo aver accettato il “no” di Dio. Paolo alla fine vide che ciò permetteva alla potenza di Dio di riposare su di lui. La debolezza di Paolo mostrò e ingrandì il potere divino in modo che la capacità umana e l’autosufficienza personale non avrebbero mai potuto ottenere.

Ottavo, sfortunatamente per lui, Paolo fu il vaso, il sofferente, che dovette sopportare afflizioni affinché la grazia, la potenza e la gloria di Dio potessero essere veramente riflesse, ma fu lieto di sopportarle per tali scopi (cfr. 2 Cor 4:7-11; Gal 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Finché non saremo pronti a fare lo stesso, non possiamo accettare né comprendere il “no” di Dio.

Un “no” può entrare nella nostra vita per molte ragioni diverse.

Quando Dio dice “No,” il cristiano deve ricordare:

Che Dio farà ciò che è giusto. “Egli è … un Dio di verità e senza iniquità, giusto e retto è egli” (Deuteronomio 32:4). Uno può non vedere; può non comprendere, come non comprese Giobbe, ma Dio farà ciò che è giusto. “Forse il Giudice di tutta la terra non farà giustizia?” (Genesi 18:25).

Che le vie di Dio non sono le nostre. “Perché i miei pensieri non sono i vostri pensieri, né le vostre vie le mie vie, dice il Signore. Poiché come sono più alti i cieli della terra, così sono più alte le mie vie delle vostre vie e i miei pensieri dei vostri pensieri” (Isaia 55:8,9). Dio vede la fine dal principio. Null’è nascosto a lui. “Una tale conoscenza è troppo meravigliosa per me; è alta, non posso raggiungerla” (Salmi 139:6). Come un bambino piange in protesta quando la madre lo tira dalla strada (È un posto così bello per andare con il triciclo!), così possiamo piangere quando Dio dice “No,” ma Egli, come il genitore del bambino, conosce il pericolo che il bambino non può comprendere o apprezzare pienamente.

Che la preghiera ha uno scopo principale. La preghiera non dovrebbe essere un tentativo di manipolare la volontà di Dio. “Non la mia volontà, ma la tua sia fatta,” gridò il Salvatore sofferente, ma quando Dio dice “No,” spesso dimentichiamo questo fatto e ci lamentiamo di fatto: “Non la tua volontà ma la mia sia fatta.” Forse lo scopo supremo della preghiera è cercare la volontà di Dio per la nostra vita, i nostri desideri, i nostri bisogni e le nostre aspirazioni. Questo aiuterà a ricordare quando Dio dice “no.”

Che un “no” presente può essere un “sì” in formazione. A Paolo fu detto che sarebbe andato a Roma (Atti 19:21; 23:11). Ma le sbarre della prigionia, le catene del servaggio e le fauci della morte sembravano dire il contrario. Due anni di reclusione non erano prova convincente di un viaggio a Roma, né lo fu un viaggio per mare disperato (Atti 24:27; 27:20). Tuttavia, come tutti sappiamo, Paolo andò a Roma (Atti 28:16)!

Che le leggi di Dio prevalgono. Le leggi della natura sono leggi di Dio. Dio non vuole che uno cada da una scogliera, ma se certe leggi fisiche vengono infrante, ciò avverrà. Dio ha leggi biologiche. Si può contrarre una malattia, e può seguire sofferenza e morte. Si può pregare: “Dacci oggi il nostro pane quotidiano,” ma se non si usano le leggi di Dio per procurarselo, o se si contraddicono i mezzi che Dio ha stabilito per ottenerlo, non lo si riceverà. Per quanto doloroso sia accettarlo, siamo frequentemente vittime delle leggi terrene nelle varie e diverse disposizioni della vita fisica. Naturalmente, vale anche l’inverso. Spesso siamo benedetti dalle leggi materiali di Dio (Matteo 5:45; Atti 14:17; 1 Timoteo 5:23).

In conclusione, Giobbe un tempo sopportò i colpi di calamità umane, angosce e torture mentali, corporali e dell’anima senza pari. La sua fedeltà e la sua costante sopportazione hanno benedetto trentacinque secoli di umanità afflitta. Stefano e Giacomo incontrarono morti premature e violente (Atti 7; 12). Morirono quando noi avremmo voluto che vivessero. Per mezzo della loro sofferenza e morte, ai primi discepoli fu mostrata la potenza della nuova fede: che gli uomini potevano morire e tuttavia vivere nella vittoria. Perciò, milioni moltiplicati sono stati incoraggiati e hanno accettato torture e morte piuttosto che rinnegare la loro fede e la speranza di vita eterna.

La liberazione venne. No, non per Stefano e Giacomo, né per servi sofferenti come Giobbe, di simile preziosa fede, ma essa venne in speranza inestinguibile, nella speranza che non confonde. Essa venne per mezzo di Colui che è potente per liberarci, noi che, per timore della morte, eravamo soggetti a schiavitù. “Rendiamo grazie a Dio per il suo dono ineffabile.”

Someone once said “When hope is alive, the night is less dark, the solitude less deep, and fear less acute.” When I worked in a prison as an assistant chaplain, I would sit with the condemned men and listen as they talked of their plight. Almost without exception, all spoke of hoping to get out of prison one day. Even if they had a life sentence, they hoped to get out.

I have spoken to people who do not confess to be born again, but still hope to go to heaven. These people dare not leave off hoping. Their hope is based upon their own hope! A diet on that kind of hope is a slim diet for sure! This reasoning reminds me of Jesus' words in John 10:1-2 about entering the sheepfold. “But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.” People build their hope for heaven on many shaky things. Some base their hope on having been baptized in a certain church. Some hope in their church membership. Some people hope in their good works, while still others hope in their hope. The Bible, however, says, “. . . except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God” (John 3:3).

There is a true hope and a false hope. The false hope is “climbing up some other way,” but true hope is “he that entereth in by the door.”

“For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?” (Romans 8:24). This word hope means “with anticipation or great expectation.” Could we say that we are saved by great expectation? Yes, we can. “Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed” (John 6:27). This seems to be a contradiction of sorts. Are we not saved by grace? Yes, we are saved by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8). Then what is this being saved by hope and laboring for the “meat which endureth unto everlasting life”?

“Then they said unto him, what shall we do, that we might work the works of God?” Jesus answered and said unto them, “this is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent” (John 6:28-29). It is only by grace that we are saved, but as this passage suggests, grace sets a condition. The condition of grace is that we believe on Him. Another condition of salvation is repentance (Mark 1:15), while another is cross-bearing. “Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross and follow me” (Mark 8:34).

Everything we would do for Christ, whether believing, repenting, or cross-bearing, is by grace. Whatever we have, or do, is because of Him. We do not work for our salvation, for Christ Himself said, “It is finished.” We have nothing to hope for if we do not meet the conditions of our salvation. Once we receive the Lord Jesus as Saviour, then “hope maketh not ashamed” (Romans 5:5).

As Christ becomes alive in us, we love Him and choose to obey Him. Jesus becomes more precious to us as we mature in our Christian life. As our relationship grows, our expectation grows as well. The more we get to know Him, the more we look forward to being in His presence. As our anticipation of seeing Him grows, we try to do all things possible to please Him. Our great eagerness keeps us from becoming weary, thus, “we are saved by hope.”

Is your hope like the one who “climbeth up some other way,” or like, “he that entereth in by the door”? Do you have a basis for your hope or is it an empty hope that has no foundation?

I trust you are growing up “. . . into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ” (Ephesians 4:15).

I hope you might grow just a little more, so your expectation of seeing Christ might grow as well. The testimony of this expectation is, “. . . in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven” (2 Corinthians 5:2).

Ada yang pernah berkata “Ketika harapan hidup, malam terasa kurang gelap, kesendirian kurang dalam, dan ketakutan kurang tajam.” Ketika saya bekerja di sebuah penjara sebagai asisten kapelan, saya duduk bersama para terpidana mati dan mendengarkan ketika mereka berbicara tentang keadaan mereka. Hampir tanpa kecuali, semua berbicara tentang berharap bisa keluar dari penjara suatu hari nanti. Bahkan jika mereka dijatuhi hukuman seumur hidup, mereka tetap berharap bisa keluar.

Saya telah berbicara dengan orang-orang yang tidak mengaku lahir baru, tetapi tetap berharap pergi ke surga. Orang-orang ini tidak berani berhenti berharap. Harapan mereka didasarkan pada pengharapan mereka sendiri! Diet dengan jenis harapan itu jelaslah sangat tipis! Penalaran ini mengingatkan saya pada perkataan Yesus dalam Yohanes 10:1-2 tentang masuk ke kandang domba. “Tetapi barang siapa masuk melalui pintu adalah gembala domba itu.” Orang-orang membangun harapan akan sorga pada banyak hal yang goyah. Beberapa mendasarkan harapan mereka pada baptisan di gereja tertentu. Beberapa berharap karena keanggotaan gereja mereka. Beberapa orang berharap pada perbuatan baik mereka, sementara yang lain berharap pada pengharapan mereka sendiri. Namun Alkitab berkata, “. . . kecuali seseorang dilahirkan kembali, ia tidak dapat melihat kerajaan Allah” (Yohanes 3:3).

Ada harapan yang benar dan harapan yang palsu. Harapan palsu adalah “memanjat dengan jalan lain,” tetapi harapan yang benar adalah “barang siapa masuk melalui pintu.”

“Karena kita diselamatkan oleh pengharapan, tetapi pengharapan yang terlihat bukanlah pengharapan lagi. Sebab: apa yang masih dilihat orang, untuk apa lagi ia berharap?” (Roma 8:24). Kata pengharapan ini berarti “dengan antisipasi atau pengharapan yang besar.” Dapatkah kita mengatakan bahwa kita diselamatkan oleh pengharapan yang besar? Ya, kita dapat. “Janganlah bekerja untuk makanan yang binasa, tetapi untuk makanan yang turun-temurun sampai hidup yang kekal, yang akan diberikan oleh Anak Manusia kepadamu; karena Ia telah mendapat meterai dari Allah Bapa” (Yohanes 6:27). Ini tampak seperti kontradiksi. Bukankah kita diselamatkan oleh kasih karunia? Ya, kita diselamatkan oleh kasih karunia melalui iman (Efesus 2:8). Lalu apakah yang dimaksud dengan diselamatkan oleh pengharapan dan bekerja untuk “makanan yang turun-temurun sampai hidup yang kekal”?

“Mereka berkata kepada-Nya, apakah yang harus kami lakukan, supaya kami melakukan pekerjaan Allah?” Yesus menjawab dan berkata kepada mereka, “Inilah pekerjaan Allah, yaitu kamu percaya kepada Dia yang telah Ia utus” (Yohanes 6:28-29). Hanya oleh kasih karunia kita diselamatkan, tetapi seperti yang ditunjukkan bagian ini, kasih karunia menetapkan suatu syarat. Syarat kasih karunia itu adalah bahwa kita percaya kepada-Nya. Syarat lain dari keselamatan adalah pertobatan (Markus 1:15), sedangkan yang lain lagi adalah memikul salib. “Barangsiapa mau mengikut Aku, ia harus menyangkal dirinya sendiri, memikul salibnya dan mengikut Aku” (Markus 8:34).

Segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan bagi Kristus, baik percaya, bertobat, maupun memikul salib, adalah karena kasih karunia. Apa pun yang kita miliki atau lakukan, adalah karena Dia. Kita tidak bekerja untuk keselamatan kita, sebab Kristus sendiri berkata, “Sudah selesai.” Kita tidak punya apa-apa untuk diharapkan jika kita tidak memenuhi syarat-syarat keselamatan kita. Setelah kita menerima Tuhan Yesus sebagai Juruselamat, maka “pengharapan itu tidak mengecewakan” (Roma 5:5).

Saat Kristus hidup di dalam kita, kita mengasihi-Nya dan memilih untuk taat kepada-Nya. Yesus menjadi lebih berharga bagi kita seiring kita bertumbuh dalam kehidupan Kristen kita. Saat hubungan kita bertumbuh, pengharapan kita juga bertambah. Semakin kita mengenal Dia, semakin kita menantikan berada di hadirat-Nya. Ketika antisipasi kita untuk melihat Dia bertumbuh, kita berusaha melakukan segala sesuatu yang mungkin untuk menyenangkan Dia. Kegairahan besar kita mencegah kita menjadi lelah, sehingga, “kita diselamatkan oleh pengharapan.”

Apakah pengharapanmu seperti orang yang “memanjat dengan jalan lain,” atau seperti “barang siapa masuk melalui pintu”? Apakah kamu memiliki dasar bagi pengharapanmu atau apakah itu pengharapan kosong yang tidak memiliki dasar?

Saya percaya kamu sedang bertumbuh “. . . ke dalam Dia dalam segala sesuatu, yang adalah kepala, yaitu Kristus” (Efesus 4:15).

Saya berharap kamu dapat bertumbuh sedikit lebih lagi, sehingga pengharapanmu untuk melihat Kristus juga bertambah. Kesaksian dari pengharapan ini adalah, “. . . dalam hal ini kami mendesah, dengan rindu menantikan untuk dipakaikan tubuh yang dari sorga” (2 Korintus 5:2).

Iemand het eendag gesê: “Wanneer hoop leef, is die nag minder donker, die eensaamheid minder diep en vrees minder skerp.” Toe ek as assistent-predikant in ’n tronk gewerk het, het ek by die ter dood veroordeelde mans gesit en geluister terwyl hulle van hul benoudheid praat. Byna sonder uitsondering het almal gehoop om eendag uit die tronk te kom. Selfs al het hulle ’n lewenslange vonnis gehad, het hulle gehoop om uit te kom.

Ek het met mense gepraat wat nie bely dat hulle wedergebore is nie, maar toch hoop om hemeltoe te gaan. Hierdie mense durf nie ophou hoop nie. Hul hoop berus op hul eie hoop! ’n Dieet van daardie soort hoop is beslis ’n magertjie! Hierdie redenasie herinner my aan Jesus se woorde in Johannes 10:1–2 oor die ingaan in die skaapkraal. “Maar wie deur die deur inkom, dit is die herder van die skape.” Mense bou hul hoop op die hemel op baie wankelrige dinge. Sommige bou hul hoop op die feit dat hulle in ’n sekere kerk gedoop is. Ander hoop op hul kerklidmaatskap. Sommige mense hoop op hul goeie werke, terwyl ander hoop op hul eie hoop. Die Bybel sê egter: “...as iemand nie van nuuts af gebore word nie, kan hy die koninkryk van God nie sien nie” (Johannes 3:3).

Daar is ’n ware hoop en ’n valse hoop. Die valse hoop is om “op ’n ander manier op te klim,” maar ware hoop is “wie deur die deur inkom.”

“Want ons is gered deur die hoop; maar hoop wat gesien word, is nie hoop nie: want wat iemand sien, waarom hoop hy nog?” (Romeine 8:24). Hierdie woord hoop beteken “met afwagting of groot verwagting.” Kan ons sê dat ons deur groot verwagting gered word? Ja, ons kan. “Werk nie vir die voedsel wat vergaan nie, maar vir dié voedsel wat bly tot die ewige lewe, wat die Seun van die mens julle sal gee; want daartoe het God die Vader Hom versegeld” (Johannes 6:27). Dit lyk asof dit ’n soort teenspraak is. Is ons nie deur genade gered nie? Ja, ons word deur genade deur die geloof gered (Efesiërs 2:8). Wat beteken dit dan om deur hoop gered te word en te swoeg vir die “kos wat bly tot die ewige lewe”?

“Toe sê hulle tot Hom: Wat moet ons dan doen, opdat ons die werke van God mag werksaam? Jesus antwoord en sê tot hulle: Dit is die werk van God, dat julle in Hom glo wat Hy gestuur het” (Johannes 6:28–29). Dit is slegs deur genade dat ons gered word, maar soos hierdie gedeelte aandui, stel genade ’n voorwaarde. Die voorwaarde van genade is dat ons in Hom glo. ’n Ander voorwaarde van die saligheid is bekering (Markus 1:15), terwyl ’n ander is die dra van die kruis. “Wie agter My wil kom, moet homself verloën en sy kruis opneem en My volg” (Markus 8:34).

Alles wat ons vir Christus sou doen — of dit nou glo, bekeer of die kruis dra is — geskied deur genade. Wat ook al ons het of doen, is weens Hom. Ons werk nie vir ons saligheid nie, want Christus self het gesê: “Dit is volbring.” Ons het niks om op te hoop as ons nie aan die voorwaardes van ons saligheid voldoen nie. Sodra ons die Here Jesus as Verlosser ontvang, dan “stel die hoop nie beskaming nie” (Romeine 5:5).

Namate Christus in ons lewendig word, liefhet ons Hom en kies om Hom te gehoorsaam. Jesus word vir ons kosbaarder soos ons in ons christelike lewe volwasse raak. Soos ons verhouding groei, groei ook ons verwagting. Hoe meer ons Hom leer ken, hoe meer sien ons daarna uit om in Sy teenwoordigheid te wees. Namate ons afwagting om Hom te sien groei, probeer ons alles moontlik doen om Hom te behaag. Ons groot ywer weerhou ons daarvan om moeg te word; daarom “is ons gered deur hoop.”

Is jou hoop soos dié van iemand wat “op ’n ander manier opklim,” of soos “wie deur die deur inkom”? Het jy ’n grondslag vir jou hoop of is dit ’n leë hoop sonder fondament?

Ek vertrou dat jy groei “...in alles na Hom toe, wat die Hoof is, Christus” (Efesiërs 4:15).

Ek hoop jy sal net ’n bietjie meer groei, sodat jou verwagting om Christus te sien ook mag groei. Die getuienis van hierdie verwagting is: “...hiervoor sug ons ook, en ons verlange is ernstig om met ons woning wat uit die hemel is beklee te word” (2 Korintiërs 5:2).

Life is like a winding pathway
For the multitude of souls,
Who are briskly walking onward,
Heedless of their final goal.

Life is mostly what we make it,
Straight or crooked, one of twain;
We’ll receive just what we merit—
Our eternal loss or gain.

O dear souls! upon life’s pathway,
Lean upon your Savior’s breast;
There no foe can e’er molest you,
‘Til you reach eternal rest.

Жизнь — как извилистая тропа
Для множества душ,
Что бодро движутся вперёд,
Не ведая о своей конечной цели.

Жизнь во многом — то, что мы из неё делаем,
Прямая или кривая, один из двух путей;
Мы получим ровно то, что заслужили—
Наша вечная потеря или обретение.

О, дорогие души! на пути жизни,
Прилегите к груди вашего Спасителя;
Там никакой враг не сможет тревожить вас,
Пока вы не достигнете вечного покоя.

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

یہ وہ مشہورانہ "کامل دنیا" تھی جو آدم اور حوا روزانہ اپنے خالق کے ساتھ لطف اندوز ہوتے تھے۔ خوبصورت باغ، جسے خود خدا نے ڈیزائن، پیدا اور ہاتھوں سے لگایا تھا، ہر لحاظ سے کامل تھا۔ ہم سب جانتے ہیں کہ یہ صورت حال زیادہ دیر برقرار نہ رہی۔ خدا نے تمام انسانیت کو اختیار دینے کا استحقاق عطا کیا، اسی لئے اُن دونوں نے جلد ہی غلط انتخاب کیا۔ حوا، اگرچہ ناگ کی صورت میں شیطان کے فریب میں آئیں، جھوٹ پر ایمان لے آئیں اور خدا کی نافرمانی کرنے کا انتخاب کیا — وہی ایک کام جو خدا نے محبت سے اُن سے نہ کرنے کو کہا تھا۔ لیکن جب اس نے پھل آدم کو دیا تو آدم دھوکہ نہیں کھا بیٹھا۔ وہ جانتا تھا کہ یہ غلط ہے۔ خدا حیران نہ ہوا مگر بےشک بہت مایوس ہوا۔ پیدائش کی کتاب باب 3 میں ہم انسانیت کے باغ سے نکالے جانے، درختِ حیات سے دور کیے جانے، اور آدم و حوا کے گناہ کے سبب لعنت کے اعلان کا افسردہ واقعہ پڑھتے ہیں۔ سب کچھ بہت تاریک اور بےامید محسوس ہوا۔ اگرچہ گناہ کرنے والا صرف ایک آدمی تھا، مگر لعنت ساری مخلوق پر منتقل ہو گئی، بشمول زمین، پودوں اور جانوروں کے۔ آئیے میرے ساتھ غور کریں کہ اس عظیم لعنت کے ساتھ کیا کچھ آیا۔

  1. بیماری
  2. مصیبت اور درد
  3. زوال اور تباہی
  4. کچھ پودوں جیسے کانٹے اور چھریلے پودوں کا غلبہ
  5. موت
  6. اپخوری اور بوسیدگی

ہم آج انہیں لعنت کے چھ “د” کے نام سے پکارتے ہیں۔

بیماری

دنیا کے ازلی، دائمی اور کامل صحت کے دن گزر چکے تھے۔ بیماری گناہ کی لعنت کے حصے کے طور پر منظرِ عام پر آگئی۔ انسان کے بچے، پرندے، جانور اور پودے سب بیماریوں کے اثرات محسوس کرنے لگے۔ مگر خدا وفادار تھا اور ایسی ہدایات فراہم کیں جن سے انسان کو بہت سی روکی جانے والی بیماریوں سے صفائی اور سادہ اطاعت کے ذریعے بچنے کا طریقہ معلوم ہوا۔ مثال کے طور پر، شادی میں اس کے اصل ارادے کا احترام کرنے، پاکیزگی برقرار رکھنے، متعدد ممکنہ بیماریوں سے بچنے وغیرہ کا حکم۔ وہ ہماری روحانی حالت میں بھی دلچسپی رکھتے تھے۔ خدا نے کبھی انسان کو جرم اٹھانے کےلیے پیدا نہیں کیا۔ وہ چاہتا ہے کہ ہمارا ضمیر صاف رہے کیونکہ وہ جانتا ہے کہ مجرم ضمیر تمہیں بیمار کر سکتا ہے!

ان میں سے بعض بیماریوں سے بچنا ممکن نہ ہوگا، مگر بہت سی بیماریوں کو قوتِ مدافعت بنا کر روکا جا سکتا ہے۔ خدا نے لوگوں، پودوں اور جانوروں کو ایک تولیدی مائیکرو بایوم (اربوں مفید بیکٹیریا) اور ایک نظامِ مدافعت کے ساتھ بنا کر بھی وفاداری دکھائی، جو بیماریوں سے لڑنے میں ہماری مدد کرتا ہے۔ یہ حیرت انگیز ہے کہ ہر پودا بظاہر غذائی یا علاجی خصوصیات رکھتا ہے جو فائدہ مند ہیں۔ کیا خالق کتنا وفادار ہے!

مصیبت اور درد

میرا خیال ہے کہ جنت میں کسی اصلی وجہ کے بغیر درد کا وجود نہیں تھا، مگر ان کے نکلنے کے دن سے ہم درد محسوس کر رہے ہیں۔ درد بلاشبہ ہماری زندگیوں کا ایک حصہ ہے۔ درد کی بہت سی اقسام ہیں۔ رنج، غم اور ترک کیا جانا وہ تمام جذباتی درد ہیں جو لعنت کے ساتھ آتے ہیں۔ دردِ جسم، سر درد، دکھتی ہوئی عضلات، ٹوٹے ہوئے رباط، متاثرہ کنڈرا، گھسنے والے جوڑ، اور ٹوٹے ہوئے ہڈی چند جسمانی درد ہیں جن کا ہم اپنی زندگی میں کبھی نہ کبھی سامنا کر سکتے ہیں۔ ایک بار پھر، خدا نے انسانیت کو زندگی کے کچھ دردوں اور مصیبتوں کو دور کرنے کا طریقہ سمجھانے میں وفاداری دکھائی ہے۔ قدیم زمانے سے پودے، جڑی بوٹیاں اور دیگر علاج معالجے کے ذرائع لوگوں کو درد اور مصیبت سے نجات دلانے میں مدد دیتے رہے ہیں۔ آج بھی ہمارے پاس کئی مفید پودے ہیں جو درد میں ہماری مدد کرتے ہیں۔

زمین پر تجربہ کیے جانے والی سب سے خوبصورت چیزوں میں سے ایک بچے کی پیدائش ہے۔ پھر بھی پیدائش عموماً زیادہ درد کے ساتھ ہوتی ہے۔ اگرچہ ہم اس وعدہ شدہ درد کو ختم نہیں کر سکتے، خدا نے وفاداری دکھائی ہے کہ پیدائش سے پہلے، دوران اور بعد میں درد کو کم اور صحت یابی کو تیز کرنے کے لیے بہت سی جڑی بوٹیوں کے استعمال کا ہمیں علم دیا۔ اسے ہمارے لیے ایسا کرنے کی ضرورت نہیں تھی۔ انسان واقعی رحم کا مستحق نہیں تھا۔ کتنا وفادار خالق ہے!

زوال اور تباہی

ہمیں اس اصول کو دیکھنے کے لیے تاریخ کا زیادہ مطالعہ کرنے کی ضرورت نہیں ہے۔ ہوا، بارش اور سورج بہت سی چیزوں پر زوال آور اثر رکھتے ہیں۔ چاہے ہم خشک ہو گئی ندی کی کناری، دریا کی تہہ میں مادّہ کھردرا ہو کر چمک گیا ہوا پتھر، یا ہوا سے گِر گیا درخت سمجھیں، یہ سب قدرتی عناصرِ تباہی ہیں۔ مگر اس کے ساتھ وہ جو انسان نے پودوں، جانوروں، مٹی اور ایک دوسرے کے ساتھ کیا، اسے بھی شامل کریں۔ خوفناک جنگوں میں ہونے والی تباہ کاریوں یا امن کے دوران خودغرض اور لالچی عمل کے نتیجے میں، انسان انتہائی تباہ کن مخلوق ہے۔ خدا نے انسانیت کو ساری مخلوق پر اختیار دے رکھا تھا۔ تاہم ہم اکثر اس کا غلط مطلب اخذ کر لیتے ہیں کہ ہم زمین کے مالک ہیں اور اس کے ساتھ جو چاہیں کر سکتے ہیں۔ جس نے اعلان کیا کہ "زمین خداوند کی ہے"، اُس کا یہ خیال نہیں کہ مرد مخلوقِ خدا کے امینوں کے علاوہ کچھ ہیں۔ مخلوق یا اس میں موجود کسی چیز کی پوجا کرنا واقعی بدی ہے۔ مگر ہمارے خالق کی مخلوق کے ساتھ ناشکری اور غفلت برتنا بھی اتنا ہی بدی ہے! بہرحال، خدا نے اس لعنت کے درمیان اپنی زمین کو پیدا کرنے میں تجدیدی صلاحیتیں وفاداری کے ساتھ رکھی ہیں۔ ہمارے رحم دل بنانے والے کو برکت دے!

کانٹوں اور چھریلے پودوں کا غلبہ

جس نے کبھی بھی باغبانی کی ہے وہ جلد ہی گھاس پھوس کے ساتھ جدوجہد کی حقیقت جان جاتا ہے۔ منصفانہ طور پر، جہاں بھی کوئی پودا وہیں جہاں اس کی خواہش نہ ہو، اسے "گھاس پھوس" کہا جاتا ہے۔ بہت سی گھاس پھوس اگر ہمیں معلوم ہو کہ انہیں کس کام کے لیے استعمال کرنا ہے تو بہت فائدہ مند پودے ہو سکتے ہیں۔ جن پودوں کو ہم گھاس پھوس کہتے ہیں، اُن میں سے بعض واقعی کافی غذائیت بخش اور صحت مند ہوتے ہیں بشرطیکہ ہم جان لیں کہ کون سے کھانے کے لائق ہیں اور انہیں کیسے تیار کرنا ہے۔ آج ہم کانٹوں اور چھریلے پودوں کے بارے میں سوچنا چاہتے ہیں۔ ہمیں یہ مان لینا چاہیے کہ وہ پہلے چھ دنوں میں پیدا کیے گئے تھے، نہ کہ لعنت کے اعلان کے بعد۔ ایسا معلوم ہوتا ہے کہ لعنت کے بعد ان کی قابلِ استعمال فصلوں پر فوقیت حاصل کرنے کی صلاحیت بڑھی۔ اسی لعنت کے حصے میں بھی ہم خدا کی رحمت کو دیکھتے ہیں کہ اس نے ہمارے لیے انتظام کیا۔

ہم اٹریکاچوک کو اس کے تلخ پتوں کے لئے اگاتے ہیں، جو ہاضمے کے لئے تلخ مشروبات بنانے میں استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ سوچئے: بلیسڈ تھیسل، ملک تھیسل، ٹیزل، رسبیری کے پتے، اور بلیک بیری کی جڑیں ان "کانٹیلے گھاس پھوس" کے ایسے چند مثالیں ہیں جو طبی اور دیگر غذائی فوائد کے لئے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ لعنت کے بیچ میں بھی ہمیں فائدے دینا خدا کتنا اچھا ہے!

موت

یہ وہ ایک "د" ہے جس کے بارے میں ہم میں سے زیادہ تر لوگ بات کرنا پسند نہیں کرتے۔ حقیقت میں، جب ہم اپنی پہلی سانس لیتے ہیں، ہم موت کے ایک سانس قریب تر ہوتے ہیں۔ اگرچہ تمام پودے، جانور اور انسان آخرکار مر جائیں گے، پھر بھی ہم اس کے ساتھ راحت محسوس نہیں کرتے۔ زندہ رہنے کی ایک فطری خواہش ہمارے اندر موجود ہے، اور اگر یہ نہ ہو تو ہمیں اس کی وجہ معلوم کرنے میں مدد لینا چاہیے۔
