Ilikuwa ni ulimwengu uliookoleza “kikaboni” ambao Adamu na Hawa walifurahia kila siku pamoja na Muumba wao. Bustani nzuri, iliyotengenezwa, kuumbwa, na kupandwa kwa mikono na Mungu Mwenyewe, ilikuwa kamilifu kwa kila upande. Sote tunajua kwamba haikuendelea hivyo kwa muda mrefu. Kwa sababu ya haki ya uchaguzi ambayo Mungu aliwapa wanadamu wote, wote wawili hivi karibuni walifanya uchaguzi mbaya. Hawa, ingawa alidanganywa na Shetani katika sura ya nyoka, alimwamini uongo na akachagua kumkana Mungu, akifanya jambo pekee ambalo Mungu kwa upendo alimwomba aselifanye. Lakini alipoleta tunda kwa Adamu, yeye hakudanganywa. Alijua ilikuwa kosa. Mungu hakushangazwa lakini, kwa vile hivyo, alihuzunika sana. Katika Mwanzo 3, tunasoma tamko la kusikitisha la wanadamu wakitupwa nje ya bustani, wakizuia kupata mti wa uzima wa milele, na laana ilitangazwa kwa sababu ya dhambi ya Adamu na Hawa. Ilionekana giza na kutokuwa na tumaini. Ingawa ni mtu mmoja tu aliyekosea, laana ilipita kwa ulimwengu wote ulioumbwa, pamoja na dunia, mimea, na wanyama. Fikiria tu pamoja nami kile kilichokuja pamoja na laana hii kuu.

  1. Magonjwa
  2. Dhiki na Maumivu
  3. Kushindwa na uharibifu
  4. Utegemeo wa mimea fulani kama vishawishi na vidonge
  5. Kifo
  6. Uozo na Mcholongo

Tutawataja leo kama “D” sita za laana.

Magonjwa

Siku za ulimwengu zenye afya ya milele na kamilifu zilipita. Ugonjwa uliingia kama sehemu ya laana ya dhambi. Watoto wa mwanadamu, ndege, wanyama, na mimea wote wangeanza kuhisi athari za ugonjwa na maradhi. Lakini Mungu alikua mwaminifu kwa kutoa maagizo ambayo yaliwasaidia wanadamu kujua jinsi ya kuepuka magonjwa mengi yanayoweza kuzuilika kwa usafi na utiifu rahisi. Kwa mfano, amri ya Mungu kuheshimu nia yake ya awali katika ndoa, kudumisha uzuri wa maisha, kuepuka maradhi mengi yatokanayo na tabia mbalimbali, n.k. Alikuwa pia na maslahi kwa hali yetu ya kiroho. Mungu hakutaka wanadamu kubeba hatia. Anataka tuyapate na kuyahifadhi miito yetu wazi kwa kuwa anajua kwamba dhamira iliyo na hatia inaweza kukufanya ugonjwa!

Kumekuwa na baadhi ya magonjwa ambayo hayangeepukika, lakini mengi yangeweza kuzuilika kwa kujenga kinga ya mwili. Mungu pia alikua mwaminifu katika kubuni watu, mimea, na wanyama kwa microbiome ya kujiendeleza (mabilioni ya bakteria zenye manufaa) na mfumo wa kinga wa mwili, ambao hutusaidia kupambana na magonjwa. Inashangaza jinsi kila mmea unaonekana kuwa na mali za lishe au za uponyaji ambazo ni za manufaa. Muumba Mwaminifu kiasi gani!

Dhiki na Maumivu

Nadhani hakuna sababu ya kweli ya maumivu katika Bustani ya Edeni, lakini tumekuwa tukipata maumivu tangu siku walipotoka. Maumivu ni sehemu ya maisha ya wengi wetu. Kuna aina nyingi za maumivu. Kuhuzunika, majonzi, na kukataliwa ni maumivu ya hisia yanayoambatana na laana. Maumivu ya mwili kama maumivu ya misuli, kupiga kichwa, misuli iliyoumia, vifundo vilivyovunjika, tendoni zilizoambukizwa, viungo vilivyovunjika, na mifupa iliyovunjika ni baadhi ya maumivu ya kimwili ambayo tunaweza kuyapata kabla ya pumzi yetu ya mwisho. Tena, Mungu amekuwa mwaminifu katika kuwasaidia wanadamu kuelewa nini cha kufanya ili kupunguza baadhi ya maumivu na dhiki za maisha. Tangu nyakati za kale, mimea, nyanya, na tiba nyingine zimewasaidia watu kushughulikia maumivu na dhiki. Hadi leo, tuna mimea mingi yenye manufaa zinazotusaidia kwa maumivu.

Mmoja wa mambo mazuri kabisa yanaweza kutokea duniani ni kuzaliwa kwa mtoto. Hata hivyo, ujauzito kwa ujumla huambatana na maumivu mengi. Ingawa hatuwezi kuondoa maumivu haya yaliyoahidiwa, Mungu amekuwa mwaminifu kwa kututoa na kutufunulia matumizi ya mimea mingi kabla, wakati, na baada ya uzazi ili kupunguza maumivu na kuharakisha urejeshaji. Hakulazimika kututendea hivyo. Mwanadamu kwa kweli hadhiri huruma. Muumba Mwaminifu kiasi gani!

Kushindwa na uharibifu

Hatuhitaji kusoma historia kwa muda mrefu kuona kanuni hii ikiendelea kufanya kazi. Upepo, mvua, na jua vyote vina athari za kuoza kwa vitu vingi. Iwe tunazingatia benki iliyochongwa na maji, miamba iliyovongwa katika mto, au mti ulioanguka na upepo, hizi ni sehemu zote za asili za uharibifu. Lakini ongeza kile ambacho mwanadamu amefanya kwa mimea, wanyama, udongo, na kwa kila mmoja wetu. Iwe ni athari mbaya za uharibifu katika vita vya kutisha au tabia za kujitakia na za tamaa wakati wa amani, mwanadamu ni kiumbe hatari wa uharibifu. Mungu alikwamua wanadamu uweza juu ya uumbaji wote. Hata hivyo, mara nyingi sana, tunatafsiri kwa uongo kwamba tunamiliki nyanja hii iitwayo dunia na tunaweza kufanya chochote tunachotaka nayo. Yeye aliyeitangaza, “Dunia ni ya Bwana,” hayakubaliani na wazo kwamba watu ni kitu zaidi ya watunza wa uumbaji wa Mungu. Ni uovu kabisa kumwabudu ulimwengu ulioumbwa au chochote kilicho ndani yake. Lakini ni uovu pia kutokuwa na shukrani na kuwa mpumbavu kwa uumbaji wa Muumba wetu! Hata hivyo, Mungu amebuni dunia Yake kwa uwezo wa kujirejesha katikati ya laana hii. Barikiwa Muumba wetu mwema!

Utegemeo wa Vishawi na Vidonge

Kila mtu aliyejaribu kulima bustani mara moja atagundua vita na magugu. Kwa haki, mmea wowote unaokua mahali hauhitajwi ni “magugu.” Magugu mengi yanaweza kuwa mimea yenye manufaa sana ikiwa tu tunajua ya kutumika kwa nini. Baadhi ya mimea tunayoita magugu kwa kweli ni yenye lishe na afya mara tu tukiuelewa ni ipi inayoweza kuliwa na jinsi ya kuipika. Leo, tunataka kufikiria kuhusu vishawi na vidonge. Tunapaswa kudhani waliumbwa siku sita za kwanza, si baada ya laana kutangazwa. Inaonekana uwezo wao wa kuzidi mazao yenye manufaa uliongezeka baada ya laana. Hata katika sehemu hii ya laana, tunaona Mungu akitupatia kwa rehema.

Tunakua artichoke kwa ajili ya majani yake yenye uchungu, ambayo hutumika kutengeneza vilainishi vya mmeng'enyo. Fikiria: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Majani ya Rasiberi, na mizizi ya Blackberry ni baadhi tu ya mifano ya wanachama wa “magugu yenye misho” yanayotumika kwa tiba na faida za chakula. Ni wema gani wa Mungu kutupa manufaa katikati ya laana yenyewe!

Kifo

Huu ndiye “D” mmoja ambao wengi wetu wangependelea kusitokelezea. Kwa kweli, tukipumua kwanza, tumejipatia pumzi moja karibu zaidi na kifo. Ingawa mimea yote, wanyama, na watu hatimaye wataaga dunia, bado hatutafurahia kuzungumzia hilo. Ni kawaida kwetu kuwa na tamaa ya kuishi, na kama hatuna, tunapaswa kutafuta msaada ili kugundua sababu.

Kifo hakina umri. Katika maisha yangu, nimewasaidia kuchukua mazishi watoto walionekana kufa wanapozaliwa, watu wenye umri wa miaka 96, na kila umri kati yao. Tuna soma kuhusu bustani nzuri iliyorejeshwa, iliyoonyeshwa na Mtume Yohana katika Ufunuo, alipokuwa akielezea Mbingu. Baadhi ya mambo anayotaja ni kuto kuwa na ugonjwa, hakuna huzuni, hakuna uamuzi wa kutenganishwa, hakuna machozi, hakuna mateso tena, na hakuna kifo. Kwa namna fulani, maisha ni kipindi cha mimba kwa ajili ya milele. Hatuwezi kukaa hapa, kama vile mtoto tumboni hawezi kuamua kwamba hataki kuingia katika ulimwengu halisi. Kwa huzuni zetu zote na majaribu, miili yetu huvunjika na kuoza. Kwa unyama, dhambi, na uovu unaotuzunguka, je, kweli tungependa kukaa hapa katika hali hii milele? Badala yake, turudi kwenye udongo tuliotengenezwa kutoka, majivu kwa majivu na vumbi kwa vumbi, tukisubiri ufufuo wa mwisho. Je, si rehema ya Mungu mwaminifu kutomruhusu mtu mwenye dhambi kula mti wa uzima akiwa katika hali yake ya mwenye dhambi, akianguka na kufa? Tunaweza kuona na kuwa na shukrani kwa uaminifu wa Mungu katika kutupatia kifo cha kimwili?

Katikati ya laana iliyotolewa kwa Hawa, unabashiri wa kwanza wa Masiya unafunuliwa. “Na nitavuna chuki kati yako na mke, na kati ya mbegu yako na mbegu yake; yeye atakupiga kichwa, nawe utakampa ugomvi kwenye pete” (Mwanzo 3:15). Yeye ndiye mshindi wa kifo! Msifiwe Mungu kwa Uaminifu Wake.

Uozo na Mcholongo

Uozo na mcholongo ni “D” nyingine ya laana. Korosho inang'uka chini, na mbegu huanza kuibuka hivi karibuni. Kwa miaka michache itakuwa mchanga mdogo. Miaka hupita, na nyani hukusanya korosho zinazang'uka kila vuli. Kisha kama mkomamko mkubwa hupata virusi, inakufa, na katika miaka michache huvunjwa kwa upepo. Hapa, inarejea kwenye udongo inapooza na kuoza. Tangu laana, kila kitu huchakaa na kuoza. Ukizingatia mimea, wanyama, na watu wengi waliokufa katika miaka 6,000 iliyopita, je, si wema wa Mungu kuwa amebuni uozo na mcholongo? Dunia ingekuwa imeonekana vipi kama mabaki yote ya miaka 6,000 yangekuwa bado yakielea? Dunia ingekuwa imefunikwa na miti iliyokufa na mayatima! Hii inaweza kuwa ngumu kuelewa, lakini Mungu alibuni falme nzima katika uumbaji hasa kwa ajili ya kutekeleza hili kabla hata haijalihitajika kwa sababu alitabiri hitaji hilo. Falme za chachu, ukungu, na uutu, falme za bakteria, viini vya kimetaboliki, na maisha madogo ya mimea na wanyama yote husaidia kuvunja nyuzi za maisha na kuifanya kuwa mbolea kamili kwa kukamilisha mzunguko wa uzima na kutoa chakula kwa kizazi kijacho. Udongo wenye afya wa kikaboni una takriban mabilioni 8 ya vimelea vya udongo kwenye kijiko kimoja tu. Hii ni sababu nyingine kwa nini ni muhimu kutendea udongo heshima, si kemikali kali.

Je, umewahi kufikiria juu ya maji makubwa ya Gadi ya Nuhu? Fikiria mizunguko ya mamilioni ya tani za mimea, wanyama, na vitu vya binadamu zikizunguka kabla hatimaye kujifunga chini na haraka kufunikwa kwa sedimenti wakati maji yaliposhuka. Hili liliunda mazingira bora ya kutengeneza makaa ya mawe na mafuta mengine ya kaboni tunayoyatumia leo. Kulikuwa pale, ndani ya udongo, hadi siku ilipogunduliwa. Hadi leo, bado yanatumika.

Tuwe watunzaji waaminifu na wenye jukumu wa dunia ya Bwana!

“Maana matarajio ya uumbaji yote yanangojea kufunuliwa kwa wana wa Mungu. Kwa kuwa uumbaji uliwekwa chini ya uharibifu, si kwa hiari, bali kwa iliyeuweka chini, kwa hiyo uwepo wa matumaini. Kwa maana uumbaji pia utakombolewa kutoka kwenye utumwa wa kuharibika, na kuingia katika uhuru wa utukufu wa wana wa Mungu. Kwa kuwa tunajua kwamba uumbaji wote unalia na unaumwa pamoja hadi sasa. Na si wao tu, bali nasi wenyewe, ambao tumepata mavuno ya kwanza ya Roho, hata sisi tunalia ndani yetu, tukisubiri umwachiliwe, yaani, ukombozi wa miili yetu” (Warumi 8:19-23).

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

Dit was die spreekwoordelike “perfekte wêreld” wat Adam en Eva daagliks saam met hul Skepper geniet het. Die pragtige tuin, ontwerp, geskep en met die hand geplant deur God self, was in elke opsig volmaak. Ons weet almal dat dit nie vir lank so gebly het nie. As gevolg van die keusevoorreg wat God aan die mensdom gegee het, het hulle albei gou die verkeerde keuse gemaak. Eva, alhoewel deur Satan in die gedaante van die slang mislei, het die leuen geglo en gekies om God te ongehoorsaam — die enigste ding wat God liefdevol aan haar gevra het om nie te doen nie. Maar toe sy die vrug aan Adam bring, was hy nie mislei nie. Hy het geweet dit was verkeerd. God was nie verras nie, maar tog baie teleurgesteld. In Genesis 3 lees ons die hartseer verslag van die mensdom wat uit die tuin verdryf is, van die boom van die ewige lewe uitgesluit is en die vloek uitgespreek is as gevolg van Adam en Eva se sonde. Dit het so donker en hopeloos gelyk. Alhoewel dit net een man was wat gesondig het, het die vloek na die hele geskape wêreld oorgedra, insluitend die aarde, plante en diere. Dink saam met my oor wat alles saam met hierdie magtige vloek gekom het.

  1. Siekte
  2. Angs en Pyn
  3. Aftakeling en vernietiging
  4. Oordomsyn van sekere plante soos dorings en distels
  5. Dood
  6. Ontbinding en bederf

Ons sal hulle vandag na verwys as die ses “D’e” van die vloek.

Siekte

Die wêreld se ongerepte dae van ewige, volmaakte gesondheid was verby. Siekte het as deel van die sondevloek in die prentjie gekom. Die kinders van die mense, die voëls, die diere en die plante sou almal die gevolge van siekte en ongesteldheid begin ervaar. Maar God was getrou deur instruksies te verskaf wat die mens help om te weet hoe om baie voorkombare siektes deur netheid en eenvoudige gehoorsaamheid te vermy. Byvoorbeeld, God se opdrag om sy oorspronklike bedoeling in die huwelik te eer, reinheid te handhaaf, verskeie moontlike siektes te vermy, ensovoorts. Hy was ook in ons geestelike toestand belangstelend. God het die mensdom nooit ontwerp om skuld te dra nie. Hy wil hê ons moet ons gewete skoon hê omdat Hy weet dat ’n skuldig gewete jou siek kan maak!

Sommige van hierdie siektes sou onvermydelik wees, maar baie kon verhoed word deur immuniteit op te bou. God was ook getrou om mense, plante en diere te ontwerp met ’n regeneratiewe mikrobiome (miljarde nuttige bakterieë) en ’n sistemiese immuunstelsel, wat ons help om siektes af te weer. Dit is verbasend hoe elke plant blykbaar sekere dieet- of genesingseienskappe het wat voordelig is. Hoe getrou is ons Skepper nie!

Angs en Pyn

Ek vermoed daar was geen regte rede vir pyn in die Tuin van Eden nie, maar ons het pyn ervaar sedert die dag van hul uittog. Pyn is inderdaad deel van baie van ons lewens. Daar is baie tipes pyn. Rou, bedroefheid en afwysing is almal emosionele pyn wat met die vloek kom. Pyn, migraine, seer spiere, geskeurde ligament, geïnfekteerde senings, verslete gewrigte en gebreekte bene is ’n paar van die fisiese pyn wat ons eendag voor ons laaste asem kan ervaar. Weereens het God getrou behulp gespring om die mensdom te laat verstaan wat om te doen om sommige van die pyn en angs van die lewe te verlig. Van antieke tye af het plante, kruie en ander middels mense gehelp om met pyn en angs te handel. Tot vandag toe het ons baie nuttige plante wat ons met pyn help.

Een van die mooiste dinge wat op aarde ervaar kan word, is die geboorte van ’n kind. Tog gaan geboorte gewoonlik gepaard met baie pyn. Alhoewel ons hierdie beloofde pyn nie kan uitskakel nie, was God getrou om vir ons die gebruik van baie kruie voor, tydens en na geboorte te voorsien en onthul om die pyn te verlig en die herstel te bespoedig. Hy moes dit nie vir ons doen nie. Die mensdom verdien regtig geen barmhartigheid nie. Wat ’n getroue Skepper!

Aftakeling en vernietiging

Ons hoef nie baie geskiedenis te bestudeer om hierdie beginsel in werking te sien nie. Wind, reën en son het almal aftakelende effekte op baie dinge. Of ons nou ’n geërodeerde stroomoewer, die rotse wat gladgeslyp is in die rivierbed, of die boom wat deur die wind omgewaai is oorweeg, dit is alles natuurlike elemente van vernietiging. Maar voeg daartoe wat die mens aan die plante, diere, die grond en mekaar gedoen het. Of dit nou die verwoestende gevolge van vernietiging tydens die afgryslike oorloge is of selfsugtige en gierige praktyke gedurende vrede — die mens is ’n baie vernietigende skepsel. God het die mens oor alle skepping heerskappy gegee. Te dikwels interpreteer ons dit egter verkeerdlik asof ons hierdie sfeer wat aarde genoem word besit en daarmee mag doen wat ons wil. Hy wat verklaar het: “Die aarde behoort aan die Here,” stem nie saam met die idee dat mense iets anders as bestuurders van God se skepping is nie. Dit is inderdaad goddeloos om die geskape wêreld of enigiets daarin te aanbid. Maar dit is ewe goddeloos om ondankbaar en onverskillig met ons Skepper se skepping te wees! Nietemin het God getrou sy aarde met regenererende vermoëns ontwerp te midde van hierdie vloek. Geseënd sy genadige Maker!

Oordomsyn van dorings en distels

Enigeen wat al tuingemaak het, het gou die werklikheid van die stryd met onkruid ervaar. In alle regverdigheid is enige plant wat groei waar dit nie gewen word nie, ’n “onkruid.” Baie onkruide kan baie nuttige plante wees as ons net weet waarvoor om hulle te gebruik. Sommige van die plante wat ons onkruid noem, is eintlik baie voedsaam en gesond sodra ons verstaan watter een eetbaar is en hoe om dit voor te berei. Vandag wil ons dink oor dorings en distels. Ons moet aanvaar dat hulle in die eerste ses dae geskep is, nie nádat die vloek uitgespreek is nie. Dit lyk asof hul vermoë om die nuttige gewasse te oorgroei ná die vloek toegeneem het. Selfs in hierdie deel van die vloek sien ons God barmhartig vir ons voorsien.

Ons kweek die artisjok vir sy bitter blare, wat gebruik word om spysverteringsbittere te maak. Denk daaroor: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, framboseblare en swartbessiewortels is net ’n paar voorbeelde van lede van hierdie “doringagtige onkruide” wat vir medisinale en ander voedselvoordele gebruik word. Hoe goed van God om ons voordele te gee te midde van die very vloek!

Dood

Dit is die een “D” waaroor die meeste van ons liewer nie wil praat nie. In werklikheid, wanneer ons ons eerste asem neem, is ons een asem nader aan die dood. Alhoewel alle plante, diere en mense eendag sal sterf, voel ons dit steeds ongemaklik om daaroor te praat. Dit is heel normaal dat ons ’n wil om te lewe het, en as ons dit nie het nie, moet ons hulp soek om uit te vind waarom.

Inderdaad het die dood geen ouderdom nie. In my leeftyd het ek gehelp om doodgeborene te begrawe, mense so oud as 96 jaar oud, en elke ouderdom daartussenin. Ons lees van die pragtige paradys wat herstel is, gesien deur die Apostel Johannes in Openbaring, soos hy die Hemel beskryf. Sommige van die dinge wat hy noem is geen siekte, geen hartseer, geen skeiding, geen trane, geen verdere lyding en geen dood nie. Op ’n manier is die lewe net ’n draoefening vir die ewigheid. Ons kan nie hier bly nie, net soos die baba in die baarmoeder nie kan besluit dat dit nie die werklike wêreld wil betree nie. Met al ons hartseerste en versoekings dra ons liggame uit en vergaan. Met al die geweld, sonde en goddeloosheid om ons, sou ons regtig vir altyd in hierdie toestand hier wou bly? Eerder keer ons terug na die grond waarvan ons gemaak is — as as tot as en stof tot stof — in afwagting van die finale opstanding. Was dit nie genadig van ons getroue God om die sondige mens te weerhou om van die boom van die lewe te eet in sy huidige sondige, sterflike toestand nie? Kan ons God se getrouheid sien en dankbaar wees vir die voorsiening van fisiese dood?

Te midde van die vloek wat aan Eva gegee is, word die eerste profesie van die Messias geopenbaar. “En Ek sal vyandskap stel tussen jou en die vrou, en tussen jou saad en haar saad; dit sal sy hoof verpletter, en jy sal sy hakskeen verpletter” (Genesis 3:15). Hy is die oorwinnaar van die dood! Lof aan God vir Sy Getrouheid.

Ontbinding en bederf

Ontbinding en bederf is nog ’n “D” van die vloek. ’n Neut val op die grond, en gou verskyn ’n spruit. In ’n paar jaar sal dit ’n klein saailing wees. Jare verby, en eekhorings versamel die eikels wat elke herfs op die grond val. Dan, as ’n magtige eikeboom, vang dit ’n virus, sterf dit, en in ’n paar jaar bring ’n windstorm dit ter aarde. Hier keer dit terug na die grond terwyl dit ontbind en vergaan. Sedert die vloek verrot en vergaan alles. Gegewe al die plante, diere en mense wat in die laaste 6 000 jaar gesterf het, is dit nie goed van God om ontbinding en bederf ontwerp te hê nie? Hoe sou hierdie wêreld gelyk het as al die rommel van 6 000 jaar nog oral geleë was? Die aarde sou bedek wees met dooie bome en lappe! Dit mag moeilik wees om te besef, maar God het hele koninkryke in die skepping ontwerp net om dit te bewerkstellig voordat dit selfs nodig was omdat Hy die behoefte voorsien het. Die koninkryke van gis, skimmel en fungus, die koninkryke van bakterieë, ensieme, en microskopiese plant- en dierelewe help almal om die vesel van die lewe af te breek en dit in die perfekte kunsmis te maak vir die voltooiing van die lewensiklus en voorsiening vir die volgende generasie. Gesonde organiese grond het ongeveer 8 miljard grondmikrobes in ’n enkele teelepel. Dit is nog ’n rede hoekom dit so belangrik is om die grond met respek te behandel, nie met harde chemikalieë nie.

Het jy al ooit oor die groot vloed van Noag gedink? Stel jou die miljoene ton plant-, dier- en menslike materiaal voor wat rondgedryf het voordat dit uiteindelik op die bodem neergesit en vinnig in sedimente begrawe is toe die waters terugtrek. Dit het die ideale toestande geskep om steenkool en ander fossielbrandstowwe wat ons vandag gebruik, te vorm. Daar was dit, diep binne die aarde, totdat die dag dit ontdek is. Tot vandag toe word dit nog gebruik.

Mag ons verantwoordelike en getroue rentmeesters van die Here se aarde wees!

“Want die gansche schepsel sęg met lang geduld en verwachting der kinderen Gods’ openbaring; want die schepsel is onderworpen aan die ijdelheid, niet met eigen wil, maer door die wil van Hem, die het onderworpen heeft, in hope; want ook het schepsel zelf zal bevrijd worden van de dienstbaarheid der verderving tot der vrijheid der heerlijkheid der kinderen Gods. Want wij weten, dat het ganse schepsel noch alleen, maar ook wij, die de eerstelinge der Geest hebben, zuchten in onszelve en acuut verlangen de aangenome zynis, dat is, de verlossing van ons ligchaam.” (Romeine 8:19-23).

Greetings in the worthy name of the Lord Jesus Christ. As I gaze out across the barren January landscape, I can’t help but wonder what this new year will bring. Undoubtedly, it will bring a mixture of joy and sorrow, excitement and drear, laughter and tears, and everything else in between, which only an Almighty Creator God can arrange in such a way that will magnify His worthy power and excellence. Yet our finite, negative minds tend to anticipate all the bad things that could happen. Will inflation drive food prices even higher? Will widespread fighting erupt across the Middle East? What will happen in the elections? Will the losing party resort to protests and rioting?

I suppose, since the fall of man, these fear-driven thoughts have roamed through the minds of humanity at the beginning of each year. Yet, as it is so aptly pointed out by the writer of the article, “God’s Faithfulness Manifest Even in the Curse”, God has kindly provided for humanity since the beginning of time. Looking back at God’s faithfulness to man over the centuries, we have no reason to doubt God will do the same for us in 2024.

Despite God’s faithfulness to us, the effects of the fall of man are still evident. Family members get sick, church and relationship struggles rob us of sleep, the checkbook runs dry, the children squabble and cry, and the demands of our schedules have us hopping from one event to the next. And sometimes, it seems that all these calamities hit us at the same time. Our bodies and minds are not created to handle this. We become weary. Bone tired. Exhausted to the point when even thinking hurts. We face burnout. In this issue, “A Word From the Doctor” guides us as we face the maze of life, giving us practical and Biblical solutions to avoid or recover from burnout. He writes, “Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.”

Perhaps one good remedy to reduce the stress of life would be to go for a bike ride. But we need to be careful and avoid getting into a bike race like the two lads did in this issue’s children’s story. We may end up with more stress than we bargained for.

Despite our best efforts to live stress-free lives, we still meet with the unexpected. Last week I was cleaning out our broiler houses in preparation for a new flock. I leaned across the tractor fender to push a partly opened door out of the way. As I stood up, my foot accidentally hit the hydrostatic pedal, lurching the tractor forward and throwing me off-balance. My foot somehow got caught under the pedal, and for a split second, I feared I would fall right in front of the rear wheel. In a last-ditch effort, I threw myself away from the tractor. My foot slipped out of my shoe, and I landed unharmed on the ground. The tractor slowly headed off with my shoe still wedged under the pedal. All ended well, and a few lessons were learned. It was nothing other than the providence of God that prevented a freak incident from becoming a bad accident. Truly I agree with Solomon, “For the LORD shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken” (Proverbs 3:26).

As we navigate through this year, let’s join the hymnwriter in worship, where he writes:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view, I’m lost
In wonder, love and praise.

It is only by the mercies of an all-loving God that we have life and breath. May we give our all to Him and to the work of His kingdom in heartfelt thanksgiving for His unspeakable gift.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Hilsener i den verdige navnet til Herren Jesus Kristus. Når jeg ser utover det golde januarlanskapet, kan jeg ikke la være å undre meg over hva dette nye året vil bringe. Utvilsomt vil det bringe en blanding av glede og sorg, spenning og mørke, latter og tårer, og alt derimellom — noe bare en allmektig Skaper kan ordne på en måte som opphøyer Hans verdige makt og herlighet. Likevel har våre begrensede, negative sinn en tendens til å forvente alle de dårlige tingene som kan skje. Vil inflasjonen presse matprisene enda høyere? Vil utstrakt kamp bryte ut i Midtøsten? Hva vil skje i valgene? Vil det tapende partiet ty til protester og opptøyer?

Jeg antar at slike fryktdrevne tanker har streifet menneskers sinn ved begynnelsen av hvert år siden menneskets fall. Likevel, som det så treffende påpekes av forfatteren av artikkelen «Gods trofasthet manifesterer seg selv også i forbannelsen», har Gud vennlig sørget for menneskeheten siden tidens morgen. Når vi ser tilbake på Guds trofasthet mot mennesket gjennom århundrene, har vi ingen grunn til å tvile på at Gud vil gjøre det samme for oss i 2024.

Til tross for Guds trofasthet mot oss, er følgene av menneskets fall fortsatt tydelige. Familiemedlemmer blir syke, kamp i kirke og nære relasjoner fratar oss søvn, bankkontoen tørker ut, barna krangler og gråter, og kravene i timeplanen får oss til å løpe fra det ene arrangementet til det andre. Og noen ganger virker det som om alle disse ulykkene rammer oss samtidig. Kroppene og sinnene våre er ikke skapt for å takle dette. Vi blir trette. Beinslitte. Utslitte til det punktet at selv å tenke gjør vondt. Vi møter utbrenthet. I dette nummeret leder «A Word From the Doctor» oss gjennom livets labyrint og gir oss praktiske og bibelske løsninger for å unngå eller komme seg etter utbrenthet. Han skriver: «Jesus kjenner våre begrensninger. Han ønsker at vi skal ha balanse, leve på en måte slik at vi ikke bare har styrke for i dag, men også for i morgen, neste uke og neste år — til Han kommer igjen.»

Kanskje en god kur for å redusere livets stress ville være å ta en sykkeltur. Men vi må være forsiktige og unngå å komme inn i et sykkelritt slik de to guttene gjorde i dette nummerets barnehistorie. Vi kan ende opp med mer stress enn vi hadde regnet med.

Til tross for våre beste anstrengelser for å leve stressfrie liv, møter vi fortsatt det uventede. Forrige uke rengjorde jeg kyllingskurene våre i forberedelse til en ny flock. Jeg lente meg over traktorens skjerm for å dytte en delvis åpnet dør til side. Da jeg reiste meg, traff foten min ved et uhell hydrosostatiske pedalen, traktoren rykka fram og kastet meg ut av balanse. Fotbladet mitt ble på en eller annen måte sittende fast under pedalen, og i et øyeblikk fryktet jeg at jeg ville falle rett foran bakhjulet. I et siste desperat forsøk kastet jeg meg bort fra traktoren. Foten gled ut av skoen, og jeg landet uskadd på bakken. Traktoren kjørte rolig av gårde med skoen min fortsatt kilende under pedalen. Alt endte godt, og noen leksjoner ble lært. Det var intet annet enn Guds forsyn som hindret en merkelig hendelse fra å bli en alvorlig ulykke. Sannelig er jeg enig med Salomo: «For HERREN skal være din tillit, og han skal bevare din fot fra å bli tatt» (Ordspråkene 3:26).

Når vi navigerer gjennom dette året, la oss slutte oss til salmeskribenten i tilbedelse, hvor han skriver:

Når alle dine barmhjertigheter, o min Gud,
Min oppvoksende sjel betrakter,
Fører synet meg i ekstase, jeg blir tapt
I undring, kjærlighet og pris.

Det er bare ved barmhjertighetene til en allkjærlig Gud at vi har liv og pust. Må vi gi alt til Ham og til Hans rikes arbeid i hjertelig takknemlighet for Hans ubeskrivelige gave.

Velsignelser til alle,

Edward Martin

Just reading the title probably brings negative thoughts to your mind. We as humans don’t typically like to be told “no” because it goes against our nature. Sometimes we bring the “no” upon ourselves because of disobedience, such as when God said “no” to Moses. “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land . . . But the Lord . . . would not hear me: and the Lord said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter” (Deuteronomy 3:25,26).

In Deuteronomy 1:42, God said “no” to Israel. “And the Lord said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies”, but they rebelled at His “no.” “And ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you” (Deuteronomy 1:45).

God said “no” to Paul. “And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me” (2 Corinthians 12:7-9).

Let us focus our attention upon prayerful Paul’s acceptance of God’s “no.”

First, acceptance does not mean that the problem does not exist. Paul accepted God’s “no”, but still had the infirmities.

Second, acceptance does not mean woeful resignation. Paul “besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.” We should be persistent, even when God’s answer is not forthcoming. (cf. Luke 18:1-8).

Third, God’s “no” may be necessary to avoid a greater evil or infirmity. Twice, Paul says the thorn in the flesh was given “lest I should be exalted above measure.” Unlike Paul, however, we may not know the purpose for God’s “no,” but we can be assured of His faithfulness and goodness. With Paul, we too may have to endure one thing, which means accepting God’s refusal in order to achieve a higher purpose or benefit.

Fourth, Paul’s weakness, as a result of God’s “no,” made him strong. “Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10). The sorrow and suffering some endure has indeed made them strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.

Fifth, Paul’s infirmity allowed the power of Christ to rest upon him. God’s strength was complete, sufficient, and made perfect in weakness. Paul’s strength was seen to be of God. Therefore, Christ, not Paul, was glorified. The infirmities that Paul endured revealed the power not of himself but of God.

Sixth, God explained his answer of “no” by saying, “My grace is sufficient for thee.” God’s love and acceptance of us, His strength and power to assist us in our infirmities and with our weaknesses, is sufficient and complete.

Seventh, Paul gloried in his infirmities, but only after he accepted God’s “no.” Paul ultimately saw that this allowed God’s power to rest upon him. Paul’s weakness displayed and magnified divine power in a manner that human adequacy and personal sufficiency could never accomplish.

Eighth, unfortunately for him, Paul was the vessel, the sufferer, who had to endure afflictions that God’s grace, power, and glory might be truly reflected, but he was glad to bear it for those purposes (cf. 2 Co 4:7-11; Gal 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Until we are ready to do the same, we cannot accept or understand God’s “no.”

A “no” may come into our life for many various reasons.

When God says, “No,” the Christian must remember:

That God will do right. “He is … a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he” (Deuteronomy 32:4). One may not see; he may not, as Job did not, understand, but God will do right. “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” (Genesis 18:25).

That God’s ways are not ours. “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts” (Isaiah 55:8,9). God sees the end from the beginning. Nothing is hidden from him. “Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it” (Psalms 139:6). as a little child cries in protest when his mother pulls him from the road (It is such a great place to ride a tricycle!), so we may cry when God says, “No,” but He, like the child’s parent, knows danger the child may not be able to comprehend or appreciate fully.

That prayer has a chief purpose. Prayer should not be an attempt to manipulate the will of God. “Not my will, but thine, be done,” the suffering Savior cried, but when God says, “No,” we often forget that fact and complain in effect, “Not Thy will but mine be done.” Perhaps the supreme purpose of prayer is to seek God’s will for our lives, our wants, our needs, and our desires. It will help to remember that when God says “no.”

That a present “no” may be a “yes” in development. Paul was told that he was going to Rome (Acts 19:21; 23:11). But the bars of incarceration, the shackles of servitude, and the jaws of death seemed to say otherwise. Two years of confinement were not convincing evidence of a trip to Rome, nor was a hopeless sea voyage (Acts 24:27; 27:20). However, as we all know, Paul went to Rome (Acts 28:16)!

That God’s laws prevail. The laws of nature are laws of God. God does not will that one to fall off a cliff, but if certain physical laws are broken, he will. God has biological laws. Disease may be contracted, and suffering and death may follow. One may pray, “Give us this day our daily bread,” but if he does not use God’s laws to procure it, or if he contradicts God’s means of acquiring it, he will not receive it. As painful as it is to accept, we frequently are victims of earthly laws in the various and diverse orders of physical life. Of course, the reverse is also true. We often are blessed by the material laws of God (Matthew 5:45; Acts 14:17; 1 Timothy 5:23).

In conclusion, Job of old bore the lashes of unparalleled human calamity and agony and torture of mind, body, and soul. His faithfulness and steadfast endurance have blessed thirty centuries of sorrowing humanity. Stephen and James met untimely, violent deaths (Acts 7; 12). They died when we would have had them to live. By their suffering and death, the early disciples were shown the power of the new faith, that men could die and yet live in victory. Hence, multiplied millions have been emboldened and have accepted torture and death rather than denounce their faith and hope of eternal life.

Deliverance came. No, not to Stephen and James, nor to suffering servants such as Job, of like precious faith, but it came in unquenchable hope, in the hope that maketh not ashamed. It came through Him that is able to deliver us who, through fear of death, were subject to bondage. “Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.”

শিরোনামটা মাত্র পড়লেই সম্ভবত আপনার মনে নেতিবাচক চিন্তা জাগে। আমরা মানুষ সাধারণত “না” বলা পছন্দ করি না কারণ তা আমাদের প্রকৃতির বিরুদ্ধে যায়। কখনও কখনও আমরা অজ্ঞাত বাধ্যতায়ই “না” পাই—অবলম্বনে অবাধ্য হওয়ার কারণে—যেমন ঈশ্বর মোশেকে “না” বলেছিলেন। “আমি প্রার্থনা করি, আমাকে পার হতে দাও, এবং সেই শুভ ভূমি দেখতে দিন . . . কিন্তু প্রভু . . . আমার কথা শোনেননি: এবং প্রভু আমার কাছে বলিল, এ পর্যাপ্ত হউক; এই ব্যাপারে আমারে আর বলিও না” (বিধিবাক্য 3:25,26)।

বিধিবাক্য 1:42-এ ঈশ্বর ইস্রায়েলের কাছে “না” বলেছেন। “এবং প্রভু আমার কাছে বলিল, তাদের বল, উঠিয়া যাহিও না, লড়াই করিও না; কারণ আমি তোমাদের মধ্যে নাই; নচেৎ তোমরা শত্রুকূলের সম্মুখে হইতে পরিতপ্ত হও;” তবুও তারা তাঁর “না”-র বিরুদ্ধে বিদ্রোহ করল। “তুমি ফিরে এসে প্রভুর সম্মুখে কাঁদিল, কিন্তু প্রভু তোমাদের কণ্ঠে শোনেননি, তোমাদের উপরে কাণ দেন নি” (বিধিবাক্য 1:45)।

ঈশ্বর পলকে “না” বলেছেন। “আর প্রকাশ্যের অধিকতায় আমি উচ্চতর হইবার উপক্রম না করি, ইহাই কার্যতঃ আমারে দেহের কাঁটা দিল, শয়তানের দূত, যাহা আমাকে মারবে, যাহাতে আমি অত্যধিক উচ্চতা পাই না। এ ব্যাপারে আমি প্রভুকে তিনবারে প্রার্থনা করিলাম, যাহা যেন আমার থেকে বিচ্ছিন্ন হয়। তৎক্ষণে তিনি বলিলেন, আমার অনুগ্রহই তোর জন্য যথেষ্ট; কারণ দুর্বলতায় আমার বল প্ররিপূর্ণ হয়। অতঃপর আমি প্রাণত্যাগে আমার দূর্বলতায় গৌরব করিব; যাতে ক্রিস্টের শক্তি আমার উপর বিশ্রাম গ্রহন করে” (2 করিন্থীয় 12:7-9)।

চলুন আমরা প্রার্থনাশীল পলের ঈশ্বরের “না” গ্রহণের প্রতি মনোযোগ মনোনিবেশ করি।

প্রথমত, গ্রহণ মানে সেই সমস্যার অনুপস্থিতি নয়। পল ঈশ্বরের “না” মেনে নিয়েছিলেন, তবুও তাঁর দুর্বলতা ছিল।

দ্বিতীয়ত, গ্রহণ মানে বেদনাদায়ক হীনচেতা আত্মসমর্পণ নয়। পল “তিসরবার প্রভুকে নিবেদন করিল, যে তা যেন আমার থেকে বিচ্ছিন্ন হয়।” আমাদেরও অনবরত চেষ্টা চালিয়ে যেতে হবে, এমনকি যখন ঈশ্বরের উত্তর না আসে। (তুলনা দেখুন: লূক 18:1-8)।

তৃতীয়ত, ঈশ্বরের “না” হয়তো বড় কোনও অনিষ্ট বা দুর্বলতা এড়ানোর জন্য প্রয়োজনীয়। পল দফায় দফায় বলেছে যে দেহের কাঁটা দেয়া হলো “যাতে আমি অত্যধিক উচ্চতর না হই।” তবে আমাদের, পলের মত নয়, হয়তো ঈশ্বরের “না”-র উদ্দেশ্য জানা নাও থাকতে পারে, কিন্তু আমরা তাঁর বিশ্বস্ততা ও কল্যাণে আশ্বস্ত থাকতে পারি। পলের সাথে, আমাদেরও কখনও একটিকে সহ্য করতে হতে পারে, অর্থাৎ উচ্চতর উদ্দেশ্য বা উপকার অর্জনের লক্ষ্যে ঈশ্বরের প্রত্যাখ্যান গ্রহণ করা।

চতুর্থত, ঈশ্বরের “না”-র ফলে পলের দুর্বলতা তাঁকে শক্তিশালী করেছে। “অতএব আমি দুর্বলতায়, অপমানে, প্রয়োজনতায়, তকমায়, দমন-চাপে খুশি হই; কারণ যখন আমি দুর্বল, তখনই আমি শক্তিশালী” (2 করিন্থীয় 12:10)। কিছু লোকের যে দুঃখ এবং কষ্ট সহ্য করতে হয়, তা সত্যিই প্রভুতে এবং তাঁর মহিমার শক্তিতে তাদের শক্তিশালী করেছে।

পঞ্চমত, পলের দুর্বলতা ক্রিস্টের শক্তিকে তাঁর উপর বিশ্রাম নিতে দিল। ঈশ্বরের শক্তি পরিপূর্ণ, যথেষ্ট, এবং দুর্বলতায় পূর্ণতা লাভ করে। পলের শক্তি ঈশ্বরের থেকে প্রদর্শিত হলো। অতএব মহানতা পেলে ক্রিস্ট, পল নয়। পল যে দুর্বলতা সহ্য করিলেন, সেগুলো তাঁর নিজের নয় বরং ঈশ্বরের শক্তিকে প্রকাশ করিল।

ষষ্ঠত, ঈশ্বর “না” বলে যে উত্তরটি ব্যাখ্যা করলেন তা হচ্ছিল, “আমার অনুগ্রহই তোর জন্য যথেষ্ট।” ঈশ্বরের আমাদের প্রতি ভালোবাসা ও গ্রহণ, দুর্বলতায় এবং কষ্টে আমাদের সহায়তার জন্য তাঁর শক্তি ও ক্ষমতা যথেষ্ট এবং পরিপূর্ণ।

সপ্তমত, পল তাঁর দুর্বলতায় গৌরব করলেন, কিন্তু কেবল তখনই যখন তিনি ঈশ্বরের “না” মেনে নেন। পল শেষপর্যন্ত দেখলেন যে এতে ঈশ্বরের শক্তি তাঁর উপর বিশ্রাম গ্রহণ করতে পারল। পলের দুর্বলতা দিব্য শক্তিকে এমনভাবে প্রদর্শন ও বাড়িয়ে তুলল যা মানবীয় সক্ষমতা ও ব্যক্তিগত পরিপূর্ণতা কখনই করতে পারত না।

অষ্টমত, দুর্ভাগ্যবশত তাঁর জন্য, পলই ছিল সেই বাহন, ভুক্তভোগী, যাকে কষ্ট সহ্য করতে হতো যেন ঈশ্বরের অনুগ্রহ, শক্তি, ও মহিমা সত্যিকারভাবে প্রতিফলিত হয়—কিন্তু তিনি সেই উদ্দেশ্যে তা বহন করতে খুশি ছিলেন (তুলনা দেখুন: 2 কর 4:7-11; গাল 4:13,14; 6:14,17)। যতক্ষণ না আমরা একই কাজ করার জন্য প্রস্তুত, আমরা ঈশ্বরের “না” গ্রহণ বা বুঝতে পারব না।

একটি “না” আমাদের জীবনে বিভিন্ন কারণে আসতে পারে।

যখন ঈশ্বর বলেন, “না,” খ্রিস্টানকে মনে রাখা উচিত:

যে ঈশ্বর ঠিক কাজ করবেন। “তিনি … সত্যের ঈশ্বর এবং পাপহীন, তিনি ন্যায্য এবং অধিকার সংবলিত” (বিধিবাক্য 32:4)। কেউ না দেখে থাকতে পারে; তিনি যেমন ইব্রাহিমের সময়ে নেই বুঝতে পেরেছিলেন, তেমনি কেউ না বুঝতে পারে; কিন্তু ঈশ্বর ঠিক কাজ করবেন। “সমস্ত পৃথিবীর বিচারক কি ন্যায় করবেন না?” (উৎপত্তি 18:25)।

যে ঈশ্বরের পথ আমাদের পথ নয়। “কারণ আমার চিন্তা তোমাদের চিন্তা নয়, তোমাদের পথ আমার পথ নয়, বলে প্রভু। যেন স্বর্গপৃষ্ঠটা পৃথিবী থেকে উচ্চ, তেমনি আমার পথ তোমাদের পথ থেকে উচ্চ, এবং আমার চিন্তা তোমাদের চিন্তা থেকে উচ্চ” (ইসাইয়া 55:8,9)। ঈশ্বর শুরু থেকে শেষ পর্যন্ত দেখে থাকেন। কিছুই তাঁকে অপ্রাপ্ত নয়। “এমন জ্ঞান আমার জন্য অতিশয় বিস্ময়কর; তা উচ্চ, আমি তাতে পৌঁছাই না” (গীৎ 139:6)। যেমন একটি ছোট শিশু রাস্তা থেকে তুলে নেওয়ার সময় প্রতিবাদে স্কীর করে (তিনচক্রে চড়তে সেখানে কত দারুণ!), তেমনি আমরা ঈশ্বর যখন “না” বলেন তখন কেঁদে উঠতে পারি, কিন্তু তিনি—শিশুর মা-বাবার মত—জানেন শিশুটির উপলব্ধি করতে না পারার বিপদটি।

যে প্রার্থনার একটি প্রধান উদ্দেশ্য আছে। প্রার্থনা ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছাকে প্রভাবিত করার চেষ্টা হওয়া উচিত নয়। “আমার ইচ্ছা নয়, তবু তোর ইচ্ছাই হউক,” সেই দুঃখী ত্রাণকারী ক্রন্দন করেছিলেন, কিন্তু যখন ঈশ্বর “না” বলেন, আমরা প্রায়ই তা ভুলে গিয়ে কার্যত অভিযোগ করি, “তোমার ইচ্ছা নয় বরং আমার ইচ্ছাই হউক।” সম্ভবত প্রার্থনার প্রধান উদ্দেশ্য হল আমাদের জীবন, আমাদের ইচ্ছা, আমাদের প্রয়োজন ও আকাঙ্ক্ষার জন্য ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছা খোঁজা। ঈশ্বর যখন “না” বলেন তখন এটি মনে রাখা সাহায্য করবে।

যে একটি বর্তমান “না” বিকাশে একটি “হ্যাঁ” হতে পারে। পলকে বলা হয়েছিল যে তিনি রোমে যাচ্ছেন (প্রেরিতকার্য 19:21; 23:11)। কিন্তু বন্দিত্বের লৌহশৃঙ্খল, দাসত্বের শৃঙ্খল, এবং মৃত্যুর চোয়াল ভিন্ন কথা বলছিল। দুই বছরের কারাবাস রোম যাত্রার প্রমাণ ছিল না, নতুবা হাহাকারজনক সমুদ্রযাত্রাও না (প্রেরিতকার্য 24:27; 27:20)। তবে, যেমন আমরা সবাই জানি, পল রোমে গেলেন (প্রেরিতকার্য 28:16)!

যে ঈশ্বরের আইন জয়ী। প্রকৃতির আইন ঈশ্বরের আইন। ঈশ্বর ইচ্ছা করেন না যে কেউ পর্বতমুখ থেকে পড়ে যাক, কিন্তু যদি নির্দিষ্ট ভৌত আইন ভাঙা হয়, তবে সে পড়বে। ঈশ্বরের জৈবিক আইন আছে। রোগ সংক্রমিত হতে পারে, এবং কষ্ট ও মৃত্যু ঘটতে পারে। কেউ প্রার্থনা করতে পারে, “আজ আমাদের দৈনিক রুটি দাও,” কিন্তু যদি সে তা অর্জন করতে ঈশ্বরের আইন ব্যবহার না করে, অথবা যদি সে তা অর্জনের ঈশ্বরীয় উপায়ের বিরুদ্ধে কাজ করে, তবে সে তা পাবেনা। গ্রহণ করতে যত কষ্টকর তাতেও, আমরা প্রায়ই ভূতাত্ত্বিক জীবনের বিভিন্ন এবং বৈচিত্র্যময় শৃঙ্খলে পৃথিবীর আইনের শিকার হই। অবশ্যই, বিপরীতটাও সত্য। আমরা প্রায়ই ঈশ্বরের ভৌত আইনের দ্বারা আশীর্বাদপ্রাপ্ত হই (মাৎথিউ 5:45; প্রেরিতকার্য 14:17; 1 তীমথিয় 5:23)।

উপসংহারে, প্রাচীন জব অতুল্য মানব দুর্যোগ ও যন্ত্রণার চামড়ার নিয়ে শাসন সহ্য করেছিল—মন, শরীর ও আত্মার যন্ত্রণার কাঁটা। তাঁর বিশ্বস্ততা এবং ধৈর্যশীল সহ্যতা তিরিশ শতক দুঃখিত মানবজাতিকে আশীর্বাদ করেছে। স্টিফেন ও যাকোব অকালমাত্রিক, হিংস্র মৃত্যুওয় ভোগ করেছেন (প্রেরিতকার্য 7; 12)। আমরা চাইতাম তারা বেঁচে থাকুক, তবুও তারা মরে গেল। তাদের কষ্ট ও মৃত্যুর মাধ্যমে প্রাথমিক শিষ্যদের নতুন বিশ্বাসের শক্তি প্রদর্শিত হল—লোকেরা মরতে পারে এবং তবু জয়ী হয়ে বাঁচতে পারে। অতএব, বহু কোটি উৎসাহিত হয়েছেন এবং তাঁরা তাদের বিশ্বাস ও চিরন্তন জীবনের আশায় বিশ্বাস ছাড়ার চেয়ে অত্যাচার ও মৃত্যুকে গ্রহণ করেছেন।

রক্ষা এসেছিল। না, স্টিফেন এবং যাকোবের জন্য নয়, না জবের মত কষ্টভোগী দাসদের জন্য নয়—যাদের বিশ্বাস অমূল্য ছিল—কিন্তু এটি অপরাজেয় আশায় এসেছিল, সেই আশায় যা লজ্জা দেয় না। এটি তাঁর দ্বারা এলো, যিনি আমাদের উদ্ধার করতে সক্ষম, যাঁদের আমরা মৃত্যুর ভয়ে দাসত্বে আবদ্ধ ছিলাম। “তার অ কণ্ঠে কৃতজ্ঞতা।”

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

Era il proverbiale “mondo perfetto” che Adamo ed Eva godevano ogni giorno con il loro Creatore. Il bellissimo giardino, progettato, creato e piantato a mano dallo stesso Dio, era perfetto in ogni suo aspetto. Sappiamo tutti che non rimase così per molto tempo. A causa del privilegio della scelta che Dio concesse a tutta l’umanità, entrambi presto fecero la scelta sbagliata. Eva, sebbene ingannata da Satana sotto forma di serpente, credette alla menzogna e scelse di disobbedire a Dio, facendo l’unica cosa che Dio le aveva amorevolmente chiesto di non fare. Ma quando portò il frutto ad Adamo, lui non fu ingannato. Sapeva che era sbagliato. Dio non fu sorpreso ma, nondimeno, molto deluso. In Genesi 3 leggiamo il triste racconto dell’espulsione dell’umanità dal giardino, della chiusura dell’accesso all’albero della vita e della pronuncia della maledizione a causa del peccato di Adamo ed Eva. Sembrava così oscuro e senza speranza. Anche se fu un solo uomo a peccare, la maledizione si trasmise a tutto il mondo creato, compresa la terra, le piante e gli animali. Considerate con me tutto ciò che venne insieme a questa potente maledizione.

  1. Malattia
  2. Angoscia e dolore
  3. Deterioramento e distruzione
  4. Dominio di piante come spine e cardi
  5. Morte
  6. Decomposizione e putrefazione

Oggi li chiameremo i sei “D” della maledizione.

Malattia

I giorni immacolati di salute eterna e perfetta del mondo erano passati. La malattia entrò in scena come parte della maledizione del peccato. I figli degli uomini, gli uccelli, le bestie e le piante iniziarono tutti a sperimentare gli effetti della sofferenza e della malattia. Ma Dio fu fedele fornendo istruzioni che aiutavano l’uomo a sapere come evitare molte malattie prevenibili con la pulizia e la semplice obbedienza. Per esempio, il comandamento di Dio di onorare il Suo intento originale nel matrimonio, mantenere la purezza, evitare molte potenziali malattie, ecc. Egli si interessava anche della nostra condizione spirituale. Dio non ha mai progettato l’umanità per portare colpa. Vuole che abbiamo e manteniamo la coscienza pura perché sa che una coscienza colpevole può renderti malato!

Alcune di queste malattie sarebbero state inevitabili, ma molte potevano essere prevenute sviluppando immunità. Dio fu anche fedele nel progettare persone, piante e animali con un microbioma rigenerativo (miliardi di batteri utili) e un sistema immunitario sistemico, che ci aiuta a combattere le malattie. È sorprendente come ogni pianta sembri avere certe proprietà dietetiche o curative che sono benefiche. Che Creatore fedele!

Angoscia e dolore

Sospetto che nel Giardino dell’Eden non ci fosse alcuna vera ragione per il dolore, ma abbiamo sperimentato il dolore sin dal giorno della loro uscita. Il dolore è infatti parte della vita di molti di noi. Esistono molti tipi di dolore. Il lutto, il dolore e il rifiuto sono tutti dolori emotivi che accompagnano la maledizione. Dolori fisici come dolori muscolari, emicranie, muscoli indolenziti, legamenti strappati, tendini infetti, articolazioni usurate e ossa rotte sono alcuni dei dolori fisici che potremmo provare prima del nostro ultimo respiro. Anche in questo caso, Dio è stato fedele nell’aiutare l’umanità a capire cosa fare per alleviare alcuni dei dolori e delle angosce della vita. Fin dall’antichità, piante, erbe e altri rimedi hanno aiutato le persone a far fronte al dolore e all’angoscia. Ancora oggi abbiamo molte piante utili che ci aiutano con il dolore.

Una delle cose più belle che si possono sperimentare sulla terra è la nascita di un bambino. Eppure il parto è generalmente accompagnato da molto dolore. Sebbene non possiamo eliminare questo dolore promesso, Dio è stato fedele nel fornirci e rivelarci l’uso di molte erbe da usare prima, durante e dopo il parto per attenuare il dolore e accelerare la guarigione. Non avrebbe dovuto farlo per noi. L’umanità davvero non merita misericordia. Che Creatore fedele!

Deterioramento e distruzione

Non dobbiamo studiare molto la storia per vedere questo principio all’opera. Vento, pioggia e sole producono effetti deterioranti su molte cose. Che si consideri un argine eroso, le rocce levigate nel letto del fiume o l’albero sradicato dal vento, questi sono tutti elementi naturali di distruzione. Ma aggiungiamo ciò che l’uomo ha fatto alle piante, agli animali, al suolo e gli uni agli altri. Sia per gli effetti devastanti della distruzione durante le orribili guerre, sia per le pratiche egoistiche e avido-centrate in tempo di pace, l’uomo è una creatura molto distruttiva. Dio concesse all’umanità il dominio su tutta la creazione. Tuttavia, troppo spesso interpretiamo erroneamente questo come se fossimo proprietari di questa sfera chiamata terra e potessimo farne ciò che vogliamo. Colui che dichiarò: “La terra è del Signore”, non concorda con l’idea che gli uomini siano altro che amministratori della creazione di Dio. È davvero malvagio adorare il mondo creato o qualsiasi cosa in esso. Ma è altrettanto malvagio essere ingrati e negligenti con la creazione del nostro Creatore! Nondimeno, Dio ha fedelmente progettato la Sua terra con capacità rigenerative in mezzo a questa maledizione. Benedetto il nostro misericordioso Creatore!

Dominio di spine e cardi

Chiunque abbia mai coltivato un giardino ha presto sperimentato la realtà della battaglia con le erbacce. A essere giusti, qualsiasi pianta che cresce dove non è desiderata è un’“erba infestante”. Molte erbacce possono essere piante molto benefiche se sappiamo solo come usarle. Alcune delle piante che chiamiamo erbacce sono in realtà abbastanza nutrienti e salutari una volta che capiamo quali sono commestibili e come prepararle. Oggi vogliamo pensare a spine e cardi. Dobbiamo presumere che furono creati nei primi sei giorni, non dopo che la maledizione fu pronunciata. Sembra che la loro capacità di superare le colture utili sia aumentata dopo la maledizione. Anche in questa parte della maledizione vediamo Dio misericordiosamente provvedere per noi.

Coltiviamo il carciofo per le sue foglie amare, usate per preparare amari digestivi. Pensateci: cardo benedetto, cardo mariano, cardo serpente, foglia di lampone e radici di rovo sono solo alcuni esempi di membri di queste “erbacce spinose” usate per benefici medicinali e alimentari. Quanto è buono Dio nel darci benefici in mezzo alla stessa maledizione!

Morte

Questo è l’unico “D” di cui la maggior parte di noi preferirebbe non parlare. In realtà, quando prendiamo il nostro primo respiro, siamo a un respiro di distanza dalla morte. Sebbene tutte le piante, gli animali e le persone alla fine moriranno, non ci sentiamo comunque a nostro agio nell’affrontarla. È del tutto normale avere una volontà di vivere, e se non ce l’abbiamo dovremmo cercare aiuto per capire il perché.

In effetti, la morte non ha età. Nella mia vita ho aiutato a seppellire neonati morti alla nascita, persone fino a 96 anni e tutte le età nel mezzo. Leggiamo del bellissimo paradiso restaurato, visto dall’apostolo Giovanni nell’Apocalisse, mentre descrive il Cielo. Alcune delle cose che menziona sono nessuna malattia, nessun dolore, nessuna separazione, nessuna lacrima, nessuna sofferenza e nessuna morte. In un certo senso, la vita è solo un periodo di gestazione per l’eternità. Non possiamo restare qui, proprio come il bambino nel grembo non può decidere di non entrare nel mondo reale. Con tutto il nostro dolore e le nostre tentazioni, i nostri corpi si consumano e si deteriorano. Con tutta la violenza, il peccato e la malvagità che ci circondano, davvero vorremmo restare qui in questo stato per sempre? Piuttosto, torniamo al suolo da cui siamo stati formati, cenere alla cenere e polvere alla polvere, aspettando la risurrezione finale. Non fu forse grazioso da parte del nostro fedele Dio non permettere all’uomo peccatore di mangiare dell’albero della vita nel suo attuale stato peccaminoso e morente? Possiamo vedere ed essere grati per la fedeltà di Dio nel provvedere la morte fisica?

Nel mezzo della maledizione data a Eva viene rivelata la prima profezia del Messia. “E porrò inimicizia tra te e la donna, e tra la tua progenie e la sua progenie; essa ti ferirà alla testa, e tu le ferirai il calcagno” (Genesi 3:15). Egli è il vincitore della morte! Lodate Dio per la Sua fedeltà.

Decomposizione e putrefazione

La decomposizione e la putrefazione sono un altro “D” della maledizione. Una noce cade a terra e presto appare un germoglio. In pochi anni sarà una piccola pianta. Passano gli anni, e gli scoiattoli raccolgono le ghiande che cadono ogni autunno. Poi, come una possente quercia, contrae un virus, muore e in pochi anni viene portata a terra da una tempesta. Qui ritorna al suolo mentre si decompone e putrefà. Da quando la maledizione è stata pronunciata, tutto marcisce e si decompone. Considerando tutte le piante, gli animali e le persone che sono morte negli ultimi 6.000 anni, non è forse buono che Dio abbia progettato la decomposizione e la putrefazione? Come sarebbe questo mondo se tutti i detriti di 6.000 anni fossero ancora sparsi in giro? La terra sarebbe coperta di alberi morti e cadaveri! Può essere difficile da realizzare, ma Dio progettò interi regni nella creazione solo per compiere questo prima ancora che fosse necessario, perché prevedeva la necessità. I regni del lievito, della muffa e dei funghi, i regni dei batteri, degli enzimi e della vita vegetale e animale microscopica aiutano a degradare la fibra della vita e a trasformarla nel concime perfetto per il completamento del ciclo vitale e la provvista per la generazione successiva. Un suolo organico sano contiene circa 8 miliardi di microrganismi in un solo cucchiaio. Questa è un’altra ragione per cui è così importante trattare il suolo con rispetto e non con prodotti chimici aggressivi.

Avete mai considerato il grande diluvio di Noè? Immaginate milioni di tonnellate di materia vegetale, animale e umana che galleggiavano prima di depositarsi sul fondo e venire rapidamente sepolte nei sedimenti mentre le acque si ritiravano. Questo produsse le condizioni ideali per formare il carbone e gli altri combustibili fossili che usiamo oggi. Là giacevano, in profondità nella terra, fino al giorno della loro scoperta. Ancora oggi vengono utilizzati.

Siamo responsabili e fedeli amministratori della terra del Signore!

“Infatti la creazione attende con ardente aspettativa la manifestazione dei figli di Dio. Perché la creazione fu soggetta alla vanità, non di sua volontà, ma per colui che l’ha soggetta, nella speranza; perché anche la creazione stessa sarà liberata dalla schiavitù della corruzione per entrare nella gloriosa libertà dei figli di Dio. Sappiamo infatti che tutta la creazione geme e soffre le doglie insieme fino a ora. E non soltanto essa, ma anche noi che abbiamo il primizia dello Spirito, anche noi gemiamo in noi stessi, aspettando l’adozione, la redenzione del nostro corpo” (Romani 8:19-23).
