It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

Det var det bildliga ”perfekta livet” som Adam och Eva dagligen njöt av tillsammans med sin Skapare. Den vackra trädgården, skapad, utformad och handplanterad av Gud själv, var perfekt på alla sätt. Vi vet alla att det inte förblev så särskilt länge. På grund av valfriheten som Gud gav åt hela mänskligheten gjorde båda snart fel val. Eva, även om hon blev förledd av Satan i ormens gestalt, trodde lögnen och valde att trotsa Gud och gjorde det enda som Gud kärleksfullt hade bett henne att inte göra. Men när hon gav frukten till Adam blev han inte förledd. Han visste att det var fel. Gud blev inte överraskad men ändå mycket besviken. I Första Moseboken kapitel 3 läser vi den sorgliga berättelsen om människans utkörning ur trädgården, avstängandet från livets träd och förbannelsens uttalande på grund av Adams och Evas synd. Det verkade så mörkt och hopplöst. Fastän det bara var en man som syndade, gick förbannelsen vidare till hela den skapade världen, inklusive jorden, växterna och djuren. Tänk bara med mig på vad som följde med denna mäktiga förbannelse.

  1. Sjukdom
  2. Förtvivlan och smärta
  3. Förfall och förstörelse
  4. Dominans av vissa växter som törnen och tistlar
  5. Död
  6. Förtäring och förruttnelse

Vi kommer i dag att hänvisa till dem som förbannelsens sex ”D:n”.

Sjukdom

Världens orörda dagar av evig, fullkomlig hälsa var förbi. Sjukdom trädde in som en del av syndens förbannelse. Människans barn, fåglarna, djuren och växterna skulle alla börja erfara effekterna av sjukdom och åkommor. Men Gud var trofast genom att ge föreskrifter som hjälpte människan att veta hur man undviker många förebyggbara sjukdomar genom renlighet och enkel lydnad. Till exempel Guds bud att hedra Hans ursprungliga avsikt i äktenskapet, behålla renhet, undvika flera möjliga sjukdomar med mera. Han var också intresserad av vårt andliga tillstånd. Gud skapade aldrig människan för att bära skuld. Han vill att vi ska ha och bevara ett rent samvete eftersom Han vet att ett skuldbelagt samvete kan göra dig sjuk!

Några av dessa sjukdomar skulle vara oundvikliga, men många kunde förebyggas genom att bygga upp immunitet. Gud var också trofast i att utforma människor, växter och djur med ett regenerativt mikrobiom (miljarder hjälpsamma bakterier) och ett systemiskt immunsystem, som hjälper oss att bekämpa sjukdomar. Det är förunderligt hur varje växt tycks ha vissa näringsmässiga eller läkande egenskaper som är fördelaktiga. Så trofast är Skaparen!

Förtvivlan och smärta

Jag misstänker att det inte fanns någon egentlig anledning till smärta i Edens trädgård, men vi har upplevt smärta ända sedan den dag de tvingades ut. Smärta är verkligen en del av många av våra liv. Det finns många typer av smärta. Sorg, bedrövelse och avvisande är alla känslomässiga smärtor som följer med förbannelsen. Värk, migrän, ömma muskler, stukade ligament, infekterade senor, utslitna leder och brutna ben är några av de fysiska smärtor vi kan uppleva någon gång före vår sista suck. Återigen har Gud varit trofast i att hjälpa människan förstå vad som bör göras för att lindra en del av livets smärtor och plågor. Från forntiden har växter, örter och andra botemedel hjälpt människor hantera smärta och ångest. Än i dag finns många nyttiga växter som hjälper oss med smärta.

Ett av de vackraste ting som kan upplevas på jorden är födelsen av ett barn. Ändå åtföljs födseln i allmänhet av mycket smärta. Fastän vi inte kan utplåna denna utlovade smärta, har Gud varit trofast i att förse och uppenbara för oss användningen av många örter före, under och efter födseln för att lindra smärtan och skynda på återhämtningen. Han behövde inte göra det för oss. Människan förtjänar egentligen ingen barmhärtighet. Vilken trofast Skapare!

Förfall och förstörelse

Vi behöver inte studera historien särskilt mycket för att se denna princip i arbete. Vind, regn och sol har alla nedbrytande effekter på många ting. Oavsett om vi ser en eroderad åbankskant, stenar rundslipade i flodfåran eller ett träd som fälls av vind, är detta naturliga inslag av förstörelse. Men lägg därtill vad människan har gjort mot växter, djur, jorden och varandra. Oavsett om det gäller förödelsen under hemska krig eller egoistiska och giriga handlingar i fredstid är människan en mycket destruktiv varelse. Gud gav människan herravälde över hela skapelsen. Alltför ofta tolkar vi dock felaktigt det som att vi äger denna sfär som kallas jord och kan göra vad vi vill med den. Den som uttalade: ”Herren tillhör jorden” håller inte med om idén att människan är annat än förvaltare av Guds skapelse. Det är verkligen ondskefullt att dyrka den skapade världen eller något i den. Men det är lika ondskefullt att vara otacksam och vårdslös med vår Skapares verk! Trots detta har Gud troget utformat jorden med regenererande förmågor mitt i denna förbannelse. Välsignad vare vår nådefulle Skapare!

Dominans av törnen och tistlar

Den som någonsin har trädgårdat har snart erfarit verkligheten i kampen mot ogräset. Med all rätt är varje växt som växer där den inte önskas ett ”ogräs”. Många ogräs kan vara mycket nyttiga växter om vi bara vet vad de kan användas till. Några av de växter vi kallar ogräs är faktiskt ganska näringsrika och hälsosamma när vi väl förstår vilka som är ätbara och hur man bereder dem. Idag vill vi tänka på törnen och tistlar. Vi måste anta att de skapades under de första sex dagarna, inte efter att förbannelsen uttalats. Det verkar som att deras förmåga att öka och tränga undan de nyttiga grödorna ökade efter förbannelsen. Även i denna del av förbannelsen ser vi att Gud barmhärtigt förser oss.

Vi odlar kronärtskockan för dess bitterblad, som används för att göra matsmältningsbitter. Tänk efter: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, hallonblad och björnbärs- rötter är bara några exempel på medlemmar i dessa ”taggiga ogräs” som används för medicinska ändamål och annan matnyttig användning. Hur god av Gud att ge oss fördelar mitt i själva förbannelsen!

Död

Detta är den ”D” som de flesta av oss helst inte talar om. I verkligheten, när vi tar vårt första andetag är vi ett andetag närmare döden. Fastän alla växter, djur och människor så småningom dör, känner vi oss ändå obekväma inför det. Det är helt normalt att vi har en vilja att leva, och om vi inte har det bör vi söka hjälp för att ta reda på varför.

Verkligen, döden har ingen ålder. Under mitt liv har jag hjälpt till att begrava dödfödda spädbarn, människor så gamla som 96 år och alla åldrar däremellan. Vi läser om det vackra paradis som återställs, sett av aposteln Johannes i Uppenbarelseboken, när han beskriver himlen. Några av de ting han nämner är ingen sjukdom, ingen sorg, ingen separation, inga tårar, inget mer lidande och ingen död. På ett sätt är livet bara en bärare-tid för evigheten. Vi kan inte stanna här, precis som fostret i livmodern inte kan bestämma sig för att det inte vill gå in i den verkliga världen. Med all vår sorg och frestelse slits våra kroppar ut och förmultnar. Med all våldsamhet, synd och ogudaktighet omkring oss, skulle vi verkligen vilja stanna här i detta tillstånd för alltid? Snarare återvänder vi till jorden som vi är gjorda av, aska till aska och stoft till stoft, i väntan på den slutliga uppståndelsen. Var det inte nådigt av vår trofaste Gud att inte låta den syndiga människan äta av livets träd i sitt nuvarande syndiga, döende tillstånd? Kan vi se och vara tacksamma för Guds trofasthet i att förse oss med döden som ett slutligt vilorum?

Mitt i den förbannelse som gavs till Eva uppenbaras den första Messiasprofetian. ”Och jag skall sätta fiendskap mellan dig och kvinnan, mellan din säd och hennes säd; han skall stöta ditt huvud, och du skall stöta hans häl” (Genesis 3:15). Han är dödens segrare! Pris vare Gud för hans trofasthet.

Förtäring och förruttnelse

Förtäring och förruttnelse är en annan av förbannelsens ”D:n”. En nöt faller till marken, och snart kommer ett skott upp. Om några år är det en liten planta. Åren går, och ekorrarna samlar ekollonen som faller varje höst. Sedan, som en mäktig ek, får den ett virus, dör och blåser omkull vid nästa storm. Här återvänder den till jorden när den förmultnar och förgår. Allt sedan förbannelsen ruttnar och förfaller allt. Med tanke på alla växter, djur och människor som dött under de senaste 6 000 åren, är det inte gott av Gud att ha utformat förruttnelse och nedbrytning? Hur skulle denna värld se ut om allt skräp från 6 000 år fortfarande låg omkring? Jorden skulle vara täckt av döda träd och lik! Det kan vara svårt att förstå, men Gud skapade hela riken i skapelsen just för att åstadkomma detta innan det ens behövdes eftersom Han förutseende såg behovet. Jäst-, mögel- och svampriken, rikena av bakterier, enzymer och mikroskopiskt växt- och djurliv hjälper alla till att bryta ner livets fibrer och göra det till den perfekta gödseln för fullbordan av livscykeln och för försörjning av nästa generation. Hälsosam organisk jord har ungefär 8 miljarder mikrober i en enda matsked. Detta är ytterligare en anledning till varför det är så viktigt att behandla jorden med respekt, inte med starka kemikalier.

Har du någonsin övervägt syndafloden i Noas dagar? Föreställ dig de miljoner ton plant-, djur- och människomaterial som flöt omkring innan de slutligen sjönk till botten och snabbt begravdes i sediment när vattnen drog sig tillbaka. Detta skapade de idealiska förhållandena för att bilda kol och andra fossila bränslen som vi använder idag. Där låg det, djupt i jorden, tills dagen då det upptäcktes. Fortfarande används det än i dag.

Må vi vara ansvariga och trofasta förvaltare av Herrens jord!

”Ty skapelsens väntan väntar på uppenbarelsen av Guds söner. Ty skapelsen blev underkastad fåfänglighet, icke av egen vilja, utan på grund av honom som underkastade den i hopp; ty skapelsen själv skall också bliva fri från förgängelsens träldom till den härliga friheten av Guds barns härlighet. För vi veta att hela skapelsen suckar och måst i smärta ända till nu. Inte allenast den, utan vi själva som hava de första frukterna av Anden; även vi sucka inom oss och vänta på barndomssonen, till kroppens förlossning” (Romans 8:19-23).

Someone once said “When hope is alive, the night is less dark, the solitude less deep, and fear less acute.” When I worked in a prison as an assistant chaplain, I would sit with the condemned men and listen as they talked of their plight. Almost without exception, all spoke of hoping to get out of prison one day. Even if they had a life sentence, they hoped to get out.

I have spoken to people who do not confess to be born again, but still hope to go to heaven. These people dare not leave off hoping. Their hope is based upon their own hope! A diet on that kind of hope is a slim diet for sure! This reasoning reminds me of Jesus' words in John 10:1-2 about entering the sheepfold. “But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.” People build their hope for heaven on many shaky things. Some base their hope on having been baptized in a certain church. Some hope in their church membership. Some people hope in their good works, while still others hope in their hope. The Bible, however, says, “. . . except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God” (John 3:3).

There is a true hope and a false hope. The false hope is “climbing up some other way,” but true hope is “he that entereth in by the door.”

“For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?” (Romans 8:24). This word hope means “with anticipation or great expectation.” Could we say that we are saved by great expectation? Yes, we can. “Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed” (John 6:27). This seems to be a contradiction of sorts. Are we not saved by grace? Yes, we are saved by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8). Then what is this being saved by hope and laboring for the “meat which endureth unto everlasting life”?

“Then they said unto him, what shall we do, that we might work the works of God?” Jesus answered and said unto them, “this is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent” (John 6:28-29). It is only by grace that we are saved, but as this passage suggests, grace sets a condition. The condition of grace is that we believe on Him. Another condition of salvation is repentance (Mark 1:15), while another is cross-bearing. “Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross and follow me” (Mark 8:34).

Everything we would do for Christ, whether believing, repenting, or cross-bearing, is by grace. Whatever we have, or do, is because of Him. We do not work for our salvation, for Christ Himself said, “It is finished.” We have nothing to hope for if we do not meet the conditions of our salvation. Once we receive the Lord Jesus as Saviour, then “hope maketh not ashamed” (Romans 5:5).

As Christ becomes alive in us, we love Him and choose to obey Him. Jesus becomes more precious to us as we mature in our Christian life. As our relationship grows, our expectation grows as well. The more we get to know Him, the more we look forward to being in His presence. As our anticipation of seeing Him grows, we try to do all things possible to please Him. Our great eagerness keeps us from becoming weary, thus, “we are saved by hope.”

Is your hope like the one who “climbeth up some other way,” or like, “he that entereth in by the door”? Do you have a basis for your hope or is it an empty hope that has no foundation?

I trust you are growing up “. . . into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ” (Ephesians 4:15).

I hope you might grow just a little more, so your expectation of seeing Christ might grow as well. The testimony of this expectation is, “. . . in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven” (2 Corinthians 5:2).

Quelqu’un a dit un jour « Quand l’espérance est vive, la nuit est moins sombre, la solitude moins profonde et la peur moins aiguë. » Quand je travaillais en prison comme aumônier adjoint, je m’asseyais auprès des condamnés et j’écoutais pendant qu’ils parlaient de leur situation. Presque sans exception, tous disaient espérer sortir de prison un jour. Même s’ils avaient une peine à perpétuité, ils espéraient sortir.

J’ai parlé à des personnes qui ne se disent pas nées de nouveau, mais qui espèrent quand même aller au ciel. Ces gens n’osent pas cesser d’espérer. Leur espérance repose sur leur propre espérance ! Un régime basé sur ce type d’espérance est assurément maigre ! Ce raisonnement me rappelle les paroles de Jésus dans Jean 10:1-2 à propos de l’entrée dans la bergerie. « Mais celui qui entre par la porte est le berger des brebis. » Les gens fondent leur espérance de ciel sur bien des choses fragiles. Certains fondent leur espérance sur le fait d’avoir été baptisés dans telle église. D’autres espèrent en leur appartenance à une église. Quelques-uns espèrent dans leurs bonnes œuvres, tandis que d’autres encore espèrent dans leur espérance. La Bible, cependant, dit : « … sauf si quelqu’un naît de nouveau, il ne peut voir le royaume de Dieu » (Jean 3:3).

Il y a une véritable espérance et une fausse espérance. La fausse espérance, c’est « monter par quelque autre chemin », mais la vraie espérance est « celui qui entre par la porte ».

« Car nous avons été sauvés dans l’espérance ; or l’espérance qu’on voit n’est pas de l’espérance : en effet, que peut-on attendre encore de ce qu’on voit ? » (Romains 8:24). Ce mot espérance signifie « avec anticipation ou grande attente ». Pourrions‑nous dire que nous sommes sauvés par une grande attente ? Oui, nous le pouvons. « Ne travaillez pas pour la nourriture qui périt, mais pour la nourriture qui demeure pour la vie éternelle, que le Fils de l’homme vous donnera ; car c’est lui que le Père a marqué de son sceau » (Jean 6:27). Cela paraît être une sorte de contradiction. Ne sommes‑nous pas sauvés par la grâce ? Oui, nous sommes sauvés par la grâce par la foi (Éphésiens 2:8). Alors qu’est‑ce que ce salut « par l’espérance » et le fait de travailler pour la « nourriture qui demeure pour la vie éternelle » ?

« Ils lui dirent donc : Que ferons‑nous, afin d’exécuter les œuvres de Dieu ? Jésus répondit et leur dit : Voilà l’œuvre de Dieu, que vous croyiez en celui qu’il a envoyé » (Jean 6:28-29). Ce n’est que par la grâce que nous sommes sauvés, mais comme le suggère ce passage, la grâce établit une condition. La condition de la grâce est que nous croyions en Lui. Une autre condition du salut est la repentance (Marc 1:15), tandis qu’une autre est le port de la croix. « Si quelqu’un veut venir après moi, qu’il renonce à lui‑même, qu’il se charge de sa croix, et qu’il me suive » (Marc 8:34).

Tout ce que nous ferons pour Christ, que ce soit croire, nous repentir ou porter la croix, se fait par la grâce. Tout ce que nous avons, ou faisons, est à cause de Lui. Nous ne travaillons pas pour notre salut, car Christ Lui‑même a dit : « C’est accompli. » Nous n’avons rien à espérer si nous ne remplissons pas les conditions de notre salut. Une fois que nous recevons le Seigneur Jésus comme Sauveur, alors « l’espérance ne fait pas honte » (Romains 5:5).

À mesure que Christ devient vivant en nous, nous L’aimons et choisissons de Lui obéir. Jésus devient plus précieux pour nous à mesure que nous mûrissons dans notre vie chrétienne. À mesure que notre relation grandit, notre attente grandit aussi. Plus nous Le connaissons, plus nous attendons d’être en Sa présence. À mesure que notre anticipation de Le voir augmente, nous essayons de faire tout ce qui est possible pour Lui plaire. Notre grand empressement nous empêche de nous lasser, ainsi, « nous sommes sauvés par l’espérance. »

Votre espérance est‑elle comme celle de celui qui « monte par quelque autre chemin », ou comme celle de « celui qui entre par la porte » ? Avez‑vous une base pour votre espérance ou est‑ce une espérance vide qui n’a aucun fondement ?

Je confie que vous grandissez « … en toutes choses vers celui qui est la tête, c’est‑à‑dire Christ » (Éphésiens 4:15).

J’espère que vous pourrez grandir encore un peu, afin que votre attente de voir Christ augmente également. Le témoignage de cette attente est : « … dans cette espérance aussi nous soupirons, désirant ardemment être revêtus de notre habitation, qui est du ciel » (2 Corinthiens 5:2).

Prayer lays hold of God's plan and becomes the link between His will and its accomplishment on earth. Amazing things happen, and we are given the privilege of being the channels of the Holy Spirit's prayer.

—Elisabeth Elliot

In May 2001, God blessed our family with a baby girl. This baby created a lot of excitement as the news flew like wildfire. “Did you hear Ivans have a girl?” Her only sister was 14 years old, and the last five babies had been boys. Such a special baby deserved a special name. We named her Judith Irene after her grandmother and called her Judy for short.

The first 24 hours after birth, Judy grunted and squawked almost continuously. “She is disgruntled about being born,” I joked. After that first day she settled into a normal baby routine with no sign of anything unordinary.

One morning when Judy was about 18 months old, I was in the living room having my personal devotions. She was in the adjoining kitchen when we heard an odd noise—a rhythmical scratch-thunk. I looked quizzically at Ivan. “What is that noise?” With raised eyebrows, he shrugged his shoulders. When the sounds continued, I got curious enough to heft myself out of my rocking chair and trudge toward the source of the sounds. An uneasy suspicion reared its head in the back of my mind and grew with every step I took. When I entered the kitchen, Judy lay on the floor, jerking rhythmically. I had never seen anyone in a seizure before, but somehow, I just knew. She’s having a seizure!

“Shall we call 911?” Ivan headed toward the phone. I debated. Since Ivan was a firefighter, we had an emergency scanner in the house. After hearing countless calls over the years and knowing it could sometimes take the ambulance a while to respond, I wasn't at rest waiting at home while our daughter was seizing.

“Let’s take her in.” I wasn’t willing to sit there and wait until help arrived.

Judy was still jerking. Ivan scooped her off the floor and handed her to me so he could get his keys. Holding Judy close, I headed for the door. “Bring my shoes,” I called over my shoulder as I hurried stocking-footed down the porch steps and toward the pickup truck parked in the lower driveway. Ivan passed me up, opened the door for me, and ran around to the driver’s side. Coming down the short, steep hill, my feet slipped in the morning dew, and I landed halfway under the truck with one leg forward and the other one bent back under me. For an instant, I thought I had broken my leg, but after a stunned second or two, I got to my feet, gathered my precious burden, and struggled into the pickup. Judy was still jerking and, worse yet, was no longer breathing properly. Saliva pooled in the corners of her mouth, turning into foam. Oh my baby! What is wrong with her? Is she going to die?! It’s amazing how many thoughts can run through your mind in a situation like this. Why, oh why doesn’t Ivan drive faster? She’s not breathing! I glanced over at the speedometer. It was pointed hard right. Oh, he was driving fast. With my whole body and mind, I willed us to be at the hospital.

We had a straight drive to the hospital, and Ivan pulled right up to the emergency entrance. I jumped out of the truck with my baby, yelled over my shoulder to bring my shoes along in, and ran for the emergency door. A nurse was just coming around the corner and I all but threw my precious baby into her startled arms. “She’s having a seizure!” I squeaked out. The nurse took one look at Judy, turned, and rushed down the hall with me at her heels. By the time we got into a room, Judy had finally stopped seizing. As she lay on the stretcher, semi-comatose, she went into a second, milder seizure.

Once she came out of the second seizure and things calmed down, the doctor ordered some tests. After reviewing the test results, the doctor decided she had experienced a febrile seizure, one that results from body temperature moving up or down too rapidly. He said they were common in babies and young children and didn’t seem too concerned. My mothering instincts questioned his diagnosis, but I was no doctor so we went with what he said.

This was our introduction to the world of seizures. A few weeks later she had another seizure. And then another. Our parents encouraged us to get a second opinion. This second doctor decided that Judy should have an MRI, even though the first doctor still maintained that she was just having febrile seizures and wasn’t in any hurry to do the MRI. Several weeks passed until they worked her into the schedule. The day after the MRI, we got a call from the doctor’s office. An appointment with a neurosurgeon had been made for two days later. The situation had changed from “no hurry” to “you will be there, no questions asked”. The neurosurgeon said Judy had an AVM and tried to explain what that was, but most of the information soared right over my head. An appointment for an angiogram was scheduled, and explanations of procedures and requirements for us as her parents were added to my spinning brain. As I tried to digest all the information I was receiving in one phone call, I realized they were preparing for the possibility of surgery.

Our prayers were getting more earnest as we progressed through an EEG (brain scan looking for seizure activity) and more doctor visits. We desired healing for our baby so she could live a normal life. Our faith in God came into play as we tried to resign ourselves to His will. Friends, family, and acquaintances all joined us in prayer.

We owned a bulk food store, and many local non-Mennonite folks knew us. We had become good friends with some Christians from a local church. When they heard of the circumstances, they asked if they could have a prayer meeting to lay hands on Judy and pray for her healing. Although the church we attended did not generally do this, we appreciated their sincerity and faith in God, so we agreed to it.

The evening came when we gathered at their church with their pastor and some of the members who knew us. They took turns praying and claimed God’s healing for Judy because they “knew” it was His will to heal her. They specifically asked that the doctors wouldn’t find anything when they did the angiogram. Then they asked us to pray. Although not used to praying out loud, particularly in front of other people, we had confidence that God could heal our baby and wanted to do our part. We prayed for God’s will and voiced our acceptance of whatever He chose.

The next day, we made the hour-and-a-half drive to Madison Children’s Hospital for the angiogram. The purpose for this test was to identify what was causing her seizures and to find its exact location. After the test, we went home to await the results.

I didn’t want my lack of faith to block my daughter’s healing, and I knew God could heal her, but who was I to tell Him what to do? As I struggled through it, we waited for news from the doctor.

Two days later we got a phone call from the doctor’s office. The nurse on the line told us the angiogram hadn’t shown anything! It seemed to puzzle them. It wasn’t at all what they had expected, and they didn’t understand why they couldn’t find the problem. Praise God! We marveled at the miracle He had wrought.

When we took Judy to her next appointment with the neurosurgeon, I asked him what Judy’s problem was since the angiogram found nothing unusual. He said it appeared she had a small amount of bleeding on her brain, but not to worry about it. I thought that was one of the strangest statements I ever heard. I had always been under the impression that bleeding on the brain is very serious and not to be ignored. But I was pretty sure I knew what had happened and told the doctor about the prayers. His response was noncommittal, and I couldn’t tell what he really thought.

They scheduled Judy for a second doctor’s visit and MRI in six months, which I thought was a little strange, considering that they didn’t think there was anything wrong with her. I wasn’t planning to need that MRI or appointment since I believed God had healed her.

That summer, we weaned her off her seizure medications, and she appeared to be healthy. The six months were almost over, and we believed her problems were behind us.

Then, one week before the scheduled MRI, she had a seizure. What a shock! How could this be? Hadn’t God healed her?? What was happening? I felt betrayed. All I could ask was, “Why?” And now what were we going to do?

Such emotional turmoil and soul-searching! I felt let down and shaken in my faith. I had believed in God and that was finally where I ended up every time when I struggled. Solid as a rock under all the turmoil was the truth that God is, and His ways are far above my understanding. I found at the core of my belief in God a safe place where He knows and has my best interest in mind. And that plan might not include the things I want to happen in my limited earth-view.

What if His plan was higher? What if there was someone we would encounter through our medical journey who needed to see Christ in us? Were we willing to be His witness at the expense of our comfort and an easier life?

Our precious little girl ended up having brain surgery at only three and a half years old. Dealing with seizures, surgery, and countless tests over the years caused us no small amount of stress, but God had and still has a plan, and the “whys” we ask might not be revealed until we see Him face to face.

So, does God always answer prayer? I say yes, He does. Sometimes He says, “Yes,” and we get what we want; sometimes, His answer is“No,” and we do not get what we ask for. Sometimes, He whispers, “Wait”, and in His own time and way, He allows us our heart’s desire. Like a child who trusts his parents, I will leave the answers to my prayers in the hands of our almighty God and trust Him to know what is best for my life.

기도는 하나님의 계획을 붙들고 그분의 뜻과 땅에서 이루어지는 그 성취 사이를 잇는 고리가 된다. 놀라운 일이 일어나며 우리는 성령의 기도의 통로가 되는 특권을 받는다.

—Elisabeth Elliot

2001년 5월, 하나님께서 우리 가정에 아기 딸을 허락해 주셨습니다. 이 소식은 순식간에 퍼지며 큰 흥분을 불러일으켰습니다. “이반네 집에 딸이 났대?” 그녀의 유일한 여동생은 14세였고, 지난 다섯 명의 아기들은 모두 남자아이였습니다. 이렇게 특별한 아기에게는 특별한 이름이 어울렸습니다. 우리는 그녀를 할머니의 이름을 따서 Judith Irene이라 지었고, 줄여서 주디라고 불렀습니다.

출생 후 첫 24시간 동안 주디는 거의 계속해서 끙끙거리며 소리를 냈습니다. “태어난 것에 불만이 있나 보네,” 저는 농담 삼아 말했습니다. 그 첫날이 지나고 난 뒤에는 평범한 아기처럼 규칙적인 생활 패턴을 보였고 특별히 이상 징후는 보이지 않았습니다.

주디가 18개월 정도 되었을 무렵 어느 아침, 저는 거실에서 개인 기도 시간을 갖고 있었습니다. 그녀는 옆 주방에 있었는데 이상한 소리—리듬감 있는 긁는 소리와 탁 하는 소리—가 들렸습니다. 저는 이반을 힐끗 쳐다보았습니다. “그 소리 뭐지?” 그는 눈썹을 치켜올리며 어깨를 으쓱했습니다. 소리가 계속되자 저는 궁금해져 흔들의자에서 몸을 일으켜 소리 나는 쪽으로 걸어갔습니다. 마음 한구석에 불길한 의심이 스멀스멀 올라왔고 한 걸음 한 걸음 나아갈수록 그 의심은 커졌습니다. 주방에 들어섰을 때 주디는 바닥에 누워 규칙적으로 경련을 일으키고 있었습니다. 저는 이전에 경련을 일으키는 사람을 본 적이 없었지만, 왠지 알 수 있었습니다. 그녀가 경련을 일으키고 있구나!

“911에 전화할까?” 이반이 전화 쪽으로 향했습니다. 저는 망설였습니다. 이반이 소방관이었기 때문에 집에는 비상상황 스캐너가 있었습니다. 수년간 수많은 출동 호출을 들어왔고 구급차가 도착하는 데 시간이 걸릴 때가 있다는 것을 알고 있었기 때문에, 딸이 경련을 일으키는 동안 집에서 안절부절하며 기다리는 것은 마음이 편치 않았습니다.

“데려가자.” 저는 도움을 기다리며 그 자리에 앉아있을 수 없었습니다.

주디는 여전히 경련을 일으키고 있었습니다. 이반이 그녀를 바닥에서 번쩍 들어 저에게 건네주고는 열쇠를 가지러 갔습니다. 주디를 꼭 안고 현관으로 향했습니다. “내 신발 가져와!”라고 등 뒤로 외치며 맨발로 현관 계단을 성급히 내려가 차고에 주차된 픽업 트럭 쪽으로 달렸습니다. 이반이 저를 제치고 앞서가 문을 열어주고 운전석으로 돌아갔습니다. 짧고 가파른 언덕을 내려오던 중 아침 이슬에 발이 미끄러져 한쪽 다리는 앞으로 쭉 뻗고 다른 쪽 다리는 뒤로 구부린 채 트럭 밑으로 반쯤 기어들어가는 듯 넘어졌습니다. 순간 다리가 부러진 줄 알았지만, 멍해진 채로 잠시 있다가 일어나 소중한 아이를 다시 품에 안고 힘겹게 트럭에 올라탔습니다. 주디는 여전히 몸을 떨고 있었고, 더 나쁜 건 호흡이 제대로 되지 않는다는 점이었습니다. 입가에 침이 고여 거품으로 변해가고 있었습니다. 아, 내 아기! 무슨 일이지? 죽는 건 아닐까?! 그런 상황에서 얼마나 많은 생각이 머릿속을 스쳐 지나가는지 놀랍습니다. 왜, 왜 이반은 더 빨리 운전하지 않는 거지? 숨을 쉬지 않아! 계기판을 힐끗 보니 바늘이 오른쪽 끝을 가리키고 있었습니다. 아, 그는 빠르게 운전하고 있었구나. 온몸과 마음을 다해 우리는 병원에 도착하기를 간절히 바랐습니다.

우리는 병원까지 곧장 달려갔고 이반은 응급실 입구 바로 앞에 차를 세웠습니다. 저는 아기를 안고 차에서 뛰어내려 신발을 가져오라고 등 뒤로 소리치고 응급실 문을 향해 달려갔습니다. 간호사가 모퉁이를 돌아오고 있었고 저는 거의 소중한 아기를 그녀의 놀란 팔에 던져 넘겼습니다. “경련을 일으켜요!” 하고 저는 깔깔거리며 말했습니다. 간호사는 주디를 한 번 보더니 저를 이끌고 복도를 달려가더니 곧바로 방으로 들어갔습니다. 방에 들어갔을 때쯤 주디의 경련은 마침내 멈췄습니다. 들것에 누워 반혼수 상태인 그녀는 두 번째로 더 가벼운 경련을 일으켰습니다.

두 번째 경련이 끝나고 상황이 진정되자 의사는 몇 가지 검사를 지시했습니다. 검사 결과를 검토한 후 의사는 체온이 너무 빠르게 오르내리는 것에서 비롯되는 열성 경련이라고 진단했습니다. 그는 이것이 아기들과 어린이들에게 흔하며 크게 걱정할 상황은 아니라고 말했습니다. 어머니로서의 직감은 그의 진단에 의문을 제기했지만, 저는 의사가 아니었기에 그의 말에 따르기로 했습니다.

이것이 우리가 경련의 세계에 들어온 첫 경험이었습니다. 몇 주 후 또다시 경련을 일으켰고 그 뒤로도 또 다른 경련이 있었습니다. 부모님들은 우리가 다른 의견을 구하도록 권했습니다. 두 번째 의사는 주디에게 MRI를 받아야 한다고 결정했는데, 첫 번째 의사는 계속해서 그것이 단지 열성 경련일 뿐이라며 MRI를 서두르지 않았습니다. 몇 주가 지나 겨우 일정을 잡아 MRI를 받았습니다. MRI 다음 날, 병원에서 전화가 왔습니다. 이틀 뒤에 신경외과 의사 진료가 잡혔다는 것이었습니다. “서두르지 않아도 된다”던 상황이 “무조건 오셔야 합니다”로 바뀐 것입니다. 신경외과 의사는 주디에게 AVM(동정맥 기형)이 있다고 말했고 그게 무엇인지 설명하려 했지만 대부분의 설명은 제 머리를 스치고 지나갔습니다. 혈관 조영술(angiogram) 예약이 잡혔고, 시술과 부모로서 우리가 알아야 할 사항들에 대한 설명이 제 어지러운 머리에 더해졌습니다. 한 통의 전화로 쏟아지는 정보를 소화하려 애쓰면서 그들은 수술 가능성에 대비하고 있음을 깨달았습니다.

EEG(뇌파 검사)를 비롯해 여러 번의 진료를 거치면서 우리의 기도는 더욱 간절해졌습니다. 우리는 아기가 정상적인 삶을 살 수 있도록 치유되기를 간구했습니다. 하나님의 뜻에 우리의 마음을 맡기려 애쓰며 우리의 믿음이 발휘되었습니다. 친구와 가족, 지인들이 함께 기도해 주었습니다.

우리는 벌크 식품점을 운영했고 많은 지역 비-메노나이트 사람들이 우리를 알았습니다. 지역 교회의 몇몇 기독교인들과도 친분이 생겼습니다. 그들이 사정을 들었을 때 주디에게 안수하고 그녀의 치유를 위해 기도 모임을 가져도 되겠느냐고 물었습니다. 우리가 다니는 교회에서는 일반적으로 그런 모임을 하지 않았지만, 그들의 성의와 하나님에 대한 믿음을 고맙게 여겨 동의했습니다.

그날 저녁 우리는 그들의 목사님과 우리를 아는 교인 몇 명과 함께 교회에 모였습니다. 그들은 차례로 기도하며 주디의 치유를 하나님께서 원하신다고 확신했습니다. 그들은 특히 혈관 조영술을 했을 때 의사들이 아무것도 발견하지 못하기를 기도했습니다. 그리고 우리에게도 기도해 달라고 요청했습니다. 다른 사람들 앞에서 소리 내어 기도하는 것에 익숙지 않았지만, 우리는 하나님께서 우리 아기를 치유하실 수 있다는 확신이 있었고 우리의 몫을 하고 싶었습니다. 우리는 하나님의 뜻을 위해 기도했고 그분이 택하시는 것에 순복함을 표현했습니다.

다음 날 우리는 혈관 조영술을 위해 매디슨 소아 병원까지 1시간 반을 운전해 갔습니다. 이 검사의 목적은 무엇이 그녀의 경련을 유발하는지, 그리고 그것의 정확한 위치를 확인하는 것이었습니다. 검사 후 우리는 결과를 기다리기 위해 집으로 돌아왔습니다.

저는 제 믿음의 부족이 딸의 치유를 막지 않기를 바랐고, 하나님께서 치유하실 수 있다는 것을 알았지만 제가 감히 그분께 무엇을 하라고 명령할 수는 없었습니다. 그렇게 갈등하며 우리는 의사의 소식을 기다렸습니다.

이틀 후 병원에서 전화가 왔습니다. 전화받은 간호사는 혈관 조영술에서 아무것도 보이지 않았다고 전했습니다! 그들은 당혹스러워하는 듯했습니다. 전혀 예상치 못한 결과였고, 왜 문제를 찾지 못했는지 이해하지 못하겠다는 말이었습니다. 하나님을 찬양했습니다! 우리는 하나님께서 베푸신 기적에 놀라워했습니다.

다음 신경외과 진료 때 주디의 문제는 무엇이었느냐고 의사에게 물었습니다. 의사는 소량의 뇌출혈이 있는 것으로 보이지만 걱정할 정도는 아니라고 했습니다. 저는 그것이 정말 이상한 말이라고 생각했습니다. 저는 항상 뇌출혈은 매우 심각한 것이고 무시할 수 없는 문제라고 알고 있었습니다. 하지만 저는 기도 덕분에 무슨 일이 있었던 것 같다고 의사에게 말했습니다. 그의 반응은 애매모호했고 그가 실제로 어떻게 생각하는지는 알 수 없었습니다.

그들은 여섯 달 후에 다시 진료와 MRI를 예약했습니다. 저는 아무 문제가 없다고 생각했기 때문에 그 여섯 달 뒤의 MRI나 약속이 조금 이상하게 느껴졌습니다. 저는 하나님께서 이미 그녀를 고쳐주셨다고 믿었기에 그 MRI나 진료가 필요하지 않을 것이라고 생각했습니다.

그해 여름 우리는 항경련제를 끊였고 그녀는 건강해 보였습니다. 여섯 달이 거의 지나갈 무렵 우리는 그녀의 문제가 끝났다고 믿었습니다.

그런데 예정된 MRI 일주일 전, 그녀가 또다시 경련을 일으켰습니다. 얼마나 충격적이었는지요! 어떻게 이럴 수 있지? 하나님께서 고쳐주지 않으셨나? 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는 거지? 저는 배신당한 기분이 들었습니다. 저는 그저 “왜?”라고 물을 수밖에 없었습니다. 그리고 이제 우리는 무엇을 해야 할까요?

정서적 격동과 자기 성찰의 연속이었습니다. 저는 실망했고 제 믿음은 흔들렸습니다. 제가 고난 속에서 항상 도달하는 마지막 지점은 하나님을 믿는 것이었습니다. 모든 혼란 속에서도 반석처럼 굳건한 진리는 하나님은 존재하시며 그분의 길은 제 이해를 훨씬 뛰어넘는다는 사실이었습니다. 저는 제 믿음의 핵심에서 하나님이 알고 계시고 제 유익을 최우선으로 여긴다는 안전한 장소를 발견했습니다. 그리고 그분의 계획은 제한된 제 지상 관점에서 바라는 것들을 포함하지 않을 수도 있습니다.

혹시 그분의 계획이 더 높을 수는 없을까? 의료 여정 중 만나는 누군가가 우리를 통해 그리스도를 보아야 할 필요가 있을 수도 있지 않을까? 우리가 안락함과 더 쉬운 삶을 대가로 그분의 증인이 되는 것을 기꺼이 받아들이겠는가?

우리의 소중한 어린 딸은 겨우 세 살 반 때 뇌 수술을 받았습니다. 그간 수년 동안 경련과 수술, 수많은 검사를 겪으면서 우리에게는 적지 않은 스트레스가 있었지만, 하나님은 한결같이 계획을 가지고 계셨고 우리가 묻는 여러 “왜”에 대한 답은 아마도 그분을 얼굴로 뵈올 때까지 드러나지 않을 것입니다.

그렇다면 하나님은 항상 기도에 응답하시는가? 저는 그렇다고 말합니다. 때로는 그분이 “예”라고 말씀하셔서 우리가 원하는 것을 얻게 하십니다; 때로는 그분의 대답은 “아니오”여서 우리가 구한 것을 얻지 못합니다. 때로는 그분이 속삭이듯 “기다려라”라고 하시고, 그분의 때와 방식으로 우리의 마음 소원을 허락하십니다. 부모를 신뢰하는 아이처럼 저는 기도에 대한 응답을 전능하신 하나님의 손에 맡기고 제 삶에 무엇이 최선인지 아시는 그분을 신뢰하겠습니다.

Just reading the title probably brings negative thoughts to your mind. We as humans don’t typically like to be told “no” because it goes against our nature. Sometimes we bring the “no” upon ourselves because of disobedience, such as when God said “no” to Moses. “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land . . . But the Lord . . . would not hear me: and the Lord said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter” (Deuteronomy 3:25,26).

In Deuteronomy 1:42, God said “no” to Israel. “And the Lord said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies”, but they rebelled at His “no.” “And ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you” (Deuteronomy 1:45).

God said “no” to Paul. “And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me” (2 Corinthians 12:7-9).

Let us focus our attention upon prayerful Paul’s acceptance of God’s “no.”

First, acceptance does not mean that the problem does not exist. Paul accepted God’s “no”, but still had the infirmities.

Second, acceptance does not mean woeful resignation. Paul “besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.” We should be persistent, even when God’s answer is not forthcoming. (cf. Luke 18:1-8).

Third, God’s “no” may be necessary to avoid a greater evil or infirmity. Twice, Paul says the thorn in the flesh was given “lest I should be exalted above measure.” Unlike Paul, however, we may not know the purpose for God’s “no,” but we can be assured of His faithfulness and goodness. With Paul, we too may have to endure one thing, which means accepting God’s refusal in order to achieve a higher purpose or benefit.

Fourth, Paul’s weakness, as a result of God’s “no,” made him strong. “Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10). The sorrow and suffering some endure has indeed made them strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.

Fifth, Paul’s infirmity allowed the power of Christ to rest upon him. God’s strength was complete, sufficient, and made perfect in weakness. Paul’s strength was seen to be of God. Therefore, Christ, not Paul, was glorified. The infirmities that Paul endured revealed the power not of himself but of God.

Sixth, God explained his answer of “no” by saying, “My grace is sufficient for thee.” God’s love and acceptance of us, His strength and power to assist us in our infirmities and with our weaknesses, is sufficient and complete.

Seventh, Paul gloried in his infirmities, but only after he accepted God’s “no.” Paul ultimately saw that this allowed God’s power to rest upon him. Paul’s weakness displayed and magnified divine power in a manner that human adequacy and personal sufficiency could never accomplish.

Eighth, unfortunately for him, Paul was the vessel, the sufferer, who had to endure afflictions that God’s grace, power, and glory might be truly reflected, but he was glad to bear it for those purposes (cf. 2 Co 4:7-11; Gal 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Until we are ready to do the same, we cannot accept or understand God’s “no.”

A “no” may come into our life for many various reasons.

When God says, “No,” the Christian must remember:

That God will do right. “He is … a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he” (Deuteronomy 32:4). One may not see; he may not, as Job did not, understand, but God will do right. “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” (Genesis 18:25).

That God’s ways are not ours. “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts” (Isaiah 55:8,9). God sees the end from the beginning. Nothing is hidden from him. “Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it” (Psalms 139:6). as a little child cries in protest when his mother pulls him from the road (It is such a great place to ride a tricycle!), so we may cry when God says, “No,” but He, like the child’s parent, knows danger the child may not be able to comprehend or appreciate fully.

That prayer has a chief purpose. Prayer should not be an attempt to manipulate the will of God. “Not my will, but thine, be done,” the suffering Savior cried, but when God says, “No,” we often forget that fact and complain in effect, “Not Thy will but mine be done.” Perhaps the supreme purpose of prayer is to seek God’s will for our lives, our wants, our needs, and our desires. It will help to remember that when God says “no.”

That a present “no” may be a “yes” in development. Paul was told that he was going to Rome (Acts 19:21; 23:11). But the bars of incarceration, the shackles of servitude, and the jaws of death seemed to say otherwise. Two years of confinement were not convincing evidence of a trip to Rome, nor was a hopeless sea voyage (Acts 24:27; 27:20). However, as we all know, Paul went to Rome (Acts 28:16)!

That God’s laws prevail. The laws of nature are laws of God. God does not will that one to fall off a cliff, but if certain physical laws are broken, he will. God has biological laws. Disease may be contracted, and suffering and death may follow. One may pray, “Give us this day our daily bread,” but if he does not use God’s laws to procure it, or if he contradicts God’s means of acquiring it, he will not receive it. As painful as it is to accept, we frequently are victims of earthly laws in the various and diverse orders of physical life. Of course, the reverse is also true. We often are blessed by the material laws of God (Matthew 5:45; Acts 14:17; 1 Timothy 5:23).

In conclusion, Job of old bore the lashes of unparalleled human calamity and agony and torture of mind, body, and soul. His faithfulness and steadfast endurance have blessed thirty centuries of sorrowing humanity. Stephen and James met untimely, violent deaths (Acts 7; 12). They died when we would have had them to live. By their suffering and death, the early disciples were shown the power of the new faith, that men could die and yet live in victory. Hence, multiplied millions have been emboldened and have accepted torture and death rather than denounce their faith and hope of eternal life.

Deliverance came. No, not to Stephen and James, nor to suffering servants such as Job, of like precious faith, but it came in unquenchable hope, in the hope that maketh not ashamed. It came through Him that is able to deliver us who, through fear of death, were subject to bondage. “Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.”

Solo leer el título probablemente trae pensamientos negativos a tu mente. Como humanos, por lo general no nos gusta que nos digan “no” porque va en contra de nuestra naturaleza. A veces atraemos el “no” sobre nosotros mismos por desobediencia, como cuando Dios le dijo “no” a Moisés. “Te ruego que me dejes pasar y ver la buena tierra . . . Pero Jehová . . . no me oyó; y Jehová me dijo: Bástate; no me hables más de esto” (Deuteronomio 3:25,26).

En Deuteronomio 1:42, Dios dijo “no” a Israel. “Y Jehová me dijo: Diles: No subáis, ni peleeis; porque yo no estoy en medio de vosotros; no sea que se os hiera delante de vuestros enemigos”, pero ellos se rebelaron a su “no”. “Y volvisteis y llorasteis delante de Jehová; mas Jehová no oyó vuestra voz, ni puso atención en vosotros” (Deuteronomio 1:45).

Dios dijo “no” a Pablo. “Y para que yo no me enaltezca sobremanera por la excelencia de las revelaciones, se me dio una espina en la carne, un mensajero de Satanás que me abofeteara, para que no me enaltezca sobremanera. Por esto, tres veces rogué al Señor que se apartase de mí. Y me ha dicho: Bástate mi gracia; porque mi poder se perfecciona en la debilidad. Por tanto, de buena gana me gloriaré más bien en mis debilidades, para que repose sobre mí el poder de Cristo” (2 Corintios 12:7-9).

Centremos nuestra atención en la aceptación del “no” de Dios por parte del orante Pablo.

Primero, aceptar no significa que el problema no exista. Pablo aceptó el “no” de Dios, pero aun así tuvo las infirmedades.

Segundo, aceptar no significa resignación afligida. Pablo “rogó al Señor tres veces que se apartase de mí.” Debemos ser persistentes, aun cuando la respuesta de Dios no llegue de inmediato. (cf. Lucas 18:1-8).

Tercero, el “no” de Dios puede ser necesario para evitar un mal o una infirmedad mayor. Dos veces, Pablo dice que la espina en la carne fue dada “para que no me enalteciera sobremanera.” Sin embargo, a diferencia de Pablo, quizá no sepamos el propósito del “no” de Dios, pero podemos estar seguros de su fidelidad y bondad. Con Pablo, también nosotros tal vez tengamos que soportar una cosa, lo que significa aceptar la negativa de Dios para alcanzar un propósito o beneficio superior.

Cuarto, la debilidad de Pablo, como resultado del “no” de Dios, lo hizo fuerte. “Por tanto, por amor a Cristo me gozo en las debilidades, en afrentas, en necesidades, en persecuciones, en angustias; porque cuando soy débil, entonces soy fuerte” (2 Corintios 12:10). El dolor y el sufrimiento que algunos soportan en verdad los ha hecho fuertes en el Señor y en el poder de su fuerza.

Quinto, la infirmedad de Pablo permitió que el poder de Cristo reposara sobre él. La fortaleza de Dios fue completa, suficiente y se perfeccionó en la debilidad. La fuerza de Pablo quedó vista como perteneciente a Dios. Por tanto, fue Cristo, no Pablo, quien fue glorificado. Las infirmedades que Pablo soportó revelaron el poder no de él mismo sino de Dios.

Sexto, Dios explicó su respuesta de “no” diciendo: “Bástate mi gracia.” El amor y la aceptación de Dios hacia nosotros, su fuerza y su poder para ayudarnos en nuestras infirmedades y debilidades, es suficiente y completo.

Séptimo, Pablo se glorió en sus infirmedades, pero solo después de aceptar el “no” de Dios. Pablo vio en última instancia que esto permitía que el poder de Dios reposara sobre él. La debilidad de Pablo mostró y magnificó el poder divino de una manera que la suficiencia humana y la capacidad personal nunca podrían lograr.

Octavo, desafortunadamente para él, Pablo fue el vasija, el que sufrió, que tuvo que soportar aflicciones para que la gracia, el poder y la gloria de Dios pudieran reflejarse verdaderamente, pero él estuvo contento de soportarlo con esos propósitos (cf. 2 Co 4:7-11; Gal 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Hasta que estemos dispuestos a hacer lo mismo, no podremos aceptar ni entender el “no” de Dios.

Un “no” puede entrar en nuestra vida por muchas razones diversas.

Cuando Dios dice “No”, el cristiano debe recordar:

Que Dios hará lo correcto. “El es … un Dios de verdad y sin iniquidad, justo y recto es él” (Deuteronomio 32:4). Uno puede no ver; puede no entender, como Job no entendió, pero Dios hará lo justo. “¿No hará el Juez de toda la tierra lo que es justo?” (Génesis 18:25).

Que los caminos de Dios no son los nuestros. “Porque mis pensamientos no son vuestros pensamientos, ni vuestros caminos mis caminos, dijo Jehová. Como son más altos los cielos que la tierra, así son mis caminos más altos que vuestros caminos, y mis pensamientos más que vuestros pensamientos” (Isaías 55:8,9). Dios ve el fin desde el principio. Nada le es oculto. “¡Cuán insondables son tus pensamientos para mí; cuán difícil es entenderlos!” (Salmos 139:6). Así como un niño pequeño llora en protesta cuando su madre lo aparta de la calle (¡Es un lugar tan bueno para andar en triciclo!), así podemos llorar cuando Dios dice “No”, pero Él, como el padre del niño, conoce el peligro que el niño puede no comprender o apreciar por completo.

Que la oración tiene un propósito principal. La oración no debe ser un intento de manipular la voluntad de Dios. “No se haga mi voluntad, sino la tuya,” clamó el Salvador sufriente, pero cuando Dios dice “No”, a menudo olvidamos ese hecho y nos quejamos en efecto: “No tu voluntad sino la mía.” Quizá el propósito supremo de la oración sea buscar la voluntad de Dios para nuestras vidas, nuestros deseos, nuestras necesidades y nuestras aspiraciones. Será útil recordarlo cuando Dios diga “no”.

Que un “no” presente puede ser un “sí” en desarrollo. A Pablo se le dijo que iba a ir a Roma (Hechos 19:21; 23:11). Pero las rejas de la incarceración, las cadenas de la servidumbre y las fauces de la muerte parecían decir lo contrario. Dos años de confinamiento no eran prueba convincente de un viaje a Roma, ni lo fue un viaje marítimo sin esperanza (Hechos 24:27; 27:20). ¡Sin embargo, como todos sabemos, Pablo llegó a Roma (Hechos 28:16)!

Que las leyes de Dios prevalecen. Las leyes de la naturaleza son leyes de Dios. Dios no quiere que uno se caiga de un precipicio, pero si se violan ciertas leyes físicas, caerá. Dios tiene leyes biológicas. Se puede contraer una enfermedad, y seguir sufrimiento y muerte. Uno puede orar: “Danos hoy nuestro pan cotidiano,” pero si no usa las leyes de Dios para procurarlo, o si contradice los medios que Dios ha provisto para obtenerlo, no lo recibirá. Por doloroso que sea aceptarlo, con frecuencia somos víctimas de leyes terrenales en los diversos y múltiples órdenes de la vida física. Por supuesto, lo contrario también es cierto. Con frecuencia somos bendecidos por las leyes materiales de Dios (Mateo 5:45; Hechos 14:17; 1 Timoteo 5:23).

En conclusión, Job de antaño soportó los azotes de calamidad humana sin igual y la agonía y tortura de mente, cuerpo y alma. Su fidelidad y resistencia constante han bendecido a treinta siglos de humanidad afligida. Esteban y Santiago encontraron muertes violentas e inoportunas (Hechos 7; 12). Murieron cuando nos hubiera gustado que vivieran. Por su sufrimiento y muerte, a los primeros discípulos se les mostró el poder de la nueva fe: que los hombres podían morir y aun así vivir en victoria. Por tanto, millones multiplicados se han envalentonado y han aceptado la tortura y la muerte antes que renunciar a su fe y a la esperanza de vida eterna.

La liberación llegó. No, no para Esteban y Santiago, ni para siervos sufrientes como Job, de igual preciosa fe, pero sí vino en esperanza inextinguible, en la esperanza que no avergüenza. Llegó por medio de Aquel que puede librarnos, nosotros que por miedo a la muerte estábamos sujetos a esclavitud. “Gracias a Dios por su don inefable.”

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

아담과 하와가 그들의 창조주와 함께 매일 누리던 것은 전형적인 의미의 “완벽한 세계”였습니다. 하나님 자신이 설계하시고 창조하시며 직접 손으로 심으신 아름다운 동산은 모든 면에서 완전했습니다. 그러나 그것이 오래가지 못했다는 것은 우리 모두 잘 알고 있습니다. 하나님께서 인류 모두에게 주신 선택의 특권 때문에, 두 사람은 곧 잘못된 선택을 했습니다. 하와는 뱀의 형태로 온 사탄에게 속았지만 그 거짓말을 믿고 하나님께서 사랑으로 금하신 유일한 일을 행하여 불순종하기로 선택했습니다. 그러나 그녀가 그 열매를 아담에게 가져갔을 때, 아담은 속지 않았습니다. 그는 그것이 잘못된 것임을 알았습니다. 하나님은 놀라지 않으셨지만, 그럼에도 매우 실망하셨습니다. 창세기 3장에서 우리는 인류가 동산에서 쫓겨나고 생명나무에서 차단되며 아담과 하와의 죄 때문에 저주가 선포되는 슬픈 기록을 읽습니다. 모든 것이 매우 어둡고 절망적으로 보였습니다. 단 한 사람의 범죄였지만, 저주는 땅과 식물과 동물을 포함한 모든 피조물에게도 미쳤습니다. 이 강력한 저주와 함께 온 모든 것을 함께 생각해 보십시오.

  2. 고난과 고통
  3. 황폐와 파괴
  4. 가시와 엉겅퀴 같은 특정 식물의 우세
  5. 죽음
  6. 분해와 부패

오늘 우리는 이것들을 저주의 여섯 가지 "D"로 부르겠습니다.

질병

영원하고 완전한 건강의 세계는 지나갔습니다. 질병은 죄의 저주의 일부로 들어왔습니다. 인간의 자손들과 새들과 짐승들, 식물들 모두 병과 질병의 영향을 경험하기 시작할 것입니다. 그러나 하나님은 청결과 단순한 순종으로 많은 예방 가능한 병을 피하는 방법을 사람이 알도록 지침을 주심으로 신실하셨습니다. 예를 들어, 결혼에 대한 하나님의 원래 의도를 존중하라는 명령, 순결을 유지하라는 명령, 여러 잠재적 질병을 피하라는 명령 등이 그것입니다. 하나님은 또한 우리의 영적 상태에 관심을 가지셨습니다. 하나님은 인류가 죄책을 지도록 디자인하지 않으셨습니다. 그는 우리가 양심을 깨끗이 유지하기를 원하십니다. 죄책감 있는 양심은 사람을 병들게 할 수 있음을 그분은 아십니다!

이들 가운데 일부 질병은 피할 수 없겠지만, 많은 것들은 면역력을 쌓음으로써 예방될 수 있습니다. 하나님은 사람과 식물과 동물을 재생 가능한 마이크로바이옴(수십억의 유익한 박테리아)과 체계적인 면역체계로 만드심으로 신실하셨습니다. 이것은 우리가 질병과 싸우는 데 도움이 됩니다. 각 식물들이 특정한 영양적 또는 치유적 속성을 가진 것처럼 보이는 것이 놀랍습니다. 얼마나 신실하신 창조주인지요!

고난과 고통

나는 에덴 동산에서 실제적인 고통의 이유가 없었다고 생각합니다만, 우리는 그들이 떠난 날 이후로 계속해서 고통을 경험해 왔습니다. 고통은 분명 우리 삶의 많은 부분을 차지합니다. 고통의 유형은 다양합니다. 슬픔, 비애, 그리고 거절은 모두 저주와 함께 오는 감정적 고통입니다. 두통, 편두통, 근육통, 인대 파열, 건 감염, 마모된 관절, 골절 등은 우리가 마지막 숨을 거두기 전에 때때로 경험할 수 있는 신체적 고통의 몇 가지 예입니다. 다시 말하지만, 하나님은 삶의 고통과 고난을 덜어주는 방법을 이해하도록 인류를 도우심으로 신실하셨습니다. 고대부터 식물, 약초 및 다른 치료법들이 사람들의 고통과 고난을 다루는 데 도움을 주었습니다. 오늘날에도 우리는 고통을 돕는 많은 유용한 식물들을 가지고 있습니다.

지구상에서 경험할 수 있는 가장 아름다운 것들 중 하나는 아이의 탄생입니다. 그러나 출산은 일반적으로 많은 고통을 동반합니다. 이 약속된 고통을 완전히 제거할 수는 없었지만, 하나님은 출산 전·중·후에 고통을 완화하고 회복을 촉진하기 위해 사용할 수 있는 많은 약초의 사용을 제공하고 계시고 계시다는 사실을 신실하게 보여 주셨습니다. 하나님은 우리를 위해 그렇게 하실 필요가 없으셨습니다. 인류는 진정으로 자비를 받을 자격이 없습니다. 참으로 은혜로우신 창조주십니다!

황폐와 파괴

이 원리가 작동하는 것을 보기 위해 역사를 많이 공부할 필요는 없습니다. 바람, 비, 그리고 태양은 많은 것들에 황폐화 효과를 줍니다. 침식된 냇가 제방이든, 강바닥에서 매끈하게 닳은 바위든, 바람에 쓰러진 나무든, 이들은 모두 파괴의 자연스러운 요소입니다. 여기에 인간이 식물과 동물과 토양과 서로에게 행한 일들을 더해 보십시오. 끔찍한 전쟁 중의 파괴적 결과이든 평화 때의 이기적이고 탐욕스러운 행태이든, 인간은 매우 파괴적인 존재입니다. 하나님은 인류에게 모든 창조물을 다스리는 권세를 주셨습니다. 그러나 우리는 너무 자주 그것을 우리가 이 지구를 소유하며 원하는 대로 해도 된다는 잘못된 해석으로 받아들입니다. “땅은 여호와의 것”이라고 선언하신 분은 인간이 하나님의 피조물의 청지기가 아니라는 생각에 동의하지 않으십니다. 창조된 세계나 그 안의 어떤 것을 숭배하는 것은 확실히 사악합니다. 그러나 창조주께서 만드신 것에 감사하지 않고 부주의한 것도 똑같이 사악합니다! 그럼에도 불구하고, 하나님은 이 저주 속에서도 자기의 땅을 재생 가능한 능력으로 신실하게 설계하셨습니다. 우리의 은혜로우신 조물주를 찬양합시다!

가시와 엉겅퀴의 우세

정원 일을 해본 사람이라면 누구나 잡초와의 전투 현실을 곧 알게 됩니다. 공정하게 말하자면, 원치 않는 곳에 자라는 모든 식물은 “잡초”입니다. 많은 잡초는 우리가 그것을 어떻게 사용해야 하는지 알기만 하면 매우 유익한 식물일 수 있습니다. 우리가 잡초라고 부르는 일부 식물들은 어떤 것이 식용인지, 어떻게 조리해야 하는지를 이해하면 실제로 꽤 영양가 있고 건강합니다. 오늘은 가시와 엉겅퀴에 대해 생각해 보고자 합니다. 우리는 그것들이 저주가 선포된 이후에 생겨난 것이 아니라 처음 여섯 날에 창조되었다고 가정해야 합니다. 유용한 작물보다 더 잘 자라는 능력은 저주 이후에 증가한 것처럼 보입니다. 저주의 이 부분에서도 우리는 하나님께서 자비롭게 우리를 위해 공급하신 것을 봅니다.

아티초크는 소화를 돕는 쓴잎을 위해 재배합니다. 생각해 보십시오: 축복받은 엉겅퀴(Blessed Thistle), 밀크 시슬(Milk Thistle), 티슬(Teasel), 라즈베리 잎, 블랙베리 뿌리 등은 약용 및 다른 식용 이득을 위해 사용되는 이러한 “가시 잡초”의 몇 가지 예일 뿐입니다. 저주의 한가운데서도 우리에게 유익을 주신 하나님이 얼마나 선하신지요!

죽음

이것은 우리 대부분이 차마 이야기하고 싶어 하지 않는 하나의 “D”입니다. 실제로 우리가 첫 숨을 들이쉴 때, 우리는 죽음에 한 숨 더 가까워지는 것입니다. 모든 식물과 동물과 사람이 결국은 죽지만, 우리는 여전히 그것에 대해 편하지 않습니다. 살고자 하는 의지가 있는 것은 매우 정상적이며, 만약 그런 의지가 없다면 그 이유를 알아보기 위해 도움을 구해야 합니다.

실로 죽음은 나이를 가리지 않습니다. 내 평생 동안 나는 사산아의 장례를 돕기도 했고, 96세의 사람의 장례를 돕기도 했으며 그 사이의 모든 연령의 장례를 도왔습니다. 사도 요한이 요한계시록에서 묘사한 것처럼 회복된 아름다운 낙원을 우리는 읽습니다. 그가 언급한 것들 중에는 병이 없음, 슬픔 없음, 분리 없음, 눈물 없음, 더 이상 고통 없음, 그리고 죽음 없음이 있습니다. 어떤 면에서 삶은 영원을 위한 임신 기간에 불과합니다. 우리는 여기 머물 수 없습니다. 마치 태내의 아기가 현실 세계로 들어가고 싶지 않다고 결정할 수 없는 것처럼 말입니다. 모든 슬픔과 유혹 속에서 우리의 몸은 닳고 부패합니다. 모든 폭력과 죄와 악이 우리 주위에 있는 이 상태에 영원히 머물고 싶겠습니까? 오히려 우리는 우리가 만들어진 흙으로 돌아갑니다. 재에서 재로, 티끌에서 티끌로, 최후의 부활을 기다립니다. 하나님께서 죄악되고 죽어가는 상태의 인간이 현재의 상태로 생명나무를 먹지 못하게 하신 것은 은혜가 아니었습니까? 육체적 죽음을 제공하신 하나님의 신실하심을 보고 감사할 수 있습니까?

에브에게 주어진 저주 가운데 첫 메시야의 예언이 드러납니다. “내가 너와 여자 사이에, 네 자손과 여자의 자손 사이에 원수를 두리니 그는 네 머리를 상하게 할 것이요 너는 그의 발꿈치를 상하게 하리라”(창세기 3:15). 그는 죽음의 정복자이십니다! 그의 신실하심을 찬양합시다.

분해와 부패

분해와 부패는 저주의 또 다른 “D”입니다. 도토리가 땅에 떨어지면 곧 싹이 트기 시작합니다. 몇 년 안에 작은 묘목이 됩니다. 세월이 흐르고 다람쥐는 가을마다 땅에 떨어지는 도토리를 모읍니다. 그리고 거대한 참나무가 바이러스에 감염되어 죽고 몇 년 뒤 바람에 의해 쓰러집니다. 여기서 그것은 분해되고 부패하면서 토양으로 돌아갑니다. 저주 이후로 모든 것은 썩고 부패합니다. 지난 6,000년 동안 죽은 모든 식물과 동물과 사람들을 생각해 보십시오. 하나님께서 분해와 부패를 설계하신 것이 얼마나 선한 일입니까? 만약 6,000년의 모든 잔해가 여전히 이곳에 널려 있었다면 이 세상은 어떻게 보였을까요? 땅은 죽은 나무와 시체로 덮였을 것입니다! 이는 실감하기 어려울 수 있지만, 하나님은 필요하기 전에도 이 필요를 예견하시고 이를 성취하기 위해 창조 속에 전체 왕국들을 설계하셨습니다. 효모와 곰팡이와 균류의 왕국, 박테리아의 왕국, 효소와 미세한 식물 및 동물 생명체의 왕국은 모두 생명의 섬유를 분해하여 다음 세대의 완성을 위한 완벽한 비료로 만드는 데 도움이 됩니다. 건강한 유기농 토양에는 한 테이블스푼에 약 80억 마리의 토양 미생물이 있습니다. 이것이 토양을 거친 화학물질이 아닌 존중으로 다루어야 하는 또 다른 이유입니다.

노아의 대홍수를 한 번이라도 생각해 본 적이 있습니까? 홍수 후 물이 빠지면서 수백만 톤의 식물·동물·인간 유기물이 떠다니다가 마침내 가라앉아 퇴적물에 빠르게 묻혔다고 상상해 보십시오. 이것은 오늘날 우리가 사용하는 석탄과 다른 화석 연료들을 만들기 위한 이상적인 조건을 만들어 냈습니다. 그것은 땅 속 깊은 곳에 존재하다가 발견되는 날까지 거기 있었습니다. 오늘날까지도 그것은 여전히 사용되고 있습니다.

주님의 땅을 책임 있고 신실한 청지기 되게 합시다!

“피조물이 아들과 하나님의 영광의 나타남을 기다리고 있는 것임을 우리가 알거니와 피조물이 자발적으로가 아니요 피조물을 종노릇하게 하신 이로 말미암아 허무한 데 복종하게 되었으나 희망이 있는 것으로다. 피조물도 또한 썩음의 멍에에서 벗어나 하나님의 아들들의 영광스러운 자유에 들어가기를 기다리느니라 우리가 바라는 줄을 아나니 곧 성령의 첫열매를 받은 우리 자신도 속으로 탄식하여 양자의 도래 곧 우리의 몸의 구속을 기다리느니라”(로마서 8:19-23).
