Just reading the title probably brings negative thoughts to your mind. We as humans don’t typically like to be told “no” because it goes against our nature. Sometimes we bring the “no” upon ourselves because of disobedience, such as when God said “no” to Moses. “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land . . . But the Lord . . . would not hear me: and the Lord said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter” (Deuteronomy 3:25,26).

In Deuteronomy 1:42, God said “no” to Israel. “And the Lord said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies”, but they rebelled at His “no.” “And ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you” (Deuteronomy 1:45).

God said “no” to Paul. “And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me” (2 Corinthians 12:7-9).

Let us focus our attention upon prayerful Paul’s acceptance of God’s “no.”

First, acceptance does not mean that the problem does not exist. Paul accepted God’s “no”, but still had the infirmities.

Second, acceptance does not mean woeful resignation. Paul “besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.” We should be persistent, even when God’s answer is not forthcoming. (cf. Luke 18:1-8).

Third, God’s “no” may be necessary to avoid a greater evil or infirmity. Twice, Paul says the thorn in the flesh was given “lest I should be exalted above measure.” Unlike Paul, however, we may not know the purpose for God’s “no,” but we can be assured of His faithfulness and goodness. With Paul, we too may have to endure one thing, which means accepting God’s refusal in order to achieve a higher purpose or benefit.

Fourth, Paul’s weakness, as a result of God’s “no,” made him strong. “Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10). The sorrow and suffering some endure has indeed made them strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.

Fifth, Paul’s infirmity allowed the power of Christ to rest upon him. God’s strength was complete, sufficient, and made perfect in weakness. Paul’s strength was seen to be of God. Therefore, Christ, not Paul, was glorified. The infirmities that Paul endured revealed the power not of himself but of God.

Sixth, God explained his answer of “no” by saying, “My grace is sufficient for thee.” God’s love and acceptance of us, His strength and power to assist us in our infirmities and with our weaknesses, is sufficient and complete.

Seventh, Paul gloried in his infirmities, but only after he accepted God’s “no.” Paul ultimately saw that this allowed God’s power to rest upon him. Paul’s weakness displayed and magnified divine power in a manner that human adequacy and personal sufficiency could never accomplish.

Eighth, unfortunately for him, Paul was the vessel, the sufferer, who had to endure afflictions that God’s grace, power, and glory might be truly reflected, but he was glad to bear it for those purposes (cf. 2 Co 4:7-11; Gal 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Until we are ready to do the same, we cannot accept or understand God’s “no.”

A “no” may come into our life for many various reasons.

When God says, “No,” the Christian must remember:

That God will do right. “He is … a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he” (Deuteronomy 32:4). One may not see; he may not, as Job did not, understand, but God will do right. “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” (Genesis 18:25).

That God’s ways are not ours. “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts” (Isaiah 55:8,9). God sees the end from the beginning. Nothing is hidden from him. “Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it” (Psalms 139:6). as a little child cries in protest when his mother pulls him from the road (It is such a great place to ride a tricycle!), so we may cry when God says, “No,” but He, like the child’s parent, knows danger the child may not be able to comprehend or appreciate fully.

That prayer has a chief purpose. Prayer should not be an attempt to manipulate the will of God. “Not my will, but thine, be done,” the suffering Savior cried, but when God says, “No,” we often forget that fact and complain in effect, “Not Thy will but mine be done.” Perhaps the supreme purpose of prayer is to seek God’s will for our lives, our wants, our needs, and our desires. It will help to remember that when God says “no.”

That a present “no” may be a “yes” in development. Paul was told that he was going to Rome (Acts 19:21; 23:11). But the bars of incarceration, the shackles of servitude, and the jaws of death seemed to say otherwise. Two years of confinement were not convincing evidence of a trip to Rome, nor was a hopeless sea voyage (Acts 24:27; 27:20). However, as we all know, Paul went to Rome (Acts 28:16)!

That God’s laws prevail. The laws of nature are laws of God. God does not will that one to fall off a cliff, but if certain physical laws are broken, he will. God has biological laws. Disease may be contracted, and suffering and death may follow. One may pray, “Give us this day our daily bread,” but if he does not use God’s laws to procure it, or if he contradicts God’s means of acquiring it, he will not receive it. As painful as it is to accept, we frequently are victims of earthly laws in the various and diverse orders of physical life. Of course, the reverse is also true. We often are blessed by the material laws of God (Matthew 5:45; Acts 14:17; 1 Timothy 5:23).

In conclusion, Job of old bore the lashes of unparalleled human calamity and agony and torture of mind, body, and soul. His faithfulness and steadfast endurance have blessed thirty centuries of sorrowing humanity. Stephen and James met untimely, violent deaths (Acts 7; 12). They died when we would have had them to live. By their suffering and death, the early disciples were shown the power of the new faith, that men could die and yet live in victory. Hence, multiplied millions have been emboldened and have accepted torture and death rather than denounce their faith and hope of eternal life.

Deliverance came. No, not to Stephen and James, nor to suffering servants such as Job, of like precious faith, but it came in unquenchable hope, in the hope that maketh not ashamed. It came through Him that is able to deliver us who, through fear of death, were subject to bondage. “Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.”

Hanya dengan membaca judulnya kemungkinan besar membawa pikiran negatif dalam benak Anda. Kita sebagai manusia biasanya tidak suka diberitahu “tidak” karena itu bertentangan dengan kodrat kita. Kadang-kadang kita mendatangkan “tidak” itu atas diri kita sendiri karena ketidaktaatan, seperti ketika Allah berkata “tidak” kepada Musa. “Kiranya engkau ijinkan aku melewati dan melihat negeri yang baik itu . . . Tetapi TUHAN . . . tidaklah mengabulkan kepadaku; dan TUHAN berkata kepadaku: Cukuplah bagimu; jangan lagi engkau berbicara kepadaku tentang perkara itu” (Ulangan 3:25,26).

Di Ulangan 1:42, Allah berkata “tidak” kepada Israel. “Lalu TUHAN berkata kepadaku: Katakanlah kepada mereka: Janganlah kamu naik dan janganlah kamu berperang, sebab Aku tidak menyertai kamu, supaya jangan kamu dipukul di hadapan musuhmu”, tetapi mereka memberontak terhadap “tidak”-Nya. “Maka kamu kembali dan menangis di hadapan TUHAN; tetapi TUHAN tidak mau mendengar suaramu, dan tidak mempedulikan kamu” (Ulangan 1:45).

Allah berkata “tidak” kepada Paulus. “Dan supaya aku jangan menjadi tinggi hati karena berlebih-lebihan wahyu-wahyu itu, diberikanlah kepadaku sebuah duri di daging, yaitu utusan Iblis untuk menampar aku supaya aku jangan menjadi tinggi hati. Karena perkara itu aku tiga kali meminta kepada Tuhan, supaya ia menjauhkan itu dari padaku. Tetapi ia berkata kepadaku: Cukuplah kasih karunia-Ku bagimu, sebab justru dalam kelemahanlah kuasa-Ku menjadi sempurna. Karena itu terlebih suka aku bermegah atas kelemahanku, supaya kuasa Kristus bersemayam atas aku” (2 Korintus 12:7-9).

Marilah kita memusatkan perhatian pada penerimaan Paulus yang penuh doa terhadap “tidak”-Nya Allah.

Pertama, menerima tidak berarti masalah itu tidak ada. Paulus menerima “tidak”-Nya Allah, tetapi ia tetap mengalami kelemahan itu.

Kedua, menerima tidak berarti pasrah yang menyedihkan. Paulus “memohon kepada Tuhan tiga kali, supaya itu menjauh dariku.” Kita harus tekun, bahkan ketika jawaban Allah tidak kunjung datang. (bandingkan Lukas 18:1-8).

Ketiga, “tidak”-Nya Allah mungkin perlu untuk menghindarkan kejahatan atau kelemahan yang lebih besar. Dua kali Paulus berkata duri di daging itu diberikan “supaya aku jangan menjadi tinggi hati.” Berbeda dengan Paulus, kita mungkin tidak mengetahui tujuan dari “tidak”-Nya Allah, tetapi kita dapat yakin akan kesetiaan dan kebaikan-Nya. Seperti Paulus, kita juga mungkin harus menanggung sesuatu, yang berarti menerima penolakan Allah untuk mencapai tujuan atau manfaat yang lebih tinggi.

Keempat, kelemahan Paulus, sebagai akibat dari “tidak”-Nya Allah, membuatnya kuat. “Sebab itu aku berkenan dalam kelemahan, dalam penghinaan, dalam kekurangan-kekurangan, dalam penganiayaan-penganiayaan, dalam kesukaran-kesukaran karena Kristus; sebab kalau aku lemah, maka aku kuat” (2 Korintus 12:10). Kesedihan dan penderitaan yang ditanggung beberapa orang memang telah membuat mereka kuat dalam Tuhan dan dalam kuasa kekuatan-Nya.

Kelima, kelemahan Paulus memungkinkan kuasa Kristus untuk bersemayam atasnya. Kekuatan Allah sempurna, cukup, dan menjadi sempurna dalam kelemahan. Kekuatan Paulus terlihat berasal dari Allah. Karenanya, Kristus, bukan Paulus, yang dimuliakan. Kelemahan yang ditanggung Paulus memperlihatkan kuasa bukan dari dirinya sendiri tetapi dari Allah.

Keenam, Allah menjelaskan jawaban “tidak”-Nya dengan mengatakan, “Cukuplah kasih karunia-Ku bagimu.” Kasih dan penerimaan Allah kepada kita, kekuatan dan kuasa-Nya untuk menolong kita dalam kelemahan dan kelemahan kita, adalah cukup dan sempurna.

Ketujuh, Paulus memegahkan kelemahannya, tetapi hanya setelah ia menerima “tidak”-Nya Allah. Pada akhirnya Paulus melihat bahwa hal ini memungkinkan kuasa Allah bersemayam atasnya. Kelemahan Paulus menampilkan dan memperbesar kuasa ilahi dengan cara yang tidak dapat dicapai oleh kecukupan manusiawi dan kecukupan pribadi.

Kedelapan, sayangnya bagi dia, Paulus adalah bejana, sang penderita, yang harus menanggung kesengsaraan supaya kasih karunia, kuasa, dan kemuliaan Allah sungguh-sungguh dipantulkan, tetapi ia bersukacita menanggungnya untuk tujuan-tujuan itu (bandingkan 2 Korintus 4:7-11; Galatia 4:13,14; 6:14,17). Sampai kita siap melakukan hal yang sama, kita tidak dapat menerima atau memahami “tidak”-Nya Allah.

Sebuah “tidak” mungkin datang dalam hidup kita karena banyak alasan yang berbeda-beda.

Ketika Allah berkata, “Tidak,” orang Kristen harus ingat:

Bahwa Allah akan berbuat benar. “Ia adalah ... Allah yang benar dan tidak ada salahnya pada-Nya, adil dan benarlah Ia” (Ulangan 32:4). Seseorang mungkin tidak melihat; ia mungkin, seperti Ayub, tidak mengerti, tetapi Allah akan berbuat benar. “Bukankah Hakim atas seluruh bumi akan berbuat benar?” (Kejadian 18:25).

Bahwa jalan-jalan Allah bukanlah jalan kita. “Sebab rancangan-Ku bukanlah rancanganmu, dan jalanmu bukanlah jalan-Ku, demikianlah firman TUHAN. Sebab seperti tingginya langit dari bumi, demikianlah tingginya jalan-Ku dari jalanmu dan rancangan-Ku dari rancanganmu” (Yesaya 55:8,9). Allah melihat akhir dari permulaan. Tidak ada yang tersembunyi dari-Nya. “Pengetahuan seperti itu terlalu ajaib bagiku; tinggi, aku tidak dapat menjangkaunya” (Mazmur 139:6). seperti seorang anak kecil yang menangis menentang ketika ibunya menariknya dari jalan (Betapa enaknya mengendarai sepeda roda tiga di sini!), demikianlah kita mungkin menangis ketika Allah berkata, “Tidak,” tetapi Dia, seperti orangtua anak itu, mengetahui bahaya yang mungkin tidak dapat dipahami atau diapresiasi sepenuhnya oleh anak itu.

Bahwa doa mempunyai tujuan utama. Doa seharusnya bukanlah usaha untuk memanipulasi kehendak Allah. “Bukan kehendak-Ku, tetapi kehendak-Mulah yang terjadi,” seru Sang Juruselamat yang menderita, tetapi ketika Allah berkata, “Tidak,” kita sering melupakan fakta itu dan mengeluh pada dasarnya, “Bukan kehendak-Mu tetapi kehendakku yang terjadi.” Mungkin tujuan utama doa adalah mencari kehendak Allah untuk hidup kita, keinginan kita, kebutuhan kita, dan hasrat kita. Hal itu akan membantu untuk diingat ketika Allah berkata “tidak.”

Bahwa “tidak” yang ada sekarang mungkin merupakan “ya” yang sedang berkembang. Paulus diberitahu bahwa ia akan pergi ke Roma (Kisah Para Rasul 19:21; 23:11). Tetapi jeruji penjara, belenggu perhambaan, dan rahang maut tampak berkata sebaliknya. Dua tahun pemenjaraan bukanlah bukti yang meyakinkan tentang perjalanan ke Roma, demikian pula pelayaran yang tampak tanpa harapan (Kisah Para Rasul 24:27; 27:20). Namun, seperti yang kita semua tahu, Paulus pergi ke Roma (Kisah Para Rasul 28:16)!

Bahwa hukum-hukum Allah berlaku. Hukum alam adalah hukum Allah. Allah tidak menghendaki seseorang jatuh dari tebing, tetapi jika hukum-hukum fisik tertentu dilanggar, ia akan jatuh. Allah mempunyai hukum biologis. Penyakit dapat tertular, dan penderitaan serta kematian mungkin mengikuti. Seseorang dapat berdoa, “Berikanlah kami pada hari ini makanan kami yang secukupnya,” tetapi jika ia tidak menggunakan hukum-hukum Allah untuk memperolehnya, atau jika ia menentang jalan Tuhan dalam memperolehnya, ia tidak akan menerimanya. Sebetulnya, betapa menyakitkannya untuk menerima, kita sering kali menjadi korban hukum-hukum duniawi dalam berbagai dan bermacam urutan kehidupan fisik. Tentunya, sebaliknya juga benar. Kita sering diberkati oleh hukum-hukum materi Allah (Matius 5:45; Kisah Para Rasul 14:17; 1 Timotius 5:23).

Kesimpulannya, Ayub pada zaman dahulu memikul cambukan malapetaka manusiaiah yang tiada tara dan siksaan pikiran, tubuh, dan jiwa. Kesetiaan dan keteguhan ketabahannya telah memberkati tiga puluh abad umat manusia yang berduka. Stefanus dan Yakobus menemui kematian yang terlalu cepat dan penuh kekerasan (Kisah Para Rasul 7; 12). Mereka mati ketika kita ingin mereka hidup. Dengan penderitaan dan kematian mereka, murid-murid awal diperlihatkan kuasa iman baru itu, bahwa manusia dapat mati dan tetap hidup dalam kemenangan. Oleh karena itu, berjuta-juta orang telah dikuatkan dan telah memilih menanggung penyiksaan dan kematian daripada menyangkal iman mereka dan harapan hidup yang kekal.

Pelepasan datang. Tidak, bukan untuk Stefanus dan Yakobus, juga bukan untuk hamba-hamba yang menderita seperti Ayub, yang memiliki iman yang sama berharga, tetapi itu datang dalam pengharapan yang tak terpadamkan, dalam pengharapan yang tidak membuat malu. Itu datang melalui Dia yang sanggup melepaskan kita yang, karena takut akan maut, tunduk kepada perbudakan. “Syukur kepada Allah atas karunia-Nya yang tak terkatakan.”

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

Itu adalah "dunia yang sempurna" secara peribahasa yang dinikmati Adam dan Hawa setiap hari bersama Pencipta mereka. Taman yang indah, dirancang, diciptakan, dan ditanam dengan tangan oleh Allah sendiri, sempurna dalam segala hal. Kita semua tahu bahwa itu tidak bertahan lama. Karena hak untuk memilih yang diberikan Allah kepada seluruh umat manusia, keduanya segera membuat pilihan yang salah. Hawa, meskipun ditipu oleh Setan dalam bentuk ular, mempercayai kebohongan dan memilih untuk tidak taat kepada Allah, melakukan satu-satunya hal yang dengan penuh kasih Allah perintahkan agar jangan dilakukannya. Namun ketika ia membawa buah itu kepada Adam, Adam tidak tertipu. Ia tahu hal itu salah. Allah tidak terkejut tetapi, bagaimanapun, sangat kecewa. Dalam Kejadian 3, kita membaca kisah sedih tentang manusia yang diusir dari taman, dilarang dari pohon kehidupan yang kekal, dan kutukan dinyatakan karena dosa Adam dan Hawa. Tampak begitu gelap dan tanpa harapan. Meskipun hanya satu orang yang berdosa, kutukan itu turun kepada seluruh dunia ciptaan, termasuk bumi, tumbuhan, dan binatang. Pertimbangkanlah bersama saya apa saja yang datang bersama kutukan dahsyat ini.

  1. Penyakit
  2. Kesengsaraan dan Nyeri
  3. Kerusakan dan kehancuran
  4. Dominasi tanaman tertentu seperti duri dan rumput duri
  5. Kematian
  6. Decomposisi dan Pembusukan

Kita akan merujuk pada mereka hari ini sebagai enam "D" dari kutukan.

Penyakit

Masa-masa murni dunia akan kesehatan yang sempurna dan kekal telah berlalu. Penyakit masuk sebagai bagian dari kutukan dosa. Anak-anak manusia, burung, binatang, dan tumbuhan semuanya akan mulai mengalami efek sakit dan penyakit. Tetapi Allah setia dengan memberikan instruksi yang membantu manusia mengetahui bagaimana menghindari banyak penyakit yang dapat dicegah melalui kebersihan dan ketaatan sederhana. Misalnya, perintah Allah untuk menghormati maksud-Nya yang asli dalam pernikahan, menjaga kesucian, menghindari berbagai potensi penyakit, dan sebagainya. Ia juga memperhatikan kondisi rohani kita. Allah tidak pernah merancang manusia untuk memikul rasa bersalah. Ia ingin kita memiliki dan mempertahankan hati nurani yang bersih karena Ia tahu bahwa hati nurani yang bersalah dapat membuatmu sakit!

Beberapa penyakit ini tidak dapat dihindari, tetapi banyak yang dapat dicegah dengan membangun kekebalan. Allah juga setia dalam merancang manusia, tumbuhan, dan hewan dengan mikrobioma regeneratif (miliaran bakteri yang bermanfaat) dan sistem imun sistemik, yang membantu kita melawan penyakit. Menakjubkan bagaimana setiap tumbuhan tampaknya memiliki sifat diet atau penyembuhan tertentu yang bermanfaat. Betapa setianya Sang Pencipta!

Kesengsaraan dan Nyeri

Saya menduga tidak ada alasan nyata untuk adanya nyeri di Taman Eden, tetapi kita telah mengalami rasa sakit sejak hari kepergian mereka. Nyeri memang merupakan bagian dari banyak kehidupan kita. Ada banyak jenis rasa sakit. Dukacita, kesedihan, dan penolakan adalah semua rasa sakit emosional yang datang bersama kutukan. Nyeri fisik seperti pegal, migrain, otot sakit, ligamen robek, tendon terinfeksi, sendi aus, dan tulang patah adalah beberapa dari rasa sakit fisik yang mungkin kita alami suatu saat sebelum napas terakhir kita. Sekali lagi, Allah setia dalam menolong manusia memahami apa yang harus dilakukan untuk meredakan sebagian rasa sakit dan kesengsaraan hidup. Sejak zaman dahulu, tumbuhan, herbal, dan obat-obatan lain telah membantu orang menghadapi rasa sakit dan kesengsaraan. Hingga hari ini, kita memiliki banyak tumbuhan berguna yang membantu kita mengatasi rasa sakit.

Salah satu hal paling indah yang dapat dialami di dunia adalah kelahiran seorang anak. Namun kelahiran umumnya disertai banyak rasa sakit. Meskipun kita tidak dapat menghilangkan rasa sakit yang dijanjikan ini, Allah setia menyediakan dan menyatakan kepada kita penggunaan banyak ramuan untuk digunakan sebelum, selama, dan setelah kelahiran untuk meringankan rasa sakit dan mempercepat pemulihan. Ia tidak harus melakukan itu untuk kita. Manusia sungguh tidak pantas mendapat belas kasihan. Betapa setianya Sang Pencipta!

Kerusakan dan kehancuran

Kita tidak perlu banyak mempelajari sejarah untuk melihat prinsip ini bekerja. Angin, hujan, dan sinar matahari semuanya memiliki efek merusak pada banyak hal. Baik kita mempertimbangkan tepi sungai yang tererosi, batu yang terhaluskan di dasar sungai, atau pohon yang tumbang diterjang angin, semua itu adalah elemen alami kehancuran. Tetapi tambahkan pula apa yang telah dilakukan manusia terhadap tumbuhan, binatang, tanah, dan satu sama lain. Baik dampak merusak selama perang yang mengerikan maupun praktik egois dan serakah pada masa damai, manusia adalah makhluk yang sangat merusak. Allah memberikan manusia berkuasa atas seluruh ciptaan. Namun, terlalu sering, kita salah menafsirkannya seolah-olah kita memiliki bumi ini dan boleh melakukan apa saja terhadapnya. Dia yang menyatakan, "Bumi adalah milik TUHAN," tidak setuju dengan gagasan bahwa manusia adalah selain dari pengurus ciptaan Allah. Memang jahat menyembah dunia yang diciptakan atau apa pun di dalamnya. Tetapi sama jahatnya menjadi tidak bersyukur dan ceroboh terhadap ciptaan Sang Pencipta! Namun demikian, Allah setia merancang bumi-Nya dengan kemampuan regeneratif di tengah-tengah kutukan ini. Terpujilah Pencipta yang murah hati kita!

Dominasi Duri dan Rumput Duri

Siapa pun yang pernah berkebun segera menemukan realitas pertarungan dengan gulma. Secara adil, setiap tanaman yang tumbuh di tempat yang tidak diinginkan adalah "gulma." Banyak gulma bisa menjadi tanaman yang sangat bermanfaat jika kita mengetahui untuk apa menggunakannya. Beberapa tanaman yang kita sebut gulma sebenarnya cukup bergizi dan sehat setelah kita memahami mana yang dapat dimakan dan bagaimana menyiapkannya. Hari ini, kita ingin memikirkan duri dan rumput duri. Kita harus berasumsi bahwa mereka diciptakan pada enam hari pertama, bukan setelah kutukan dinyatakan. Tampaknya kemampuan mereka untuk melampaui tanaman yang berguna meningkat setelah kutukan. Bahkan dalam bagian kutukan ini, kita melihat Allah dengan penuh belas kasihan menyediakan bagi kita.

Kita menanam artichoke untuk daunnya yang pahit, yang digunakan untuk membuat obat pencernaan pahit. Pikirkan: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, daun Raspberry, dan akar Blackberry hanyalah beberapa contoh anggota "gulma berduri" ini yang digunakan untuk manfaat obat dan makanan lainnya. Betapa baiknya Allah memberi kita manfaat di tengah-tengah kutukan itu!

Kematian

Ini adalah salah satu "D" yang paling banyak dari kita tidak ingin bicarakan. Sebenarnya, ketika kita menghirup napas pertama, kita satu napas lebih dekat kepada kematian. Meskipun semua tumbuhan, hewan, dan manusia pada akhirnya akan mati, kita tetap tidak merasa nyaman dengannya. Sangat wajar bagi kita memiliki keinginan untuk hidup, dan jika tidak, kita sebaiknya mencari bantuan untuk mengetahui mengapa.

Memang, kematian tidak mengenal usia. Sepanjang hidup saya, saya telah membantu menguburkan bayi yang lahir mati, orang-orang hingga usia 96 tahun, dan segala usia di antaranya. Kita membaca tentang surga yang dipulihkan yang indah, yang dilihat oleh Rasul Yohanes dalam Wahyu, ketika ia menggambarkan Firdaus. Beberapa hal yang ia sebutkan adalah tidak ada penyakit, tidak ada kesedihan, tidak ada perpisahan, tidak ada air mata, tidak ada lagi penderitaan, dan tidak ada kematian. Dalam arti tertentu, hidup hanyalah masa mengandung untuk kekekalan. Kita tidak bisa tinggal di sini, seperti bayi dalam kandungan tidak bisa memutuskan bahwa ia tidak ingin memasuki dunia nyata. Dengan semua kesedihan dan pencobaan kita, tubuh kita menjadi aus dan membusuk. Dengan semua kekerasan, dosa, dan kejahatan di sekitar kita, mungkinkah kita benar-benar ingin tinggal di sini dalam keadaan ini selamanya? Sebaliknya, kita kembali ke tanah yang dari mana kita dibuat, abu kepada abu dan debu kepada debu, menantikan kebangkitan akhir. Bukankah baik hati Allah setia memberi tahu bahwa manusia yang berdosa tidak diizinkan makan dari pohon kehidupan dalam keadaan berdosa dan sekaratnya saat itu? Dapatkah kita melihat dan bersyukur atas kesetiaan Allah dalam menyediakan kematian fisik?

Di tengah-tengah kutukan yang diberikan kepada Hawa, nubuat pertama tentang Mesias dinyatakan. "Aku akan mengadakan permusuhan antara engkau dan perempuan itu, dan antara keturunanmu dan keturunannya; ia akan meremukkan kepalamu, dan engkau akan meremukkan tumitnya" (Kejadian 3:15). Ia adalah penakluk maut! Puji Allah atas Kesetiaan-Nya.

Decomposisi dan Pembusukan

Decomposisi dan Pembusukan adalah "D" lain dari kutukan. Sebuah kacang jatuh ke tanah, dan tunas segera muncul. Dalam beberapa tahun, itu akan menjadi bibit kecil. Tahun-tahun berlalu, dan tupai mengumpulkan biji-bijian yang jatuh ke tanah setiap musim gugur. Lalu sebagai pohon oak yang gagah ia terjangkit virus, mati, dan dalam beberapa tahun diterjang badai angin. Di sini, ia kembali ke tanah saat ia membusuk dan terurai. Sejak kutukan, segala sesuatu membusuk dan terurai. Mempertimbangkan semua tumbuhan, binatang, dan manusia yang telah mati dalam 6.000 tahun terakhir, bukankah baik Allah merancang dekomposisi dan pembusukan? Seperti apa dunia ini jika semua puing-puing 6.000 tahun itu masih berserakan? Bumi akan tertutup pohon mati dan mayat! Ini mungkin sulit disadari, tetapi Allah merancang kerajaan-kerajaan seluruhnya dalam ciptaan hanya untuk melakukan ini sebelum itu bahkan diperlukan karena Ia meramalkan kebutuhan itu. Kerajaan ragi, jamur, dan fungi, kerajaan bakteri, enzim, dan kehidupan tumbuhan dan hewan mikroskopis semuanya membantu memecah serat kehidupan dan menjadikannya pupuk sempurna untuk menyelesaikan siklus kehidupan dan penyediaan bagi generasi berikutnya. Tanah organik yang sehat memiliki sekitar 8 miliar mikroba tanah dalam satu sendok makan. Ini salah satu alasan mengapa penting untuk memperlakukan tanah dengan hormat, bukan bahan kimia keras.

Pernahkah kamu mempertimbangkan air bah Nuh yang dahsyat? Bayangkan jutaan ton materi tumbuhan, binatang, dan manusia yang mengapung sebelum akhirnya menetap ke dasar dan cepat terkubur dalam sedimen saat air surut. Ini menghasilkan kondisi ideal untuk membentuk batu bara dan bahan bakar fosil lain yang kita gunakan hari ini. Di sana ia berada, jauh di dalam bumi, sampai hari ditemukannya. Hingga hari ini, itu masih digunakan.

Semoga kita menjadi pengurus bumi Tuhan yang bertanggung jawab dan setia!

"Karena pengharapan makhluk berharap dan menantikan penyataan anak-anak Allah. Sebab makhluk telah diperhamba­kan kepada kebinasaan, bukan karena kehendaknya, tetapi karena Dia yang telah memperhambakannya, dengan harapan, bahwa juga makhluk itu sendiri suatu hari nanti akan dibebaskan dari perbudakan kebinasaan itu dan masuk ke dalam kemerdekaan mulia anak-anak Allah. Sebab kita tahu, bahwa seluruh makhluk sampai sekarang mengeluh dan merintih sebagai dalam penderitaan. Dan bukan saja makhluk itu saja, tetapi kita sendiri juga yang mempunyai penyerahan Roh pertama, juga kita sendiri dalam batin kita mengeluh sambil menantikan hari yang penuh; yaitu penebusan tubuh kita" (Roma 8:19-23).

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

Это был пресловутый «совершенный мир», который Адам и Ева ежедневно наслаждались с их Творцом. Прекрасный сад, спроектированный, созданный и посаженный своими руками самим Богом, был совершенен во всех отношениях. Мы все знаем, что это не продлилось очень долго. Из-за привилегии выбора, которую Бог дал всему человечеству, они оба вскоре сделали неправильный выбор. Ева, хотя и была обманута Сатаной в образе змеи, поверила лжи и выбрала непослушание Богу, сделав единственное, о чем Бог с любовью просил её не делать. Но когда она принесла плод Адаму, он не был обманут. Он знал, что это неправильно. Бог не был удивлён, но, тем не менее, был очень разочарован. В Бытии 3 мы читаем печальное повествование о том, как человечество было изгнано из сада, отстранено от древа жизни и на него был наложен проклятие из‑за греха Адама и Евы. Казалось, всё так мрачно и безнадёжно. Хотя согрешил только один человек, проклятие перешло на весь созданный мир, включая землю, растения и животных. Подумайте со мной о том, что всё это принесло вместе с могучим проклятием.

  1. Болезни
  2. Страдания и боль
  3. Ухудшение и разрушение
  4. Насилие определённых растений, таких как шипы и колючки
  5. Смерть
  6. Разложение и гниение

Мы будем называть их сегодня шестью «Д» проклятия.

Болезни

Безупречные дни мира с вечным, совершенным здоровьем прошли. Болезни вошли в картину как часть проклятия греха. Дети человеческие, птицы, звери и растения все начали испытывать последствия болезней и заболеваний. Но Бог был верен, дав инструкции, которые помогали человеку знать, как избежать многих предотвратимых болезней через чистоту и простое повиновение. Например, Божья заповедь сохранять изначальное намерение в браке, поддерживать чистоту, избегать множества потенциальных болезней и т. д. Он также заботился о нашем духовном состоянии. Бог никогда не сделал людей для того, чтобы они несли вину. Он хочет, чтобы мы имели и сохраняли чистую совесть, потому что Он знает, что виновная совесть может сделать тебя больным!

Некоторые из этих болезней были бы неизбежны, но многие можно было предотвратить, вырабатывая иммунитет. Бог также был верен, создав людей, растения и животных с восстановительной микробиотой (миллиарды полезных бактерий) и системой иммунитета, которая помогает нам бороться с болезнями. Удивительно, как каждое растение, кажется, имеет определённые пищевые или лечебные свойства, которые полезны. Какой верный Творец!

Страдания и боль

Полагаю, в Эдемском саду не было реальной причины для боли, но мы испытываем боль с того дня, как вышли оттуда. Боль действительно является частью многих наших жизней. Существует множество видов боли. Горе, печаль и отвержение — это все эмоциональные боли, связанные с проклятием. Боли в суставах, мигрени, боль в мышцах, разорванные связки, инфицированные сухожилия, изношенные суставы и переломы — это лишь некоторые из физических болей, которые мы можем испытывать где‑то до нашего последнего вздоха. Снова же, Бог был верен, помогая человеку понять, что делать, чтобы облегчить некоторые страдания и беды жизни. Со времен древности растения, травы и другие средства помогали людям справляться с болью и страданиями. И поныне у нас есть много полезных растений, которые помогают нам при боли.

Одно из самых прекрасных переживаний на земле — рождение ребёнка. Тем не менее рождение обычно сопровождается большой болью. Хотя мы не можем устранить эту предначертанную боль, Бог был верен, предоставляя и открывая нам использование многих трав до рождения, во время и после него, чтобы облегчить боль и ускорить восстановление. Ему не нужно было этого делать для нас. Человечество действительно не заслуживает милосердия. Какой верный Творец!

Ухудшение и разрушение

Нам не нужно много изучать историю, чтобы увидеть этот принцип в действии. Ветер, дождь и солнце оказывают разрушительное воздействие на многие вещи. Будь то размытый берег речки, камни, зашлифованные в русле реки, или дерево, снесённое ветром — всё это естественные элементы разрушения. Но прибавьте к этому то, что человек сделал с растениями, животными, почвой и друг с другом. Будь то опустошительные последствия разрушений во время ужасных войн или эгоистичные и жадные практики в мирное время, человек — очень разрушительное существо. Бог даровал человеку владычество над всем творением. Однако слишком часто мы ошибочно понимаем это как то, что мы владеем этой сферой под названием Земля и можем делать с ней всё, что хотим. Тот, кто провозгласил: «Земля — Господня», не согласен с идеей, что люди — не более чем распорядители Божьего творения. Прямо ужасно поклоняться созданному миру или чему‑либо в нём. Но так же ужасно быть неблагодарным и небрежно относиться к творению нашего Творца! Тем не менее Бог верно предусмотрел для Своей земли восстановительные способности посреди этого проклятия. Благословен наш благодатный Создатель!

Преобладание шипов и колючек

Кто когда‑либо занимался садоводством, тот вскоре почувствовал реальность борьбы с сорняками. По справедливости, любое растение, растущее там, где его не хотят, — «сорняк». Многие сорняки могут быть очень полезными растениями, если мы только знаем, как их использовать. Некоторые растения, которые мы называем сорняками, на самом деле довольно питательны и полезны, если понять, какие из них съедобны и как их готовить. Сегодня мы хотим подумать о шипах и колючках. Нам нужно предположить, что они были созданы в первые шесть дней, а не после провозглашения проклятия. Кажется, что их способность превосходить полезные культуры увеличилась после проклятия. Даже в этой части проклятия мы видим, как Бог милостиво обеспечивает нас.

Мы выращиваем артишок ради его горьких листьев, которые используют для приготовления горечей для пищеварения. Подумайте об этом: Blessed Thistle (благословенный чертополох), Milk Thistle (расторопша), Teasel (репейник), лист малины и корни ежевики — это лишь несколько примеров представителей этих «колючих сорняков», используемых в медицине и в пищу. Как хорошо от Бога давать нам пользу посреди самого проклятия!

Смерть

Это та «Д», о которой большинство из нас предпочло бы не говорить. На самом деле, когда мы делаем первый вдох, мы на один вдох ближе к смерти. Хотя все растения, животные и люди в конце концов умрут, нам всё же не по себе из‑за этого. Это совершенно нормально — иметь волю к жизни, и если её нет, следует обратиться за помощью, чтобы узнать причину.

Действительно, смерть не имеет возраста. За свою жизнь мне приходилось помогать хоронить недоношенных детей, людей до 96 лет и всех между ними. Мы читаем о прекрасном восстановленном рае, увиденном апостолом Иоанном в Откровении, когда он описывает Небеса. Некоторые из вещей, которые он упоминает: никакой болезни, никакого горя, никакой разлуки, никаких слёз, больше никаких страданий и никакой смерти. В некотором смысле жизнь — лишь период внутриутробного развития перед вечностью. Мы не можем здесь остаться, так же как ребёнок в утробе не может решить, что он не хочет входить в реальный мир. Со всеми нашими скорбями и искушениями наши тела изнашиваются и разлагаются. С учётом всего насилия, греха и нечестия вокруг, разве мы действительно хотели бы оставаться здесь навечно в таком состоянии? Скорее мы возвращаемся в прах, из которого были сделаны, пепел к праху и прах к праху, в ожидании окончательного воскресения. Разве не было милосердно с стороны нашего верного Бога не позволить грешному человеку вкусить от древа жизни в его нынешнем грешном, умирающем состоянии? Можем ли мы увидеть и быть благодарными за Божью верность в даровании физической смерти?

Посреди проклятия, данного Еве, открывается первое пророчество о Мессии. «И положу вражду между тобою и между женщиною, и между семя твоим и между семенем её; оно будет поражать тебе голову, а ты будешь поражать ему пяту» (Бытие 3:15). Он — победитель смерти! Слава Богу за Его верность.

Разложение и гниение

Разложение и гниение — ещё одна «Д» проклятия. Орех падает на землю, и вскоре появляется росток. Через несколько лет это будет маленький сеянец. Проходят годы, белки собирают желуди, упавшие каждую осень. Затем, будучи могучим дубом, оно заражается вирусом, умирает и через несколько лет падает от бурного ветра. Здесь оно возвращается в почву по мере разложения и гниения. Со времени проклятия всё гниёт и разлагается. Учитывая все растения, животных и людей, умерших за последние 6 000 лет, разве не хорошо от Бога было создать разложение и гниение? Как бы выглядел этот мир, если бы весь мусор шести тысяч лет всё ещё валялся вокруг? Земля была бы покрыта мёртвыми деревьями и трупами! Возможно, это трудно представить, но Бог создал целые царства в творении именно для того, чтобы выполнить это ещё до того, как это стало нужно, потому что Он предвидел такую необходимость. Царства дрожжей, плесени и грибов, царства бактерий, ферментов и микроскопической растительной и животной жизни — всё это помогает разложить ткань жизни и превратить её в идеальное удобрение для завершения жизненного цикла и обеспечения следующего поколения. Здоровая органическая почва содержит около 8 миллиардов почвенных микробов в одной столовой ложке. Вот ещё одна причина, почему так важно уважительно относиться к почве, а не применять жёсткие химикаты.

Вы когда‑нибудь задумывались о великом потопе Ноевого времени? Представьте миллионы тонн растительного, животного и человеческого материала, плавающего, прежде чем в конце концов осесть на дно и быстро быть погребённым в осадке по мере отступления вод. Это создало идеальные условия для образования угля и других ископаемых топлив, которые мы используем сегодня. Там это находилось, глубоко в недрах земли, до дня своего открытия. По сей день оно всё ещё используется.

Будем ответственными и верными хранителями земли Господней!

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

Quando sono stato convertito, non avevo mai sentito il termine anabattista. Non avevo mai sentito molto parlare di testimoniare agli altri. Ricordo che pensavo a tutti i miei amici che non sapevano nulla di quello che mi era appena successo. La mia fidanzata di sette anni non capiva. Una cosa continuava a ripetersi nella mia mente: “Devo dirlo!” Mi era successo qualcosa di buono, e tutti dovevano sapere che la stessa cosa poteva accadere anche a loro! Ricordo un periodo in cui mio fratello ed io pensavamo a un posto dove poter dire a molte persone di Gesù. Decidemmo di andare a una partita di baseball di prima divisione. Ero nervoso, avevo paura, e non dimenticherò mai quello che accadde. Non avevo mai parlato davanti a una grande folla prima, ma quando aprii la bocca, Dio la riempì.

Non andavo solo a parlare con persone che non conoscevo. Quando vedevo un vecchio amico, gli raccontavo quello che mi era successo. Di solito mi dicevano che l’avevano già sentito e cercavano di convincermi a calmarmi e rilassarmi. Sarò il primo ad ammettere che feci degli errori in quegli anni iniziali. Notai, con mia costernazione, che mentre molte persone non mi gradivano, erano proprio coloro che dicevano di essere cristiani a sembrare odiarmi di più. Un giorno stavo parlando con un uomo anziano che disse di essere stato cristiano per la maggior parte della sua vita. Durante la conversazione indicò una lampadina e disse: “Vedi quella lampadina? Non parla.” Rimasi scioccato. Mi stava dicendo che, sì, mentre Gesù dice che noi siamo la luce del mondo, le lampade dovrebbero brillare silenziose. Non parlano.

Rimasi sbalordito. Era vero? Tornai a casa per fare uno studio biblico. Non passò molto tempo prima che trovassi versetti come Matteo 4:23: “E Gesù percorreva tutta la Galilea, insegnando nelle loro sinagoghe, e predicando il vangelo del regno, e sanando ogni infermità e ogni malattia fra il popolo.” Poi in Matteo 9, quando Gesù “vide le folle, fu preso da compassione per loro, perché erano stanche e disperse come pecore che non hanno pastore. Allora disse ai suoi discepoli: ‘La mietitura è molta, ma gli operai son pochi; pregate dunque il Signore della mietitura che mandi operai nella sua mietitura’” (Matteo 9:36-38).

Mi sembra che ovunque andasse, Gesù parlasse alla gente del regno. Ho visto persone testimoniare di Dio, ma talvolta in modo offensivo. Ma questo significa che non dobbiamo testimoniare? Se leggi il libro degli Atti, è quasi tutto quello che vedi—il Vangelo che esce! In un racconto le autorità catturarono i discepoli e dissero che potevano andare liberi se si fossero solo zitti. Tuttavia, i discepoli dissero che non potevano. “Poiché non possiamo tacere ciò che abbiamo visto e udito” (Atti 4:20). Più tardi furono messi a tacere—con la morte.

Tempo dopo sentii parlare di queste persone chiamate anabattisti. Studiandoli, cominciai a vedere come anche loro non volevano stare zitti. Ordinai una copia di The Martyr’s Mirror e rimasi sbalordito quando lessi di queste persone che vivevano come i discepoli. Adempivano alle parole di Gesù, “E sarete odiati da tutti a causa del mio nome; ma chi avrà perseverato fino alla fine sarà salvato” (Matteo 10:22). E in Romani 8:36, “Com’è scritto: Per causa tua siamo messi a morte tutto il giorno; siamo considerati come pecore da macello.”

Cari fratelli e sorelle, credo che il fuoco si stia spegnendo. Sento molti dei nostri popoli anabattisti parlare di vivere una vita tranquilla e pacifica. Gesù ci dice nella parabola del seminatore: “Chi ha ricevuto il seme tra le spine è colui che ascolta la parola; e la preoccupazione di questo mondo e l’inganno delle ricchezze soffocano la parola, e diventa infruttuoso” (Matteo 13:22). Potrebbe essere questo il punto in cui molti di noi si trovano? Viviamo nella terra libera dell’America dove il denaro sembra facile da ottenere. È possibile che siamo stati ingannati dalle nostre ricchezze e dalle preoccupazioni di questo mondo? Siamo diventati simili al mondo per evitare di esserne perseguitati?

Molti anni fa, un gruppo di anabattisti fuggì dalla persecuzione e si trasferì in un paese dove l’oppressione era minore. Aprirono un negozio di mobili per mantenersi, ma non riuscivano a vendere mobili perché erano i temuti anabattisti. Presto la situazione divenne disperata perché non avevano soldi per comprare cibo. Un giorno un uomo facoltoso entrò nel negozio. Tutti i lavoratori smisero quello che stavano facendo. Pensarono tra sé: “Forse quest’uomo comprerà qualcosa, e potremo mangiare!” Un vecchio fratello si avvicinò al possibile cliente e gli chiese se conosceva Gesù. Dopo una breve conversazione, l’uomo uscì di furia dal negozio in preda all’ira. I lavoratori affamati chiesero al vecchio perché aveva spaventato la loro unica possibilità di vendita. Egli spiegò che per quell’uomo conoscere Gesù era molto più importante che guadagnare qualche soldo.

Nella mentalità dei primi anabattisti, il Vangelo di Gesù era la cosa più importante. Come negli Atti, non potevano tacere le cose che avevano visto e udito. E anche loro furono “messi a morte tutto il giorno”.

Allora, cosa facciamo con il versetto sulla vita tranquilla e pacifica? Il versetto si trova in 1 Timoteo 2:1-2: “Esorto dunque, prima di tutto, che si facciano suppliche, preghiere, intercessioni e ringraziamenti per tutti gli uomini; per i re e per tutti quelli che sono in autorità; affinché possiamo condurre una vita tranquilla e pacifica in ogni pietà e onestà.” Cosa intendeva l’apostolo Paolo quando scrisse questo? Voleva forse dire che dovremmo stare zitti sul vangelo e non sfidare mai un peccatore? È difficile credere che Paolo ci stia dicendo di fare qualcosa che lui non fece mai, qualcosa che Cristo stesso non fece mai. Infatti, nessuno nelle Scritture che seguì Dio fu silenzioso riguardo alla propria fede. In numerosi racconti dei primi cristiani arrestati per la loro fede, le autorità imploravano che stessero zitti! Ma rifiutarono, proprio come fecero i discepoli. Anche loro scelsero la morte, piuttosto che una vita tranquilla e pacifica.

Un giovane anabattista arrestato lasciò la sua cara moglie in attesa del loro primo figlio. Le autorità aspettarono che il bambino nascesse e poi portarono l’infante al nuovo padre in prigione. Gli dissero che ora era padre e che poteva tornare a casa e stare con la moglie e il figlio. Poteva anche continuare a credere nello stesso modo, ma doveva starsene zitto e non parlare contro il peccato nella chiesa di Stato. Il giovane padre rifiutò. Per lui, stare zitto non era un’opzione. Lo bruciarono sul rogo.

Quindi, cosa significa 1 Timoteo 2:1-2? Sembra che i cristiani nella Bibbia e la chiesa primitiva fossero tutti impegnati a diffondere il vangelo, tutti dedicati alla chiesa di Cristo. Andavano in giro a predicare il vangelo, tenevano riunioni sui monti, nei boschi o ovunque la gente si radunasse. Quella era la loro vita. Nel versetto di 1 Timoteo 2, Paolo sta dicendo che dovremmo pregare che le autorità ci permettano di vivere in pace così possiamo diffondere il vangelo. I cristiani dovrebbero essere fuori a diffondere la parola e a spingere verso il regno. La nostra preghiera è che le autorità ci lascino vivere in pace, mentre serviamo il Principe della pace.

Oggi è facile essere cristiani quando ti sistemi e vivi una vita tranquilla e pacifica, senza mai sfidare un peccatore o correggere un fratello. Ma chi ha detto che sarebbe stato facile?

Quando vivevamo ad Haiti, insegnavamo alla nostra chiesa il costo di seguire Gesù. Fu sorprendente ascoltare le testimonianze degli haitiani che applicavano gli insegnamenti di Gesù alle loro vite. Una volta, due membri ci dissero che stavano per perdere il lavoro a causa del seguire il vangelo. Sentirli prendere posizione per la verità mi rese felice. Un’altra sorella nella chiesa mi raccontò che la scuola che i suoi figli frequentavano aveva uniformi e le ragazze dovevano indossare i pantaloni. Quando mandò sua figlia a scuola con un vestito modesto, tornò a casa con un biglietto del preside che diceva che non doveva tornare a scuola indossando quella cosa.

1 Pietro 4:14 dice: “Se voi siete vituperati nel nome di Cristo, beati voi; perché lo spirito della gloria e di Dio riposa su di voi; da parte loro è maledetto, ma da parte vostra è glorificato.”

La vera gioia viene dalla sofferenza. La sofferenza deriva dall’obbedire a Gesù. Siamo troppo occupati con questioni futili mentre il mondo va a rovina? Seguiamo Gesù come i primi cristiani, dove nessuno poteva negare che la potenza di Dio operava in loro. Abbiamo qualcosa di cui tutti hanno bisogno. Cosa stiamo aspettando? Riconciliamoci, raccogliamoci insieme, neghiamo noi stessi, prendiamo la croce e seguiamolo!
